en: Śāṅkhāyana Śrautasūtra. Edited by Alfred Hillebrandt (Bibliotheca Indica).
Typed by Muneo Tokunaga, April 1995.
ŚŚS 1.1: We shall explain the sacrifice (yajña). (Paribhāṣās) ŚŚS 1.1:
It belongs to the three social classes (varṇa). (Paribhāṣās)

[These rules apply] to the Brāhmaṇa, the Kṣatriya, and the Vaiśya. (Paribhāṣā 1.1.3) That which is prescribed without being connected [to a specific caste] is common [to all]. (Paribhāṣā 1.1.4) Through connection, it becomes restricted [to a specific caste]. (Paribhāṣā 1.1.5)
Wearing the sacrificial cord over the left shoulder (yajñopavītī), one performs rites for the gods. (6) Wearing it over the right shoulder (prācīnāpavītī), one performs rites for the ancestors.
(7) From the act of sipping water (ācamana) onwards, one should not turn away from whichever hand is engaged in the performance of the rite. (8)
Nor should one separate [the two].
(9) (Paribhāṣās) Thus ends the definition of the *āvṛt* (repetition). (10) (Paribhāṣās) This is the enumeration (*uddeśa*). (11) (Paribhāṣās)
1.1. The procedure is from the north. (Paribhāṣā 12) 1.1. Rites for the gods proceed from east to west. (Paribhāṣā 13) 1.1. Rites for the ancestors proceed from south to north. (Paribhāṣā 14)
The Bāhvṛcya [portion] concerning the rules for sitting is established.
(15) Position [is determined] by explicit statement.
(16) And the Hotṛ shall perform that which is not otherwise prescribed. (17)
In groups of three or more *ṛc*s, the first and the last are each recited three times, except in the case of *japa* (muttered prayers).

And in the case of the final *chandoma*, after the initial consonant, the syllable *om* is substituted; it is protracted (*pluta*), consisting of three morae (*trimātra*), and pure (*śuddha*). Or else, it ends with the letter *m*.
They call that the *praṇava*.

(21) At the end [of a verse], it ends with the letter *m* in all groups of *ṛc*s, including those accompanied by *puronuvākyā*s. (22) Having joined the half-verse of the following [verse] with that, one pauses; or [having joined] a quarter-verse, they call that *saṃtata* (continuous). (23)

This is the rule for all groups of *ṛc*s that are enjoined through connection with a ritual action: [the *paridhānīyā*] is used. (24) Even when the ritual actions are distant [from one another], there is a requirement for continuity by means of a half-verse (*ardharca*) between the first [verse] and the *paridhānīyā*.
(25) And the *ṛc*s follow the principle of the half-verse. (26)
[The Veda] is different from what is stated [in the rule].

(27) (Paribhāṣās) The Ṛgveda is characterized by being recited loudly and according to the correct method. (28) (Paribhāṣās) [The Yajurveda] is characterized by being recited in a low voice, because of a specific scriptural statement. (29) (Paribhāṣās)
The correct application of *saṃhitā* and the proper usage of words; (30) [Paribhāṣās] Monotony of accent;
(31) [Paribhāṣās] The *praṇava* is at a higher pitch than the *puronuvākyā*. (32) [Paribhāṣās]
The *yājyā* [verse] is higher than the *praṇava*.
(33) (Paribhāṣās) The *vaṣaṭ*-call is higher still. (34) (Paribhāṣās) Or it may be equal. (35) (Paribhāṣās)

The *praṇava*, the *ye yajāmahe*, the *vaṣaṭkāra*, the *saṃpraiṣas*, and the *praiṣas* are to be uttered loudly during oblations; [however], they are to be whispered (*upāṃśu*) for [oblations] involving cooked offerings (*havirṣu*). (36) The name of the deity is to be whispered (*upāṃśu*) at the places where the *nigamas* [are recited].
(37) "Bhūr bhuvaḥ" is the *japa* to be performed before [the sacrifice]. (38)

In all *yājyā* verses, the fourfold formula—“ye yajāmahe,” “vauṣaṭ,” “ojas sahas saha ojas svar”—is placed at the end. (39) However, in the *anuyāja* offerings, there is no “ye yajāmahe. (40) And likewise in the *anuvaṣaṭkāra*. (41) (Paribhāṣās)
The joining of the *vaṣaṭ* call with the end of the *yājyā* verse occurs when that [end] is protracted (*pluta*). Or it occurs when it is not protracted.
This [joining] does not take place in the *upāṃśuyāja*. (Paribhāṣās 1.1.42–44)
The syllable *ā* used for invocation (*āvāhana*) should be protracted.

(Paribhāṣā 1.2.1) The *ye yajāmahe* formula, with its initial syllable protracted, precedes the *yājyā* verses. (Paribhāṣā 1.2.2) The protraction used in sacrificial recitation (*yājñikī-pluti*) consists of four morae (*mātrā*). (Paribhāṣā 1.2.3)

1.2. The diphthongs *ai* and *au* have the palate as their place of articulation; they become *ā*, *i*, and *ī*. (Paribhāṣās) 1.2. They have the lips as their place of articulation; they become *ā*, *u*, and *ū*. (Paribhāṣās) 1.2.
The other vowels remain in their original form (*prakṛti*). (Paribhāṣās)
The vowels *e* and *o* are *pragṛhya*.
(Paribhāṣā 7) At the end of a *yājyā* verse, [the *e* and *o* are *pragṛhya*]. (Paribhāṣā 8) A *visarjanīya* followed by a *repha* (r) becomes *repha*. (Paribhāṣā 9)
10. A non-repeated consonant (*ariphita*) is elided. 11. The letter *m* becomes an *anusvāra*.
12. Other consonants remain in their original form (*prakṛti*).

The vowel *au* in the syllable *vaṣaṭ* has a duration of four morae. (13) The vowel *a* following the letter *ṣ* [in *vaṣaṭ*] [is also four morae]. (14) Or both may remain in their original form (*prakṛti*). (15) (Paribhāṣās)
16. Or the former [syllable] by its original nature.
17. According to Jātūkarṇya, the vowel *a* is by its original nature.
18. One should utter the *vaṣaṭ* call according to the *bārhata* and *rāthaṃtara* meters: long at the beginning and short at the end.

1.2. And after the *ye yajāmahe* formula, there is the designation of the deity together with the *puronuvākyā*. (19) (Paribhāṣās) 1.2. But this does not occur when there is a *praiṣa* (direction). (20) (Paribhāṣās) 1.2.
When "he offers" (*juhoti*) is stated, clarified butter (*sarpiḥ*) is intended [as the substance]. (21) (Paribhāṣās)
The utterance of *svāhā* occurs at the end of the sacrificial mantras (ŚŚS 1.2.22).
It also occurs at the end of the mantras for placing the fuel-sticks (ŚŚS 1.2.23).
Due to the distinctness of the mantras, there is a distinctness of the ritual acts (ŚŚS 1.2.24).

25. The particle *iti* occurs at the end of a mantra. 26. By means of the final word of a mantra, there is the application of the ritual action to the instruments [of the rite]. 27. Having been prompted by the *saṃpraiṣa*, he recites.
He sacrifices in that manner.
(28) This constitutes the general rule for all sacrifices.
(29) Having fasted, he sacrifices with the full-moon oblation. (1) [Darśapūrṇamāsa]
Likewise, with the New Moon [offering]. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) 3.
There are two Full Moon [offerings]. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) 4.
And the New Moon [offerings]. (Darśapūrṇamāsa)

The two *paurṇamāsī* (full-moon) days are those on which the moon rises full after it has set [on the previous day], and those on which it sets while still full. The two *amāvāsye* (new-moon) days are that day on which one will not see the moon tomorrow, and that day on which the moon is not seen at all. Regarding the performance of the sacrifice (*ijyā*) on these occasions, one may act according to one's preference.
Thus, by the instruction "at the full moon" and "at the new moon," [the rites] are established as distinct. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) 8.
And the words associated with those [rites] are likewise. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) 9.
The rest is the same. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) 10.
In both [the New and Full Moon sacrifices], there is a cake (puroḍāśa) for Agni.
(Darśapūrṇamāsa) There is a silent sacrifice (upāṃśuyāja) for Agni-Soma. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) Or it may be for Viṣṇu. (Darśapūrṇamāsa)

On the new moon day (Amāvāsyā), for one who does not perform the Sāṃnāyya offering, the second oblation is dedicated to Indra and Agni. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) For one who performs the Sāṃnāyya offering, the [second] oblation is dedicated to Indra. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) Or it may be dedicated to Mahendra. (Darśapūrṇamāsa)
1.3. However, one who does not offer the *saṃnayya* (curdled milk) should perform the *upāṃśuyāja* as belonging to Viṣṇu. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) 1.4.

Being addressed by the Adhvaryu, the Hotṛ proceeds between the *utkara* (mound of rubbish) and the *praṇītā* waters; he steps upon the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) with the forepart of his right foot. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) 1.4.
The heel [of the foot] is aligned with the edge of the altar behind. (Darśapūrṇamāsa)
And having stepped forward, he takes his place. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) When he has been prompted with the call, "For Agni being enkindled," (Darśapūrṇamāsa) [he recites the verse]. 1.4.3–4.

Whom shall I resort to? Him I resort to. That meter which is your refuge, O Prajāpati, that I resort to. As much as you know, O Viṣṇu, so much shall I perform for you. Impelled by the divine Savitṛ, I shall perform the office of the officiating priest. Homage to Agni, the overseer; homage to Vāyu, the listener; homage to Āditya, the announcer. Today I shall speak speech pleasing to the gods, worthy of being heard by men, accompanied by *svadhā* for the ancestors, and providing stability for all beings, O Praśāstṛ.

"By means of myself, my offspring, and my cattle, I take refuge in Prajāpati; may there be safety for us. I shall recite the section pertaining to Prajāpati. Having murmured "Bhūḥ bhuvaḥ svaḥ," and having uttered the sound *him* three times, he should join [the verses] with a moderate voice, beginning with "pra vo vājā. (Darśapūrṇamāsa Śrautasūtra 1.4.5–7)
"O Agni, come for the feast! and "O thou who art worthy of praise!"—these two triplets (Ṛgveda 6.16.10–12 and 7.1.1–3).
(Darśapūrṇamāsa) "We choose Agni as our messenger"—this one verse (Ṛgveda 1.12.1). (Darśapūrṇamāsa) "The sacrificial rite being kindled"—this one verse (Ṛgveda 3.27.1). (Darśapūrṇamāsa)
There are three [verses] in the *sāptadaśya* (the seventeen-fold stoma). (11) These occur elsewhere than at the two seasonal sacrifices (*sāyana*) of the New and Full Moon (*darśapūrṇamāsa*).
(12) "O Agni, kindled, invoked with oblations..."—these two [verses]. (13) (Darśapūrṇamāsa)

"O Agni, you are great, O Brāhmaṇa, descendant of Bharata"—having joined [the mantra] with the *praṇava* (OM). (Darśapūrṇamāsa) Having recited the three ancestral lineages (*ārṣeya*) of the sacrificer from the remote past down to the present. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) But for one who belongs to two *gotras*, there are six. (Darśapūrṇamāsa)
17. For one who is not a Brāhmaṇa, [the invocation] is with the name of a distinguished family priest (*purohita-pravara*).
18. Or rather, for all [classes], it is with the *Mānava* [pravara].

19. Having paused after [reciting]: "Kindled by the gods, kindled by Manu, praised by the seers, rejoiced by the wise, lauded by the poets, sharpened by the sacred word (*brahman*), and offered with clarified butter (*ghṛta-āhavana*)."
"Leader of sacrifices, charioteer of rites, invincible Hotṛ, swift bearer of oblations"—having paused here;
(Darśapūrṇamāsa) "The vessel of the mouth, the ladle of the gods, the cup from which the gods drink; like the felly around the spokes, O Agni, you encompass the gods"—having paused here;
(Darśapūrṇamāsa) "While concluding [the rite], he invokes the deities. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) 1.4.22.

"Bring the gods for the sacrificer. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) "O Agni, bring Agni; bring Soma"—thus for the two butter-portions (*ājyabhāgau*). (Darśapūrṇamāsa) "Bring Agni; bring Agni-Soma, or [bring] Viṣṇu; bring Agni-Soma; bring Indra-Agni; bring Indra, or Mahendra. (Darśapūrṇamāsa)
Bring the gods who drink the clarified butter.
(Darśa-pūrṇamāsa) Bring Agni for the office of the Hotṛ. (Darśa-pūrṇamāsa) Bring [the gods] according to their own greatness. (Darśa-pūrṇamāsa)
"O Jātavedas, come hither and perform the sacrifice well," with these words he invokes [the fire].
(Darśapūrṇamāsa) Having sat down with his right knee raised and having touched the ground with his right forefinger, he mutters [the following]: (Darśapūrṇamāsa)

"For this foundation, O Mother Earth, may I not be cut off; do not harm me, do not injure me. I shall conceive honey, I shall win honey, I shall produce honey. Today I shall utter speech full of honey for the gods, and pleasant for men. With this fifteenfold thunderbolt, I strike down my evil rival. Or [he does so] with the seventeenfold [stoma]. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) 1.5. When addressed as "O man," [he responds]. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) 1.6.

"O God Savitṛ, they choose thee here together with Vaiśvānara as father; O Indra, Pūṣan, Bṛhaspati, speak forth and sacrifice! May we be among the bounty of the Vasus, among the favor of the Rudras, and among the faultless Ādityas. When the sidelong glance flew away during the choosing of this Hotṛ, may Agni Jātavedas, the far-seeing, bring it back again. Having murmured this while the Pravara is being performed, (he concludes the Darśa-Pūrṇamāsa).

Having risen, having touched the right shoulder of the *adhvaryu* with his right forefinger and the right shoulder of the *āgnīdhra* with his left, he recites: "We take hold of Indra, the domestic priest, for the choosing of the Hotṛ, by whom the gods and the Aṅgirases went to the highest heaven, to the sky. Sixty and ninety fetters are spread between heaven and earth; they bind the simple one, but I, the wise, pass over them. May both these, heaven and earth, be pleasant to me. (Darśapūrṇamāsa)

"May the six expanses protect us from distress: heaven and earth, day and night, water and plants"—having thus released [the food], he turns his right arm following the turn of Indra and the turn of the Sun, saying: "I turn following the turn [of the gods]. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) ŚŚS 1.6.4–5.

"Parāvasu has been cast out—he who hates us and whom we hate, together with him. Having thus torn off a dry blade of grass from both sides at the Hotṛ’s seat and thrown it away toward the south-western intermediate direction, (6) he touches water. (7) Having placed a non-dry blade of grass with its tip pointing northward, (8) [he sits down]. (Darśapūrṇamāsa)
"I sit here in the seat of Arvāvasu," saying this, he sits down.

(Darśapūrṇamāsa) Having placed his right hand over his left and extending his hands forward, he mutters: "Homage to Heaven and Earth, to the two Hotṛs, the first-born, the all-makers! You two are the protectors of my body; guard my body, do not harm me, do not distress me. Thus he speaks, looking at the Āhavanīya and the Gārhapatya fires. (Darśapūrṇamāsa)

As the water flows out, he says, "This is your space. (Darśa-Pūrṇamāsa) Having murmured, "O Viśvedevas, instruct us; today [is the day] of speech; homage to the great ones," (Darśa-Pūrṇamāsa) he concludes with, "May Agni as Hotṛ know [the sacrifice]; may Agni know the office of the Hotṛ; may he know the means of protection; O sacrificer, may the deity be well-pleased with you. (Darśa-Pūrṇamāsa)
"Yo agnim hotāram avṛthāḥ"—this he recites in a low voice.

(Darśapūrṇamāsa) "O Adhvaryu, take up the butter-spoon, the one that belongs to the gods and contains all boons; let us invite the gods, let us invite those who are to be invited, let us pay homage to those worthy of homage, and let us sacrifice to those worthy of sacrifice. Having thus taken up the two offering-spoons (*sruva*), he performs the five fore-offerings (*prayāja*). (Darśapūrṇamāsa) "O Agni, may the kindling-sticks (*samidh*) partake of the clarified butter"—this is the first [fore-offering]. (Darśapūrṇamāsa)

"May the butter enjoy [the offering]"—this is the second [verse]. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) "O Agni, may Narāśaṃsa enjoy the butter"—this is the second [verse] for the Vasiṣṭhas, the Śunakas, the Atris, the Vadhryaśvas, the Kaṇvas, the Saṃkṛtis, the Kṣatriyas, and those desiring progeny. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) "O Agni, may [the gods] enjoy the butter"—this is the third [verse]. (Darśapūrṇamāsa)
"O Agni, may the sacrificial grass partake of the clarified butter"—this is the fourth [Prayāja offering].

(Darśa-Pūrṇamāsa) "Svāhā! To Agni! Svāhā! To Soma! Svāhā! To Agni! Svāhā! To Agni and Soma, or to Viṣṇu! Svāhā! To Agni and Soma! Svāhā! To Indra and Agni! Svāhā! To Indra, or to Mahendra! Svāhā! May the gods who drink the clarified butter, being pleased, O Agni, consume the oblation of clarified butter"—these are the Yājyās for the Prayājas. (Darśa-Pūrṇamāsa) "Agni [destroys] the Vṛtras; you, O Soma, are the lord of the virtuous"—these are the two Ājyabhāga offerings, known as the "Vārtraghnas," at the Full Moon sacrifice. (Darśa-Pūrṇamāsa)

"O Agni, with the ancient [song]; O Soma, with our hymns"—these two [verses] containing the word *vṛdh* (increasing) are used at the new moon sacrifice (*amāvāsyā*). (Darśapūrṇamāsa) "May Agni, being pleased, accept the oblation of clarified butter; may Soma, being pleased, accept the oblation of clarified butter"—these are the two *yājyā* verses. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) "Agni is the head"—this is the *puronuvākyā* for the offering to Agni. (Darśapūrṇamāsa)
"Bhuvo yajñasya" is the *yājyā* [verse] for the [Darśapūrṇamāsa sacrifice].
(Darśapūrṇamāsa) "Agnīṣomāv imam" is the *puronuvākyā* for the *upāṃśuyāja*. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) "Juṣāṇāv agnīṣomāv ājyasya haviṣo vītām" is the *yājyā*. (Darśapūrṇamāsa)
"Idam viṣṇuḥ" and "vaṣaṭ te viṣṇave" are for the offering to Viṣṇu (sacrificial cake). Or [one may use] "juṣāṇo".
"Agnīṣomau savedasā yuvam etāni" is for the offering to Agni and Soma.

"O Indra and Agni, with your protection, come forward for the sake of the people"—this is for the offering to Indra and Agni. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) "Come, O Indra, bringing gain; you have conquered"—this is for the Sānnāyya offering. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) "Great is Indra, who by his might; great is Indra, like a hero"—this is for the offering to Mahendra. (Darśapūrṇamāsa)
"Indra, exhilarate yourself on all sides with your bay steeds for you"—this is [the invitatory verse] for Indra, who has no substitute.
(Darśapūrṇamāsa) "Pleasantly satisfy the gods"—this is the invitatory verse for the Sviṣṭakṛt offering. (Darśapūrṇamāsa)

He has sacrificed with this [oblation] to the dear abodes of Agni; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Soma; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Agni; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Agni and Soma, or of Viṣṇu; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Agni and Soma; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Indra and Agni; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Indra, or of Mahendra; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of the gods who drink the clarified butter (*ājyapāḥ*). May he sacrifice to the dear abodes of Agni the Hotṛ; may he sacrifice to his own majesty; may they be worshipped. ŚŚS 1.9.1–2.
"May he, Jātavedas, make the offerings effective; may he enjoy the oblation, O Agni, whatever today belongs to the people of the sacrifice"—this is the *yājyā* (verse for the offering).
(Darśapūrṇamāsa Śrauta Sūtra 1.9) Having uttered the *vaṣaṭ* call, there is the touching [of the mouth].

(Darśapūrṇamāsa Śrauta Sūtra 1.10) While about to invite [the guest] to eat, he anoints the forefinger of his right hand, as well as its upper joint and its middle joint. (Darśapūrṇamāsa Śrauta Sūtra 1.1)

"Of that which has been offered by the Lord of Speech, I partake for the sake of food and out-breath"—with these words, he first smears the ointment on the lower lip. "Of that which has been offered by the Lord of Mind, I partake for the sake of strength and up-breath"—with these words, he applies the subsequent [ointment] to the upper lip. (2) (Darśapūrṇamāsa) Having touched [water], (3) (Darśapūrṇamāsa) holding the northern blade with his right hand, (4) (Darśapūrṇamāsa) he proceeds.
With fingers not spread out and not formed into a fist, (5) having himself taken up the fifth [ladle], (6) he holds it level with his mouth or level with his heart. (7) (Darśa-Pūrṇamāsa)

Invited is the Bṛhat, together with the sky, together with the sun, together with sight; may the Bṛhat, together with the sky, together with the sun, together with sight, invite me. Invited is the Vāmadevya, together with the intermediate space, together with the wind, together with breath; may the Vāmadevya, together with the intermediate space, together with the wind, together with breath, invite me. (Darśapūrṇamāsa)

The *Rathantara* has been invoked together with the earth, together with Agni, together with speech, together with the cattle; may the *Rathantara*, together with the earth, together with Agni, together with speech, together with the cattle, invoke me. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) The stationary world has been invoked; may the stationary world invoke me. (Darśapūrṇamāsa)

Invited is the moving world; let the moving world invite me. Invited is the companion, the portion to be consumed; let the companion, the portion to be consumed, invite me. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) Invited are the seven officiating priests; let the seven officiating priests invite me. Invited are the cows along with the milk-mixture; let the cows along with the milk-mixture invite me. (Darśapūrṇamāsa)

"Speech has been invoked together with breath; may speech together with breath invoke me. Speech has been invoked together with the mind; may speech together with the mind invoke me. (Darśa-Pūrṇamāsa) "Food and rain have been invoked; may food and rain invoke me. Food that conquers has been invoked; may food that conquers invoke me. You are indeed she who has been invoked; enjoy me, O food! Having murmured this, he invokes food. (Darśa-Pūrṇamāsa)

The *iḷā* has been invoked; the *iḷā* has been invoked. May the *iḷā* call upon us; the *iḷā* has been invoked—the daughter of Manu, whose foot is dripping with ghee, the one belonging to Mitra and Varuṇa.

(Darśapūrṇamāsa) The Brahman created by the gods has been invoked. The divine *adhvaryus* have been invoked; the human ones have been invoked—those who protect this sacrifice and those who strengthen the lord of the sacrifice. Heaven and Earth have been invoked—the two born of old, observers of cosmic order (*ṛta*), goddesses, mothers of the gods. (Darśapūrṇamāsa)

"Invited is this sacrificer to the subsequent sacrifice to the gods; invited to the preparation of abundant oblation; may the gods enjoy this my oblation"—having thus invoked him with "Invited! (in that [spot]), he should pound [the grain] within the *īḍā* while reciting the four-verse mantra.

Or, at the end, the fourth [verse]. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) "Thou art refreshing; thou art pleasant; thou art the maker of pleasantness. As such, do thou establish us in good offspring and royal prosperity. O beloved one, may I attain thy favor; O invited one, may I obtain thy invitation. For the splendor of the mouth, for the fragrance of the mouth, I eat thee. Having thus eaten the northern *iḍā*, (Darśapūrṇamāsa) the others, with the sacrificer as the fifth, shall eat. (Darśapūrṇamāsa)

Until the *mārjana* (sprinkling), there is restraint of speech. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) With the three verses beginning "idam āpaḥ," they perform the *mārjana* within the altar (*antarvedi*) where the *pavitra* grass is present.
(Darśapūrṇamāsa) Once the portion for the Brahman priest has been carried around, they bring the *anvāhārya* rice. (Darśapūrṇamāsa)
This is the time for the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) for all *iṣṭi* sacrifices. (Darśa-Pūrṇamāsa) There is no *anvāhārya* rice in those sacrifices where a specific fee has been prescribed.

(Darśa-Pūrṇamāsa) Having consecrated the fuel-stick (*samidh*) with the mantra: "This is your fuel-stick, O Agni; through it may you increase and swell; and may we increase and swell," (Darśa-Pūrṇamāsa)

He performs three after-offerings (*anuyāja*). (Darśapūrṇamāsa) "May the divine sacrificial grass (*barhis*) partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of obtaining wealth. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) "May the divine Narāśaṃsa partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of obtaining wealth. (Darśapūrṇamāsa)

"May Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, the god, the giver of good wealth, the delightful, the sage, whose thoughts are true, the sacrificing priest—more worthy of sacrifice than the priest of every priest—O Agni, those gods whom thou hast sacrificed to and whom thou hast gratified, who have rejoiced in thy office as Hotṛ"—having paused here; "that sacrificial office which has been performed, leading to the gods, send this sacrifice to the gods in heaven. And as Sviṣṭakṛt, O Agni, thou hast become the Hotṛ; for the winning of wealth and the granting of wealth, accept it at the utterance of 'Namas'. These are the invitatory and offering verses for the after-sacrifices (anuyājas). (Darśapūrṇamāsa) 1.13.4.

"Whatever he prays for with this oblation, may he attain it; may he prosper in it; may the gods grant it to him; may the divine Agni win it from the gods, and we, the humans, [win it] from Agni. Having unloosed the cord from the *veda* with the mantra, "I release thee" (*pra tvā muñcāmi*), [he places] the *veda* and the unloosed cord in the hollowed palms of his wife. Pouring water over the *veda* and the cord, he mutters [the following]. (Darśapūrṇamāsa)

"For desire thee! Thou art the Veda (sacrificial knowledge). By that [means] through which thou didst become the Veda for the gods, as such, O Veda, be for us! Thou art the Veda; thou art acquisition; may I acquire. Thou art action; thou art the instrument; thou art performance. Thou art gain; thou art the gainer; may I gain. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) "May the Veda grant us wealth, abounding in ghee, providing a secure home, nourishing, thousandfold, and full of vigor. Having taken blades of grass, he places them between his thighs. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) Reciting "Stretching the thread," he spreads the sacrificial grass (barhis) to the north of the Gārhapatya fire. (Darśapūrṇamāsa) Having worshipped the remainder of the Veda with the formula, "Thou art the filler, the complete filler; fill me with offspring and cattle," (Darśapūrṇamāsa) he concludes. "O Agni Jātavedas, with this prayer you have sacrificed the sacrifice; sitting down within as the first among us, bestowing gain, release us with a good release. Bestow upon us wealth, O Jātavedas!

And a cow is the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā). (10) (The Ānvārambhaṇīyā Iṣṭi) The optional re-establishment of the sacred fires (punarādheya) is for one who is unaware [of the proper procedure]. Or [the fire] belongs to Agni and Varuṇa.

Before the shadows overlap, he carries fire from the *gārhapatya* to the *āhavanīya*.
(Āgnihotra 2.6) At the end of the night. (Āgnihotra 2.6) The making manifest [of the fires] applies to those maintained as a constant duty. (Āgnihotra 2.6)
A Brāhmaṇa who has heard [the Vedas], a village headman, or a Kṣatriya whose prosperity has departed;

(Āgnihotra) "Being lifted up, lift me up from evil—whatever I have done unknowingly and whatever I have done knowingly; whatever sin we have committed here by day—being lifted up, protect us from all that!

(Āgnihotra) "I offer the immortal oblation into the immortal [fire] on the earth, for the conquest of immortality. By means of it, may I conquer the infinite world which Prajāpati first conquered. (Āgnihotra)

"By night"—this is the modification for the morning [offering]. (Āgnihotra 2.6) Having swept around [the fires] and being about to offer, (Āgnihotra 2.6) he should sprinkle water around each fire three times with the formula, "I sprinkle thee, the Ṛta, with the Satya," and then offer the oblation. (Āgnihotra 2.6)
"In truth, with the *ṛta*, I sprinkle thee," [he says] in the morning.

(Āgnihotra 2.6.11) "You are the continuity of the sacrifice; for the continuity of the sacrifice, I lead thee," [with these words, he pours] a continuous stream from the *gārhapatya* fire toward the *āhavanīya*.
(Āgnihotra 2.6.12) "Stretching the thread," [he says] when a wild beast has passed between [the fires]. (Āgnihotra 2.6.13)
He offers when the sun has first set; (1) (Agnihotra);
or when a star is visible; (2) (Agnihotra);

Or [the sacrifice may be performed] after sunrise. (4) (Agnihotra) One should direct one’s mind toward the performance at the earlier time. (5) (Agnihotra) In the event of a failure in that [performance], there is an expiation. (6) (Agnihotra)
Having lifted [the fire] up until sunset, having sat [there], having offered the oblation, and having given a boon, he should consecrate it with the formula "bhūḥ.
(Āgnihotra 2.7) Or, without having offered [the oblation], having carried [the fire] out and having led forth another Āhavanīya fire, he should offer.
(Āgnihotra 2.7) Milk, gruel, curd, and clarified butter are the sacrificial offerings for the Agnihotra. (Āgnihotra 2.7)
2.7. He does not place the curd over the fire. (Āgnihotra) 2.7. He does not pour water back into the clarified butter. (Āgnihotra) 2.7.
Having thrown two young *kuśa* blades [into the pot], he ladles out the clarified butter. (Āgnihotra)

Afterwards, standing facing west toward the sun behind the *anvāhāryapacana* fire, the sacrificer worships it in the evening with the formula: “For the sake of truth and cosmic order (*ṛta*), may I lead thee, O sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*). (13) In the morning, he worships the *āhavanīya* fire with the formula: “For the sake of cosmic order and truth, may I lead thee, O sacrificial fee.

"From hunger and thirst; women indeed afflict a woman; may [Agni] protect you from the female that afflicts you—with the fire-stick (yoktrī), with the calf, with the hero," thus [he says] at evening and at dawn.

(Āgnihotra 2.8.6) "With the Anvāhāryapacana fire, with the hero," thus [he says] when there is a female calf. "From hunger and thirst; with the Agnihotra-pot, with the Gārhapatya fire, with the hero"—this is the modification. (Āgnihotra 2.8.8)
"O Agni, look upon me with your eye," saying this, he lights a fuel-stick and illuminates it.

(Āgnihotra 2.8.10) Having heated it again and silently illuminated it once more. (Āgnihotra 2.8.11)
Having extinguished [the fire] three times by pouring water from north to south,
as if not cutting off [the continuity],
and having touched the embers from the south while saying, "Homage to the gods," (Āgnihotra).

Having warded off the obstacles with the mantra "To Subhūti, vaḥ," (15). Having heated both the *sruva* and the *sruk* ladles, he pours [the clarified butter] into the *sruk* with the mantra "For hunger and thirst"; the word "vīreṇa" is a modification for the *sruva*. (16). He does so four or five times. (17).

The mantra is for each *sruva* ladle. (18) When the [oblation] has been drawn up, he touches the *sruk* ladle. (19) In the evening, he mutters: "In unison with the gods who move at night. (20) (Agnihotra)

"Joined with the gods who come in the morning," thus [he offers] in the morning. He then places the fuel-stick upon it, using the formula "With the fuel-stick that wards off hunger and thirst, with the hero [Agni]... as the modification for the *āhavanīya*. (Āgnihotra 2.8.22) Having moved the fuel-stick two finger-breadths away [from the edge of the fire], he makes the offering over it. (Āgnihotra 2.8.23)
"Fire is light, light is fire, svāhā"—thus [he offers] in the evening.
(Āgnihotra 2.9.1) "Sun is light, light is sun, svāhā"—thus [he offers] in the morning.
(Āgnihotra 2.9.2) Bending his right knee during those offerings for which there is no *vaṣaṭ* call. (Āgnihotra 2.9.3)
Having set it down to the north without letting it touch [the fire], he sets it down silently with more [ghee] than the previous offering.

"Life-breath has gone to the heavenly world; having conquered, I conquer. May there be safety for me from the state of being without a world, without a son, or without cattle"—with these words, the sacrificer breathes out over the first oblation.

(Āgnihotra 2.9.7) "Inhalation has gone to the self; having conquered, I conquer. May there be safety for me from the state of being without a world, without a son, or without cattle"—with these words, he breathes in over the second oblation.

2.9.10. To the north of the two oblations, he wipes [the spoon] twice toward the west in the evening.

He places his right hand, palm upwards, on top [of the left] with the thought in his mind, "I gratify the ancestors.

(13) Having sipped twice with the forefinger, having turned toward the north making a sound, having eaten from the ladle whose handle points eastward, having tilted it so its handle points eastward, having wiped it, having washed it, having sipped water, and having sprinkled water toward the northeast, he offers [the remainder] toward the northeast.

But for all [the offerings], they sacrifice wool after having placed the *sruva*-ladle to the north of the *gārhapatya* fire.

(16) "May the Lord of Prosperity bestow prosperity here; may Prajāpati cause offspring to be born here. To Agni, the possessor of wealth, the possessor of cattle, the Lord of Prosperity—*svāhā*! "Of that Savitṛ, the most excellent; *bhūḥ*, may speech be abundant, very abundant for me, svāhā! (The *āgnyupasthāna* in the *āgnyādheya*) "Going forward to the sacrifice," "This Agni is thousandfold," "Both of you," "This is your womb," "This one here," and "His ancient"—of these six [verses], he recites the first and the last three times each. "O Agni, you are the giver of life; give me life. O Agni, you are the giver of splendor; give me splendor. O Agni, you are the protector of the body; protect my body. O Agni, whatever is deficient in my body, fill that up for me. Kindling you, may we worship you for a hundred winters, radiant, we who possess vigor, making us vigorous; we who possess power, making us powerful—O Agni, the subduer of rivals, we who are undeceived, [worship] you the undeceivable. Having muttered this, (the ritual of *āgnyupasthāna* in the *āgnyādheya*).

"Citra-vaso, may there be well-being for you; may I reach the further shore"—thus three times. (The *agnyupasthāna* in the *āgnyādheya*) "O Agni, you have come together with the splendor of the Sun, together with the praise of the seers, together with the praise of the seers, together with your beloved abode. May I be united with long life, with splendor, with progeny, with your beloved abode, and with the increase of wealth"—having sat down, [he recites this]. (The *agnyupasthāna* in the *āgnyādheya*)

"O waters, may I partake of you as water; O greatness, may I partake of you as greatness; O strength, may I partake of you as strength; O increase of wealth, may I partake of you as the increase of wealth. O wealthy ones, rejoice in this womb, in this world, in this stall, in this dwelling, in this blessing, in this foundation! Be right here; do not depart from this place!"—with these words he approaches the cow. (The ritual attendance on the fires at the establishment of the sacred fires.)
"Thou art the collection (saṃhitā), possessing all forms; enter me with vigor and with lordship over cattle"—having touched her forehead with this [verse].

(Āgnyupasthāna in Āgnyādheya) "With 'Come near thee, O Agni'—this triplet—and with the two-footed verse 'O Agni, thou for us'—[he worships] the Gārhapatya fire. (Āgnyupasthāna in Āgnyādheya) "O Iḷā, come! O Aditi, come! O Sūnṛtā, come!"—with these words he approaches the cow. (Āgnyupasthāna in Āgnyādheya)
With the triplet beginning "To Soma, the one who makes sound" (RV 1.91.1–3), he [addresses] the Anvāhāryapacana fire from the north.

(ŚŚS 2.12.5) Having murmured the Māhitra formula between the Gārhapatya and Āhavanīya fires, he worships the Āhavanīya fire. (ŚŚS 2.12.6) He recites this [verse] three times: "That desirable [splendor] of Savitṛ," "Never art thou ungenerous," and "Thy spies, O Agni. (ŚŚS 2.12.7)
While offering oblations into all [fires], he places three fuel-sticks each time with the Mahāvyāhṛtis into the Āhavanīya fire; for one who performs a single oblation, it is into that one alone.

(ŚŚS 2.12.8) Having touched the embers to the south of the Āhavanīya fire with the mantra: "Thou art the divine thread; I take hold of thee; may I not be severed from thee," (ŚŚS 2.12.9) [he continues].

"Then you are the thread; do you continue this [line] for me with offspring, cattle, increase of wealth, good progeny, and great heroism. You are the human thread; take hold of me. Do not let yourself be cut off from me, O [Name]!"—having thus pronounced the name of his eldest son, or as many sons as he may have. (ŚŚS 2.12) /10/ (Agnisthāpana in Agnyādheya) "One who has no son born is [the thread] of himself. (ŚŚS 2.12) /11/ (Agnisthāpana in Agnyādheya)
"By truth I descend to the final bath; in the waters my vow [ends]. Having sipped water (*ācamya*), he releases his speech.

(ŚŚS 2.12) Then, in the morning: (ŚŚS 2.13) "Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! May I be rich in offspring through my offspring, rich in nourishment through my nourishments, and rich in heroes through my heroes. Fearlessness for you, fearlessness for us! With my mind I worship you. I go to the world and to heaven. Thus he worships the Āhavanīya fire. (ŚŚS 2.13)

Standing right here, he [approaches] the other two. (The *agnyupasthāna* in the *āgnyādheya*) "May there be safety for you; may there be safety for us. With speech I approach you; I approach offspring and cattle"—thus [he approaches] the *gārhapatya* fire. (The *agnyupasthāna* in the *āgnyādheya*) "May there be safety for you; may there be safety for us. With the out-breath (*prāṇa*) I approach you; I approach the diffused breath (*vyāna*) and life-span"—thus [he approaches] the *anvāhāryapacana* fire. (The *agnyupasthāna* in the *āgnyādheya*)

"May there be fearlessness for you; may there be fearlessness for us. With the desire [for prosperity], he approaches [the fires] with the words, "I approach for wealth and prosperity," addressing all [the fires]. (ŚŚS 2.13.6) The procedure is the same from the fuel-stick (*samidh*) onwards until the dismissal of the vow (*vratavisarjana*).
(ŚŚS 2.13.7) Or rather, [he may perform the worship] with this very [formula] every evening and morning. (ŚŚS 2.13.8)

Or, [the ritual] may be performed without attendance in the morning. (ŚŚS 2.13) One who is about to depart on a journey gazes at the fires, saying: "Fearlessness for you; let there be fearlessness for us.
(ŚŚS 2.14) He addresses the Gārhapatya fire, saying: "O friend of men, protect my offspring; protect me from human danger. (ŚŚS 2.14)
Then, [he addresses] the Anvāhāryapacana fire with: "O Aryaman, protect my food; protect me from the fear of my ancestors.
(3) Having gone to the north of that, [he addresses] the Āhavanīya fire with: "O Śaṃsa, protect my cattle; protect me from the fear of the gods.
(4) Having lifted up three steps with the words "Food! Food!", he restrains his speech from the vicinity [of the fires]. (7)

For the reason [for this] has not departed. (8) At the two junctions of day and night (*saṃdhivelā*), having sipped water (*ācamya*) and restrained his speech, and having sipped water again, he may release [his speech] with the *mahāvyāhṛti* formulas.
(9) He should restrain his speech within the range of vision of the fires. When returning from a journey, (10)
And likewise, the gazing [at the fires].

(The *agnyupasthāna* in the *āgnīdheya*) "O Agni, sovereign lord, we have come to you, the greatest slayer of Vṛtra, the best finder of wealth for us. Bestow upon us splendor and power. "O *śaṃsya*, you have protected my cattle; protect them for me indeed. You have protected me from fear of the gods; protect me from that indeed," [with these words] he addresses the *āhavanīya* fire. (The *agnyupasthāna* in the *āgnīdheya*) The removal of grass and the placing of fuel-sticks are performed in all [fires]. (The *agnyupasthāna* in the *āgnīdheya*)

"This Agni Purīṣya is wealthy and increases prosperity. O Agni Purīṣya, bestow upon me splendor and power! O Atharvan, you have protected my food; protect that for me from the fear of the ancestors. You have protected it from that [fear]; therefore, protect me indeed!"—with these words he addresses the Anvāhāryapacana fire. (Āgnyupasthāna in the Āgnyādheya)

"This Agni Gṛhapati, from the Gārhapatya fire, is the best provider of wealth for his offspring. O Agni Gṛhapati, bestow upon me splendor and power! O hero, you have protected my offspring; protect them for me! You have protected them from human fear; protect them for me!"—thus [he addresses] the Gārhapatya fire. (ŚŚS 2.15) He departs on a journey while keeping the fires separated. (ŚŚS 2.15) By that very [separation], he is released from [the obligation of maintaining] them. (ŚŚS 2.15)
ŚŚS 2.16. The rite for Vāstoṣpati is performed when the ten-night period of the *dhruva* sacrifice has passed during the subsequent half [of the year], after the fires have been carried forth.

(The Āgnyupasthāna in the Āgnīdhra-ādhāna) ŚŚS 2.16. Having unyoked the fire-stick standing on the south side and spread out a garment, he recites the invitatory verse: "O Vāstoṣpati, acknowledge [us]," and then offers the oblation with the offering verse: "O Vāstoṣpati, grant us prosperity. (The Āgnyupasthāna in the Āgnīdhra-ādhāna) ŚŚS 2.16. Once the oblation has been offered, he should discard that which was not formally installed. (The Āgnyupasthāna in the Āgnīdhra-ādhāna)
While ascending [the ladder], having warmed his hands over the *gārhapatya* fire, he touches his vital breaths with the mantra: "Come, ascend to my vital breaths.

(1) He does so once each time with the mantra, twice each time silently. (2) With the mantra, "This is your womb," he warms the *vāraṇī* wood over the fire. (3) (The *agnyupasthāna* in the *āgnyādheya*)

With the mantra, he should do so once each time; silently, twice each time. (Regarding the worship of the fires in the *Āgnādheya*) In this same manner, [he worships] from the Āhavanīya fire. (Regarding the worship of the fires in the *Āgnādheya*) In the case of a fire that is maintained perpetually, it is different. (Regarding the worship of the fires in the *Āgnādheya*)
2.17. And the churning [of the fire] must take place before sunset. (The worship of the fires in the *Āgnyādheya*) 2.17.

Having descended [the fire] from himself into his two kindling woods (*araṇi*) with the verse: "Descend again, O Jātavedas; knowing, carry our oblation to the gods. Bestow upon us long life, progeny, and wealth; shine unharmed within our home," he performs the churning. (The worship of the fires in the *Āgnyādheya*) 2.17.
[He may do so] either in a common fire or in a common fire. (The worship of the fires in the *Āgnyādheya*)
When the full moon has concluded, there is an *iṣṭi* sacrifice to Indra Vimṛdh.
It is a modification of the New Moon sacrifice. [The verses are:
"O Indra, the ruling power," and "Like a terrifying wild beast."
"O Agni, beloved of the house, be strong"—with these words is the offering to Agni Sviṣṭakṛt performed.
(ŚŚS 3.1.4) On the new moon day, when the sacrifice to Aditi has been completed.
(ŚŚS 3.1.5) This is a modification of the Full Moon sacrifice. (ŚŚS 3.1.6)
Those [verses] which belong to the Vaiṃṛdha [offering] are for the Sviṣṭakṛt [portion].

Having invoked [the ancestors], they do not eat this [food]. (25) Having smelled the portions, they cast them away. (26) They give [the portions] to the ancestors. (27) (Cṃ: Śāka; Pitrya)

Reciting, "By this station, generating deeds; for he is glowing, a wide path for the one seeking [him]; he has risen up to the support, the summit of the honey, when he extended his own body within his body," they go to the north of the *anvāhāryapacana* fire.

(Cṃ: Śrāddha: Pitrya) Having worshipped the *āhavanīya* fire with, "We have eaten thee, O fair-to-behold; thou hast rejoiced; do thou hear us well," (Cṃ: Śrāddha: Pitrya) [They worship] the *dakṣiṇāgni* with the three verses beginning, "Now we call the mind hither. (Cṃ: Śrāddha: Pitrya)
"May my mind return to me," they should say.

When [the sacrifice] has been completed, [he performs] the Full Moon sacrifice (Paurṇamāsa).

"Crossing over, visible to all, the golden ornament of heaven"—
this is the *upāṃśu* offering to Sūrya.

Either a cow, or a plough with twelve yokes, or not at all—a horse. (ŚŚS 3.18) (Cm: Śunāsīrya) (Cm: Śunāsīrya) (Cm: Śunāsīrya)

The other [rites] are the same as those for the Vaiśvadeva sacrifice. (Cm: Śunāsīrya) But the Paurṇamāsa [offering] is performed when the fire-drills are not being churned. (Cm: Śunāsīrya) 3.18.14.

O wise ones, offer the oblation with the ladle to Indra Śunāsīra; may he, the discerning one, accept it. Bring together the ghee-rich offerings for this Lord of the Tawny Steeds (Haryaśva); O Indra, being in harmony with the Ṛbhus through sacred prayer, as Śunāsīra, enjoy this oblation.
Seeking horses, we invoke Śuna for prosperity.

Or on the full moon day of Māgha.

3.19. Expiation (*prāyaścitta*) is prescribed for the failure to perform a rite. 3.19. When a substance is lost, a substitute (*pratinidhi*) is used. 3.19. "Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā! O Agni, you are the one who comes straightway (*ayās*), you are beyond reproach, you are indeed truth; you are the straightway-come one. Created by a mind that is straightway-come, being straightway-come yourself, you have carried the oblation. As the straightway-come one, grant us healing. With this, two expiation-oblations (*prāyaścittāhutī*) are offered in all cases of defects.
The Āhavanīya fire is [the locus] for all oblations. (4) The *juhū* ladle is the vessel. (5) In expiatory rites (*prāyaścitta*), four portions [of ghee] are taken up. (6)

3.19. Immediately after a fault, there must be an expiation (*prāyaścitta*); for as long as a fault has not been removed, there can be no engagement in the subsequent [rite]. 3.19. Furthermore, in some cases, an expiation is prescribed directly by perception; in such instances, one should perform both: the general expiation and the specific expiation pertaining to that particular qualification.

If the Āhavanīya fire should go out before it has been lifted up, a Brāhmaṇa who knows much [of the ritual] shall perform the lifting. Having tied a piece of gold (*jātarūpa*) with *kuśa* grass, they carry it in front. If it goes out after sunrise, silver is used. A choice gift (*vara*) is the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*). (Cṃ:

Prāyaścitta) If the Āhavanīya fire has gone out, the lifting is performed from the Gārhapatya fire, and an oblation to Agni Jyotiṣmat is offered. (Cṃ: Prāyaścitta) "Upward, O Agni, [go] pure with light... (Cṃ: Prāyaścitta)
If the Gārhapatya fire has gone out, one should first determine the site, then lead forward another Āhavanīya fire and offer oblations.

Or, having consigned the fires into the kindling woods, one should depart toward the north. If both fires have gone out, the churning of the Gārhapatya fire is performed from the upper fire-stick using a brand of the Gārhapatya fire.
If the firebrands are not available, one should touch the churning sticks with ashes and perform an *iṣṭi* sacrifice to Agni Tapasvat, Janadvat, and Pāvakavat.

"Come hither with fervor among the people, O Agni, as the purifier with your flame; come to this my well-spoken hymn. Come to us with fervor among the people, O Agni, shining as the purifier; place our offerings among the gods.

In the event that the fires have risen [and then gone out], or have set [and then failed to rekindle], or have been lost for some other reason, one should produce them again by means of the *agnyādheya* rite.

If the *agnihotrī* cow, being approached [by a bull], should low, one should offer a handful of barley with the verse: "From well-grazed pastures... (RV 10.27.22). If she should sit down, one should make her stand up with a fresh stick while reciting:

"From whatever you fear that you sit down, from that make us free of fear. For the sake of all progeny, homage to Rudra, the giver of gifts. Then one should address her with the mantra: "The goddess Aditi has risen; she has bestowed long life upon the lord of the sacrifice. She prepares a portion for Indra, and for Mitra and Varuṇa" (RV 10.63.10). (Āśvalāyana Gṛhya Sūtra 3.20, Prāyaścitta section).

Or he may give it to one who is hateful. (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra Prāyaścitta 3.20) When the sacrificial oblation has been spilled, [he should recite]: "To you two, O Viṣṇu and Varuṇa, who come hither—by whose power the worlds are propped up, who are most heroic in valor, most mighty, who rule over all with irresistible strengths; O Viṣṇu and Varuṇa, you have come at the first invocation. Having sprinkled it with water, [he says]: "It has fallen, it has settled, it has been propagated. The sacrifice has gone to heaven, to the gods, as the third; may wealth attend me from there. The sacrifice has gone to the intermediate space, to the fathers, as the third; may wealth attend me from there. The sacrifice has gone to the earth, to men, as the third..."
Then he should consecrate it with the mantra: "May wealth come to me. (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 3.20).
If a Brāhmaṇa, out of contempt, should not consume it, this is the mark of one who is defiled. For him, water is the means of purification.
(Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 3.20)

3.20. When a remainder exists, the completion [of the rite] is performed with that. (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra: Prāyaścitta) 3.20. In the absence of a remainder, one should produce another [substance]. (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra: Prāyaścitta) 3.20.
If that substance is unavailable, one should substitute whichever other *sāman* one considers appropriate. (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra: Prāyaścitta)
This is the rule regarding substitutes.

(10) And there is no modification of the words. (11) When that which has been offered to the deity is spoiled, there is no repetition of the *hautra* (the duties of the Hotṛ priest); having prepared another oblation, he should offer it to the deity. (12)

(Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 3.20.20) In the *iṣṭi* sacrifices, animal sacrifices (*paśubandha*), and the Soma sacrifice, the Brahman priest performs the expiation (*prāyaścitta*). (Brahmatvam & Yājamānam, Īṣṭis)
If there should be a fault in the Ṛgveda, [he should offer] "bhūḥ svāhā" in the Gārhapatya fire; (Brahmatvam & Yājamānam in the Iṣṭis).
If there should be a fault in the Yajurveda, [he should offer] "bhuvaḥ svāhā" in the Anvāhāryapacana fire; (Brahmatvam & Yājamānam in the Iṣṭis).
But in the Soma sacrifice, [he should offer] in the Āgnīdhrīya fire. (Brahmatvam & Yājamānam in the Iṣṭis).

If [the fire] is in the Sāmaveda, one should offer with "svaḥ svāhā" into the Āhavanīya fire. (ŚŚS 3.21.6) If the [fire] goes out while one has not yet performed the *upasthāna* (reverential attendance), one must perform the *upasthāna* facing each of the directions. (ŚŚS 3.21.7)

Having performed the *upasthāna* (reverential attendance), if there is no interruption, it is as when one has returned from a journey. (ŚŚS 3.21.8) Having consigned the fires into the kindling woods (*samāroha*), if there is no interruption, [the procedure for] churning [the fire] applies.
(ŚŚS 3.21.9) There is no *upasthāna* performed upon the two kindling woods (*araṇī*). (ŚŚS 3.21.10)

One should not abandon the sacred fires (*agni*) without performing an oblation (*homa*) or a sacrifice (*ijyā*). (11) However, having performed an expiation (*prāyaścitta*), one should perform the rites that were omitted; one should perform them.

The two [the sacrificer and his wife] should eat before the calves are driven away.

In the Āhavanīya fire, with the last of the Mahāvyāhṛtis;
(ŚŚS 4.2.2) in the Gārhapatya fire, with the first;

And the attendance [is performed] with the remainder.

(ŚŚS 4.2.8) With the seven verses beginning "May the evil be burnt away" (*apa naḥ śośucad agham*), or with the ten verses beginning "O Agni, lead us" (*agne naya yas tvā hṛdā tvam no agne adharāt*), [he performs the attendance].
(ŚŚS 4.2.9) And the attendance is performed with the two hymns beginning "To Agni [I direct] my speech" (*pra agnaye vācam*) and "This hymn" (*imam stomam*). (ŚŚS 4.2.10)
The [sacrifice] of the Prāgahīya is performed silently. (ŚŚS 4.2.11) The [sacrifice] of the Paiṅgya is performed with the Mahāvyāhṛtis.

The *Āruṇa* [Brāhmaṇa] is the final [text].

(ŚŚS 4.3.1) Having placed the winnowing basket, the cooking pot, the wooden sword (*sphya*), the vessel, and the mortar and pestle to the east of the southern fire, (ŚŚS 4.3.2)
3. Having placed the wooden sword (sphya) on the *kuśa* grass to the south of the Gārhapatya fire;

[Having placed] the cooking pot (*sthālī*) in a winnowing basket (*śūrpa*) in front [of the fire]. (The Piṇḍapitṛyajña)

Bending his left knee and holding the rice grains with his fist closed low, he takes them while meditating on the ancestors. (ŚŚS 4.3.6) Having had the grains husked once by his wife, having cooked them in the southern fire, having poured clarified butter over them, having removed them from the fire toward the west, having swept around the area, having strewn grass, and having sprinkled water, he bends his right knee, wears the sacrificial cord over the left shoulder, sits facing east, and offers the oblation with a stirring-spoon. (ŚŚS 4.3.8)

"To Agni Kavyavāhana, svāhā! To Soma Pitṛmat, svāhā! To Yama Āṅgirasvat Pitṛmat, svāhā! (ŚŚS 4.4). Having cast the stirring-stick (mekṣaṇa) into the fire, he should wipe the southern part of the southern fire-altar with the wooden sword (sphya), saying: "The Asuras and Rakṣas who sit upon the altar are driven away," and then sprinkle it with water. "Those Asuras who, assuming various forms, move about with the funeral offering (svadhā), who carry the *parāpur* and *nipura*—may Agni thrust them out from this world. (ŚŚS 4.4.2a)

Having thus wiped the firebrand and placed it in the southern half [of the altar], and having placed once-cut *kuśa* grass at the base of the wiped spot, he pours water onto the *kuśa* grass with his hand turned downwards, pronouncing the name of the father: "O [Name], pour water for yourself and for those who follow you here!
(ŚŚS 4.4). In the same manner, he performs this for the grandfather to the south (ŚŚS 4.4), and likewise for the great-grandfather (ŚŚS 4.4).
Having placed the rice-balls (*piṇḍas*) according to the manner of the water-offering (*avanejana*), saying: "O [Name], this is for you, and for those who follow you here," (ŚŚS 4.4.5).
When there is a division among the paternal ancestors, both [offerings] are made in a single [place]. (ŚŚS 4.4.6). There is no [offering] for one whose father is living. (ŚŚS 4.4.7).

Not for one whose life has been cut short. (ŚŚS 4.4.8) [Piṇḍapitṛyajña] Or rather, for those [ancestors] from whom his father descended, or for those from whom his son will descend. (ŚŚS 4.4.9) [Piṇḍapitṛyajña] Or [the rite may end] with the oblation. (ŚŚS 4.4.10) [Piṇḍapitṛyajña]

"O Pitṛs, rejoice here; O Pitṛs, come hither according to your respective portions. (ŚŚS 4.4.11) Having turned toward the north, (ŚŚS 4.4.12) he should remain seated there until three times [the sound of the water has been made]. (ŚŚS 4.4.13) (The Piṇḍapitṛyajña)

"Amīmadanta pitaro yathābhāgam avīvṛṣata" (The fathers have rejoiced; they have been satisfied according to their portions). (15) (Piṇḍapitṛyajña) "Omo vaḥ pitaraḥ jīvāya, namo vaḥ pitaraḥ śoṣāya / Namo vaḥ pitaraḥ ghorāya, namo vaḥ pitaraḥ rasāya / Namo vaḥ pitaraḥ balāya, namo vaḥ pitaraḥ mṛtyave //" (1a) (Piṇḍapitṛyajña) "Homage to you, O fathers, for life; homage to you, O fathers, for sapidity. Homage to you, O fathers, for the terrible; homage to you, O fathers, for flavor. Homage to you, O fathers, for strength; homage to you, O fathers, for death. (1a) (Piṇḍapitṛyajña)

"Homage to you, O fathers, for your wrath; homage to you, O fathers, for your *svadhā*. Homage to you, O fathers; O fathers, homage to you! Those who are here as fathers—may you be the most excellent among them. Those who are here as human beings—we may we be the most excellent among them. That which is yours there as *svadhā*, let that be ours here. That prosperity which is yours there, let that be ours here. O fathers, grant us houses! (Piṇḍapitṛyajña) 1b–1c.
"O Pitṛs, this garment is for you; put it on, O Pitṛs"—having thus offered three threads;
(ŚŚS 4.5). "Carrying strength, nectar, ghee, milk, honey, and flowing liquor—you are the *svadhā*; satisfy our Pitṛs"—having poured out the remainder of the water;
(ŚŚS 4.5). Having smelled the *piṇḍas*; (ŚŚS 4.5).
Having placed [the remainder] down, he should eat it;
(5) or he should give it to a Brāhmaṇa; (6) or he should cast it into water. (7) (The Piṇḍapitṛyajña)

Having cast the firebrand into the fire (ŚŚS 4.5.9), and having thrown the grass-bundle, which was cut in one stroke, after it (ŚŚS 4.5.10).

When the fire is being led forward, he should follow it. (Regarding the office of the Brahman priest at the *iṣṭi*s.

"Thou art the protector of the breath; protect my breath," [he says] over the two nostrils and the mouth.
