(Regarding the office of the Brahman priest in the *iṣṭis*) "Thou art the protector of the ear; protect my ear," [he says] over the two ears. (Regarding the office of the Brahman priest in the *iṣṭis*)
"I seat you in the belly of Indra"—with these words, [he places it] on the navel.

(Brahmatvam in sacrifices) "You are the protector of hearing; protect my hearing"—with these words, [he places it] on the two ears. (Brahmatvam in sacrifices) "I seat you in the belly of Indra"—with these words, [he places it] on the navel. (Brahmatvam in sacrifices)

"Who gave? To whom did he give? Desire gave; to desire did he give. Desire is the giver; desire is the receiver; O Desire, this is for thee"—having thus recited while receiving the *anvāhārya* rice, [the Adhvaryu says]:
"O Brahman, I shall proceed. Having been addressed thus, [the Brahman] mutters:

"O God Savitṛ, they have proclaimed this sacrifice of thine to Bṛhaspati the Brahman; through him protect the sacrifice, through him protect the lord of the sacrifice, through him protect me; impelled by the divine Savitṛ," and then he gives the impulse: "Om, proceed! (ŚŚS 4.7.15–17).
When the *praṇītā* waters have been released, the dismissal of the Brahman priest [takes place].

(Brahmatvam in sacrifices) The Brahman portion is consumed. (Brahmatvam in sacrifices) With the formula, "I gaze upon thee with unimpaired vision for the increase of wealth, for good progeny, and for heroic vigor; thou art the tongue of Agni, a good invoker for the gods; for every station, be mine; for every sacrificial formula," the wife gazes at the clarified butter. (Yājamānam in sacrifices)
"Thou art brilliance; thou art pure; thou art immortality; thou belongest to all the gods"—with these words the sacrificer touches the sacrificial ladles when they have been placed.

(ŚŚS 4.8) "They have settled, firm in the womb of Truth, in the world of good deeds; protect them, O Viṣṇu; protect the sacrifice; protect the lord of the sacrifice"—having touched the oblations thus placed, he says, "Protect me, O mother of the sacrifice," referring to himself. (ŚŚS 4.8, 3a)

"Thou art rain; cut off my evil! Thou art knowledge; know my evil! Having sipped water with these words, he places a fuel-stick on the Āhavanīya fire with the formula: "O Agni, Lord of Vows, I shall perform the vow; may I be able to do it; may it be successful for me. Here I approach truth from untruth," and then he restrains his speech. (ŚŚS 4.8) "O Agni, O Vāyu, O Lightning, O Moon, may I attain your world!"—with this he should meditate. (ŚŚS 4.8) Or whatever desire he may have [he should meditate upon that]. (ŚŚS 4.8)
"May I obtain food and other provisions that are not subject to exhaustion," [he says] regarding the sky or the ocean.

(ŚŚS 4.8) "May this great power of Indra bestow strength upon us; may the liberal lords attend to us. May our blessings be realized; may our blessings be fulfilled. [He says this] when the *ilā* is being invoked. (ŚŚS 4.9)

"O Bradhna, overflow! Protect my breath; protect my offspring; protect my cattle. Yield me the Brahman; yield me the Kṣatra; yield me the people. You are the ordainer of the quarters; may the quarters be favorable to me; may the quarters be favorable to me. When they are so ordained, may I prosper therein. O Fathers, rejoice here; O Fathers, come to your respective portions. Having thus touched the sacrificial cake placed upon the *barhis* grass. (The portion for the Sacrificer in the *iṣṭis*)
Having placed [the food] back down with the mantra, "The ancestors have rejoiced; they have satisfied themselves according to their portions," (ŚŚS 4.9.3).

Then, having touched the *anvāhārya* rice with the mantra, "Thou art the portion of Prajāpati, full of vigor, full of milk; thou art imperishable; mayest thou not perish for me in yonder world, in that world, and here on earth," (ŚŚS 4.9.4). (The duties of the sacrificer during the *iṣṭis*).

When the after-offerings (*anuyāja*) have been performed, he moves the two offering-ladles (*srucau*) apart. With the ladle for Agni (*juhū*) held upward with his right hand, facing eastward, he says: "May I win the victory of Agni and Agni-Soma; by the impulse of strength (*vāja*), I push him forward. With the ladle for Agni-Soma (*upabhṛt*) held downward with his left hand, facing westward, he says: "May Agni, Agni-Soma, and [the other deities] drive away him who hates us and whom we hate; by the impulse of strength, I push him away. (ŚŚS 4.9) In other cases, it is according to the respective deity. (ŚŚS 4.9)
ŚŚS 4.9: When the master of the house has not yet performed his sacrifice, he offers oblations with the *sruva* ladle into the *gārhapatya* fire.

ŚŚS 4.10: "O you two of a hundred powers, that portion of strength which the gods ordained for you both—by this I gratify you; may you be satisfied by it! To Ahāha and Ahuhū, svāhā! To the Gandharvas Nārīṣṭa and Ahāha-Ahuhū, svāhā! (The Sacrificer’s Duties at the Iṣṭis)

O Agni, lord of the earth; O Vāyu, lord of the atmosphere; O Savitṛ, lord of instigations; O Sūrya, lord of the constellations; O Soma, lord of the plants; O Tvaṣṭṛ, lord of the forms of fuel-sticks; O Mitra, lord of the truthful; O Varuṇa, lord of the laws; O Indra, lord of the preeminent; O Prajāpati, lord of creatures—O gods, display your prowess among the gods! (The Sacrificer’s Address at the Iṣṭis)
"Exert yourselves in the first and second [pressings]!"—thus [he says], increasing by one up to eleven [verses]. (The *yājamāna* section for the *iṣṭi*s)

"O Viśvedevas, thirty-three in number, thrice eleven, whose paths lead ever upward, whose beings are ever superior, you who belong to all men, who are common to all, who possess universal greatness—protect me here! In this sacred formulation (brahman), in this power (kṣatra), in this rite, in this blessing, in this foundation, in this invocation of the gods—may this desire of mine be fulfilled, svāhā! Thus he says according to whatever desire he may have. (ŚŚS 4.10) "Prajāpati... is the fourth [invocation]. (ŚŚS 4.10)

"May the *dhruvā* [ladle] swell with the oblation of ghee, for each sacrifice offered to the gods. The udder of Sūryā, the lap of Aditi, the wide-streamed Earth—[may she be present] at this sacrifice. With these words, he causes the *dhruvā* to swell. (Yājamāna section, regarding the *iṣṭis*) He touches the *samiṣṭayajus* as it is being offered. (Yājamāna section, regarding the *iṣṭis*)

"May you be present in my assembly; you are everything, may you be everything for me; you are full, may you be full for me; you are imperishable, may you not perish for me, both there in yonder world and here. Having touched the full vessel with these words, he sprinkles water toward the quarters. (The Sacrificer’s Duties in the Iṣṭis)

"May the gods together with the eastern quarter purify [me]. May the months together with the southern quarter, and the ancestors, purify [me]. May the houses together with the eastern quarter, and the cattle, purify [me]. May the sacrifice together with the upward quarter, the year, and the lord of the sacrifice, purify [me]. (Thus at the sacrifices for the sacrificer. [He purifies] once each time with the mantra, twice each time silently. (Thus at the sacrifices for the sacrificer.)
Having touched [the water] with the three verses beginning with *āpo hi ṣṭha*, he pours it out toward the east or the north with the verse, *acchāyam vo yayor ojasā*.
Having consecrated it with the mantra: "I send you forth to the ocean; go to your own source. May our heroes be unharmed; let not our wealth be poured away. (ŚŚS 4.11, Yājamāna section of the Iṣṭis).

Having touched his chest with the four verses beginning with *śaṃ no devīr*, [he recites]: "O Indra, may we be united with you; may we be united with splendor, with milk, and with our bodies; may we be united with a gracious mind. May Tvaṣṭṛ, the giver of good gifts, bestow wealth upon us. With this, he touches his vital breaths (*prāṇas*). Then, saying "May he wipe away whatever is injured in our bodies," he wipes his face. He then strides the Viṣṇu-steps.
(ŚŚS 4.11) From the southern hip-region of the altar toward the Āhavanīya fire. (ŚŚS 4.12)

"In the sky Viṣṇu strode with the Jāgata metre; may I stride after him; excluded from that is he who hates us and whom we hate"—having lifted up the right foot while the left remains lower—(ŚŚS 4.12). "In the intermediate space Viṣṇu strode with the Triṣṭubh metre"—this is the second (stride)—(ŚŚS 4.12). "On the earth Viṣṇu strode with the Gāyatrī metre"—this is the third (stride)—(ŚŚS 4.12).

"Viṣṇu strode through the quarters with the Anuṣṭubh metre," [saying this] he strides transversely. (ŚŚS 4.12.5) The conclusion is the same. (ŚŚS 4.12.6) "We have gone to heaven," [saying this] he looks toward the east. (ŚŚS 4.12.7)
"May we be united with light," [he says] regarding the Āhavanīya fire.

(ŚŚS 4.12.8) "May I be united with offspring, may my offspring be united with me; may I be united with the increase of wealth, may the increase of wealth be united with me; the sacrifice is the Vasu; may I become more prosperous. [He says this] facing eastward. (ŚŚS 4.12.9)

"Thou art self-existent, the best ray; thou art the giver of life, give me life. Thou art the giver of splendor, give me splendor. Thou art the protector of the body, protect my body. From these quarters, from this heaven, from this atmosphere, from this food-eating world, from this foundation, I banish my hateful rival. May the hateful rival be banished,"—having thus worshipped the sun. (The portion for the sacrificer during the sacrifices).

"Turn according to the turning of Indra; turn following the turning of the Sun," saying this, he turns around toward the right arm. Having returned with his left side turned toward the Gārhapatya fire, he says: "O Agni, Lord of the House, may I be a master of the house together with you, O Agni, Lord of the House; may you be a good master of the house together with me, O Agni, Lord of the House. (10b) (The Sacrificer’s Duties at the Iṣṭis)

"May our household fires not be deficient; may there be a hundred winters for me from such-and-such [person]," having thus pronounced the names of his sons; "Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, unite me with desire," having touched a coal of his [fire]—(10c) [the Yājñika’s duties during the sacrifices].

Having murmured: "The sacrifice has come into being; it has come back; it was born; it has grown again. It became the overlord of the gods; may it make us overlords"—(10d) [the Yājñika’s duties during the sacrifices].

Having likewise sipped water (ācamana), he places a fuel-stick on the Āhavanīya fire with the formula: "O Agni, Lord of Vows, I have performed the vow; I have been able to do it; through it I have succeeded. Whatever I am, that I am. Then, having released his speech, [he recites]:

"O Agni, whoever hates us from afar, whoever hates us nearby—whether he be a kinsman or a stranger—may nothing of him remain, just as nothing remains of a log being consumed by fire. Having thus cast the embers of the Āhavanīya fire together [into the Gārhapatya], [the ritual concludes].
He mutters the triplet beginning with "O Agni, may I be rich in cattle" (RV 8.2.1–3).

Having worshipped the sun with the formulas, "We have risen," "That eye," "May I not be cut off from thy sight," and "What fervor is thine, may I not be deprived of that," he returns in the same manner, turns to the left, and sits down.

"May this oblation be productive for me—yielding ten heroic sons, with a complete retinue, for my well-being; may it grant me self, progeny, fearlessness, cattle, and the world. May Agni make my progeny abundant; bestow food, milk, and seed upon us. Thus [he recites] while consuming milk if he desires offspring. (ŚŚS 4.13) Or, if he desires to prosper, he consumes curds [with the mantra]: "I have performed the praise of Dadhikrāvan... (ŚŚS 4.13). (The *Yājamāna* section regarding the *iṣṭis*).
"May the lord of the sacrifice prosper with his blessing," [with these words] he eats the sacrificer’s portion. (Yājamānam īṣṭiṣu) 3.
He offers the *samiṣṭayajus* oblation together [with the other offerings] when departing on a journey. (Yājamānam īṣṭiṣu) 4.
The rites for one who is living. (Funeral rites of the *āhitāgni*) 1.

ŚŚS 4.14. If he should desire [to die] before the [funeral rites] are completed, there is no completion for him in the one-day (ekāha) sacrifices; [the rites end] with death. ŚŚS 4.14. Having cast all the oblations (havīṃṣi) into the Āhavanīya fire, ŚŚS 4.14.
[The officiants] should remove the hair and nails of the deceased.
Having bathed and adorned himself, (he proceeds). 5. (Regarding the funeral rites of one who maintained the sacred fires.
In the southern direction, on ground sloping toward the south, or sloping toward the southeast (or east), 6. (Regarding the funeral rites of one who maintained the sacred fires.
Having swept [the site] with a branch of the *palāśa* tree while reciting, "Depart, go away," 7. (Regarding the funeral rites of one who maintained the sacred fires.)
Having wiped [the ground] with the wooden sword (sphya) and sprinkled it with water;
having constructed the funeral pyre facing southeast;
having placed the Āhavanīya fire in the east, the Gārhapatya fire in the west, and the Dakṣiṇa fire in the south.
Having carried [the body] between the *gārhapatya* and the *dakṣiṇa-agni* fires, (11) having laid it face upwards upon the funeral pyre,
(12) and having pushed a cow or a red goat intended for the funeral rite toward the south with its head facing south, (13) [he proceeds].
14. Having extracted the two kidneys from a woman who is either still living or one who has been rendered unconscious, [he places them] behind [the corpse].
15. Having heated the kidneys over the *anvāhāryapacana* fire until they are lukewarm, he places them in her hands while reciting the two verses beginning with "ati drava.
16. Having placed pieces of gold upon the openings of the vital breaths (*prāṇa-āyatana*).
Having covered the mouth [of the deceased] with the omentum while reciting "The armor of Agni" (ŚŚS 4.14.17),
he places the *juhū* ladle in the right hand and the *upabhṛt* ladle in the left hand (ŚŚS 4.14.18–19).
He places the *dhruvā* ladle on the chest;
(20) the *agnihotrahavaṇī* ladle on the neck;
(21) and the two *sruva* spoons on the nostrils. (22) (The funeral rites for one who maintained the sacred fires.)
The *prāśitra* vessel is placed at the right ear;
(23) the pouring of the *praṇītā* water is at the left;
(24) the skull-bones are placed on the head. (25) (Funeral rites for one who maintained the sacred fires)
The pressing-stones [are placed] in the waters. (26) The vessel for the collected portions is in the belly. (27) The two bowls are on the two sides. (28) (Funeral rites of the *āhitāgni*)
The wooden sword (sphya) on the right side;
the black antelope skin on the left side;
the two kindling sticks (araṇī) in the lap.

The mortar and pestle [are placed] on the thighs and the two kneecaps. (ŚŚS 4.14.32) The winnowing basket and the cart [are placed] on the feet. (ŚŚS 4.14.33) The implements for the *agnihotra* [are placed] on the buttocks.

Having filled those [funeral vessels] with clarified butter and speckled ghee, [he says]: "Verily, this one is from you; you are from this one. This is your source; you are his source. O Jātavedas, carry him to that world where the doers of good deeds dwell. Verily, this one begot you; may he be born again from you, O so-and-so! Svāhā!"—with these words, they place [the fires] together with the funeral fires.
Having recited "Mā enam agne" ten times while the fire is blazing, they turn to the left, do not look back, and proceed toward the northeast.

(ŚŚS 4.15) He consecrates [the path] with two verses beginning with "mṛtyoḥ padam. (ŚŚS 4.15) They touch water while reciting the two hymns "āpo hi ṣṭhā" and "sanā ca soma," without bowing down, without immersing themselves [completely], and without running. (ŚŚS 4.15)

Having offered one handful of water with the formula, "O N.N., this is for you," having stepped out with the verse, "The waters [have carried away] us," having put on a new (unwashed) garment, and having worshipped the sun with the verse, "That eye [of Mitra]," they return, the youngest going first.

Having thrown dūrvā grass, barley, and mustard seeds into a water-vessel and placed it upon fresh cow-dung, they touch a stone that has been anointed with oil, the fire, and the water-vessel, with the verse, "The stone-bearing [river]."

Sleeping on the ground, eating sacrificial food (*haviṣya*), and the suspension of ritual acts—except for those pertaining to the sacred fires (*vaitāna*)—are the observances (*vrata*) to be maintained for one night, three nights, or nine nights until the collection of the bones (*saṃcayana*). Kauṣītaki said that they should not prolong the days of impurity (*agha-aha*).

In the dark fortnight, having collected [the bones] on odd-numbered nights, he should extinguish the bones with water mixed with milk while reciting the two verses beginning with *yam tvam agne*. Having placed the remains in an old jar, he should cover it with a clod of earth while reciting *ut te stabhnāmi*. Then, having buried it in a pit while reciting *ucchvancasva*, and having deposited it in a measured space while reciting *ucchvancamānā*, they bury it in the forest.
When the bodies are no longer visible, there are three hundred and sixty palāśa stalks. (ŚŚS 4.15) These constitute their place of insertion. (ŚŚS 4.15) Forty are placed on the head. (ŚŚS 4.15)
Ten [strokes] on the neck. (ŚŚS 4.15.12) One hundred [strokes] on the shoulders, the spine, and the arms. (ŚŚS 4.15.13) Thirty [strokes] on the chest. (ŚŚS 4.15.14)
In the belly, twenty [oblations]. (ŚŚS 4.15.15) In the two testicles, six. (ŚŚS 4.15.16) In the penis, four. (ŚŚS 4.15.17)
One hundred [bones] in the thighs;
(ŚŚS 4.15.18) thirty in the knees, shanks, and kneecaps;
(ŚŚS 4.15.19) twenty in the toes of the feet. (ŚŚS 4.15.20)

Thus, there are three hundred and sixty [bricks]. (ŚŚS 4.15) Having fashioned a human form, having wrapped it with woolen threads, having smeared it with barley flour, and having anointed it with clarified butter, they cremate it with the sacred fires. (ŚŚS 4.15) If he desires [to marry] another wife after his first wife has died before him, he should perform her funeral rites with the sacred fires—or with the *sāmtapana* fire—and then establish the fires again. (ŚŚS 4.15)
ŚŚS 4.16. Upon the completion of the vow, the rite of the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*) takes place.

ŚŚS 4.16. Having spread out the hide of a red bull, with its neck pointing north or east and the hair side up, behind the fire, they sit down upon it—or upon *kuśa* grass blades whose tips are likewise directed [toward the north or east]. 2. (Funeral rites of the *āhitāgni*)

Between the fire and these [objects], having placed a stone smeared with oil, and having made *śamyā* sticks as the enclosing-sticks (*paridhi*), he offers oblations with fuel of *śamī* wood or *palāśa* wood, using either a ladle (*sruva*) made of *vāraṇa* wood or one of bell-metal (*kāṃsya*). (ŚŚS 4.16) Having assumed the *upastha* posture while they have taken hold of him from behind. (ŚŚS 4.16)

"May death pass away from these living beings; may immortality come to me. May Vaivasvata grant us fearlessness. Like the leaf of a tree, may wealth fall upon us. May the Lord of Might attend us. And [he recites]: "The ten that are in the ruddy one, at the setting up of the fires.
(ŚŚS 4.16) Having offered twelve oblations, (ŚŚS 4.16).

ŚŚS 4.16: Having looked at the right shoulder with the two verses beginning "Just as the days," and having mixed collyrium with clarified butter, he anoints the eyes of the women with *kuśa* grass using the verse "Come, O women" (*ā nārīḥ*), once for each eye with the mantra, and twice for each silently.
ŚŚS 4.16: With the two verses beginning "Arise, O Brahmanaspati" (*uttiṣṭha brahmaṇaspate*), he addresses those who are rising while they hold onto the Brahmin's right arm.
Or [he may give] the tail of an ox.
(ŚŚS 4.16.8) An ox, a new garment, and a bronze vessel are the sacrificial fee.
(ŚŚS 4.16.9) With the hymn beginning, "Turn back with wealth from the right," the Pratyenas circumambulates [the corpse] three times from left to right. (ŚŚS 4.16.10)
ŚŚS 4.16: The ritual for the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*) is performed for the *pratyenas* (the deceased).

ŚŚS 4.17: One sacrifices a cow to Rudra for the sake of well-being. ŚŚS 4.17: This is called the *śūlagava* (the spit-ox sacrifice). ŚŚS 4.17: It is known as the *śūlagava*. ŚŚS 4.17: They call it the *śūlagava*. ŚŚS 4.17: It is designated as the *śūlagava*.
Having fasted during the bright fortnight under the Puṣya asterism, in the north-easterly direction,
(3) having churned the fire and carried it forward toward the east,
(4) and having fixed a Palāśa branch with its leaves in front, (5) [he proceeds]. (Śūlagava)
Having stationed the animal to the north of it:
(Śūlagava) "I dedicate you, acceptable to Rudra.
(Śūlagava) "I sprinkle you, acceptable to Rudra. (Śūlagava) 4.17–4.18.1.8.
"O Rudra, I bind you, who are dear to him," [he says].

(Śūlagava 4.17:9) They lead it, which has been circumambulated by fire, toward the north. (Śūlagava 4.17:10) They cause it to be slaughtered with its head to the east and feet to the north, or with its head to the west and feet to the north, while it is not crying out. (Śūlagava 4.17:11)

"Whatever cry the animal has uttered, or whatever it has struck with its feet against the chest—may Agni Jātavedas release me from that sin! Svāhā!"—with these words, he makes an offering while the animal is crying out.

(Śūlagava 4.17) Having extracted the omentum, washed it, cooked it over the eastern fire, sprinkled clarified butter over it, and removed it from the fire, he sprinkles water around the fire three times, saying "May it be auspicious, may it be auspicious," and offers oblations of clarified butter.
(Śūlagava 4.17) "She who does not go sideways, thinking 'I am the upholder'—her I yoke with a stream of clarified butter; may I prosper her! Svāhā! (Śūlagava 4.18)
"We invoke him to whom all this belongs; may he, the Lord of Desires, grant my desires—Svāhā! This is the second [offering].
(Śūlagava) "O Agni, Lord of the Earth! This is the third [offering]. (Śūlagava) "O Prajāpati! This is the fourth [offering]. (Śūlagava)

Having gathered three middle palāśa leaves, having spread them out as a base, and having placed the omentum upon them and sprinkled it with clarified butter, [he says]: "As many as I am lord over, as many as my attendants are—O God, I honor you for their sake; O God, protect us for their sake. (The Śūlagava sacrifice)

"I know your father, I know your mother; heaven is your father, earth is your mother. To that god Bhava, Śarva, Paśupati, Ugra, Deva, Mahādeva, Rudra, Īśāna, Aśani—svāhā! Having thus offered the omentum (*vapā*), he throws the *palāśa* leaves [into the fire].
(Śūlagava) He also throws the two omentum-roasting spits [into the fire].

(Śūlagava) Having offered the second oblation of clarified butter with the mantra, "To Darśa for thee, to Pratidarśa, svāhā!", he sprinkles water around the fire in the same manner as before. (Śūlagava)
To the west, he cooks the pot-offering (*sthālīpāka*) over the fire. (Śūlagava 4.18) To the north, the portions for sacrifice (*avadāna*) are placed.

(Śūlagava 4.18) Having combined the pot-offering, the broth, the meat, and the clarified butter, and having sprinkled water around [the fire] three times with the formula "For Śamyo, for Śamyo," he offers the oblation. (Śūlagava 4.18)

"To Bhava, svāhā! To Śarva, svāhā! To Rudra, svāhā! To Īśāna, svāhā! To Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, svāhā!"—thus [he offers]. (Śūlagava) Having sprinkled water around [the fire] in the same manner, having brought those [remnants] together, (Śūlagava) [he performs the offering]. (Śūlagava) 4.19.3.
In the fire at the western [side]. (Śūlagava) "To Bhavānī, svāhā! To Śarvāṇī, svāhā! To Rudrāṇī, svāhā! To Īśānānī, svāhā! To Agnāyī, svāhā!
(Śūlagava) The sprinkling around [the fire] is the same. (Śūlagava)
Having placed Palāśa leaves toward the east and north from the place of cutting, and having deposited the entrails mixed with blood upon them, he assigns [the offering] to the armies of Rudra:
(7) “The sounding ones, the echoing ones, the clamorous ones, the scavenging ones, the snorting ones, the flesh-eaters—this is your portion; enjoy it, svāhā! (8) Thus [he speaks].
The sacrificer also pays homage [to the offering]. (9) (Regarding the *śūlagava* sacrifice.)

O Lord of the earth, Lord of the world, Lord of the universe, Lord of beings, Lord of all creatures, Lord of the Great Being! Harm us not, nor our bipeds and quadrupeds; harm neither our bipeds nor our quadrupeds. He who hates us and whom we hate—O Durāpūra (the one difficult to fill), you are the shadow of the good through your high-mindedness (or pride). (Śūlagava)

"Your bow is the heart, your mind the arrows, and your gaze the discharge; I know you thus—homage be unto you! O Soma, may he protect you; do not harm me. To the two who are lords in the forest, like wolves snapping at their prey—to Bhava and Śarva, the sons of Mahādeva, homage!
(Śūlagava) "The hymns *kad rudrāya*, *imā rudrāya*, *te pitar imā rudrāya*, and *sthiradhanvana* [are recited]. (Śūlagava) "A choice gift is the sacrificial fee. (Śūlagava)
The rites of *upākaraṇa* (dedication), *prokṣaṇa* (sprinkling), and *paryagnikaraṇa* (circumambulation with fire) follow the procedure of the animal sacrifice (*paśubandha*).

A branch of the *palāśa* tree [is used] for the deity [to whom the offering is made]. For other animals, there is the omentum (*vapā*) for the deity, the sacrificial oblation (*havis*) for the deity, and [the portion] for Sviṣṭakṛt. The two portions of clarified butter (*ājyabhāga*) belong to Agni and Soma. There is the omentum for the deity, the oblation for the deity, [the portion] for Sviṣṭakṛt, and an oblation of clarified butter for Anumati. And there are the cooked messes of grain (*sthālīpāka*).

21.21. Six persons are worthy of the *arghya* offering: the teacher (*ācārya*), the officiating priest (*ṛtvij*), the father-in-law (*śvaśura*), the king (*rājā*), one who has completed his Vedic studies (*snātaka*), and a dear friend (*priya*). 21.22. Facing north or east, he sits upon or steps over a grass-bundle (*kūrca*) with the mantra: "I, the height among those equal to me, like the sun among lightnings, step upon this [bundle]—upon him who seeks to harm us. 21.23. Having accepted the water for the feet (*pādya*) with the formula: "Thou art the milking of Virāj; may I obtain the milking of Virāj; may the milking of Virāj be in my feet," he accepts it.
When told, "The *arghya*," he receives the water. (4) When told, "The *ācamanīya*," having sipped water with each of the three verses beginning with *āpo hi ṣṭha*, one by one;
(5) when told, "The *madhuparka*," having looked at it, he consumes it just as he would the *prāśitra*. (6) (Section on the *arghya*)
He accepts it in this manner; the modification is: "For glory and for Vedic splendor.

(The Arghya) Having accepted it and placed it in his left hand, he takes a portion from the eastern half with his thumb and ring finger and smears it on the eastern half of the bronze vessel [with the formula]: "May the Vasus, whose king is Agni, consume thee. (The Arghya) With the formula:
"May the Pitṛs, whose king is Yama, consume thee," he [smears it] from the southern half onto the southern half. (The Arghya)
"May the Ādityas, with Varuṇa as their king, consume you"—with this [formula], he [takes] from the western half of the middle portion.

(Ārghya 10) "May the Rudras, with Indra as their king, consume you"—with this [formula], he [takes] from the northern half of the middle portion. (Ārghya 11) "May the Viśve Devas, with Prajāpati as their king, consume you"—with this [formula], he [takes] from above the middle portion. (Ārghya 12)
With the mantra, he should eat once each time; silently, twice each time.
(Ārghya 13) Having eaten with each of the three Mahāvyāhṛtis one by one, he should consume the fourth portion without water. (Ārghya 14–15)
16. Giving the remains of food to a Brāhmaṇa [is an act of hospitality]. 17. Or giving all the drink [is an act of hospitality].
18. Or pouring water into his hands [is an act of hospitality].
Having touched his chest with the four verses beginning with *śaṃ no devīr*,
(19) [the guest performs] the same touching of the vital breaths (*prāṇa-sammarśana*) and the wiping of the mouth. (20–21) (The Arghya ceremony.)
22. [The cow] remains silent until it has been led away. 23. When it is said, "O cow," he should respond, "Om.
24. Having murmured, "She is the mother of the Rudras," he should say, "Release her; let her eat grass."

He should announce: "A seat of grass (*kūrca*), water for the feet (*pādya*), the guest-offering (*arghya*), water for sipping (*ācamanīya*), the honey-mixture (*madhuparka*), and a cow. He should announce [this] repeatedly. (ŚŚS 4.21) One who intends to perform the Soma sacrifice chooses as officiating priests (*ṛtvij*) those who belong to a lineage of seers (*ārṣeya*), who are young, and who are learned in the Vedas (*anūcāna*). (ŚŚS 5.1) [He chooses] either four or all [of them]. (ŚŚS 5.1)
"The moon is my divine Brahman; you are the human one"—this he says in a whisper. "Thus for all.
"The sun is my divine Udgātṛ; you are the human one."

"Agni is my divine *hotṛ*; you are my human [hotṛ]. (Soma: Invitation of Priests & Sacrifice to the Gods) "Vāyu is my divine *adhvaryu*; you are my human [adhvaryu]. (Soma: Invitation of Priests & Sacrifice to the Gods) "Prajāpati is my divine *sadasya*; you are my human [sadasya]. (Soma: Invitation of Priests & Sacrifice to the Gods)
The seasons are my divine officiating priests; you, O men, are the human reciters of the *hotṛ* offices. 9. (Soma: Invitation; Selection of Priests & Sacrifice to the Gods)

"Speak for me the *bhargas*; speak for me the *bhadra*; speak for me prosperity; speak for me glory; speak for me fame. Having been chosen, he should mutter this, and then, having asked, "Are you not one who has performed a *ahīna* sacrifice, nor one for whom the office of priest was relinquished, nor one to whom the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) has already been led?"—if he accepts [the office], he should respond accordingly, or else he may decline it. 10. (Soma: Āṣ: Choosing the Priest & Devayajana)

The sacrificial ground for the gods (*devayajana*) should slope toward the east. (ŚŚS 5.2.1) For one who desires the sacrifice, it should slope toward the northeast. (ŚŚS 5.2.2) Where, while reciting the formulas, the Hotṛ can see the Āhavanīya fire, the sun, and water—that is the place for one who desires spiritual luster (*brahmavarcasa*). (ŚŚS 5.2.3)
In the bright fortnight, under an auspicious lunar mansion, there shall be initiation and the conclusion [of the rite].
(ŚŚS 5.2) In the afternoon, the *dīkṣaṇīyā* sacrifice is offered to Agni and Viṣṇu.
(ŚŚS 5.3) It is a modification of the Full Moon sacrifice (*paurṇamāsī*). (ŚŚS 5.3)
There are fifteen *sāmidhenī* verses. (Soma: Āśv.
Dīkṣaṇīyā-iṣṭi) The oblation is performed in a low voice (*upāṃśu*). (Soma: Āśv.
Dīkṣaṇīyā-iṣṭi) The two *virāj* verses are used for the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering. (Soma: Āśv. Dīkṣaṇīyā-iṣṭi)

[ŚŚS 5.3] Or [the formula may be recited] constantly. (Soma: Ātithyeṣṭi and Dīkṣaṇīyeṣṭi) "May this sacrificer be invited; may I attain the conclusion of the invocation of this sacrifice"—thus he prays. "May this sacrificer pray: 'May I attain the conclusion of the invocation of this sacrifice'"; [this is the rule] regarding the place of blessings and in the *sūktavāka*, prior to the offering of the rice-cakes belonging to the third pressing.
In the *sūktavāka*, he does not utter the name of the sacrificer prior to the *savanīya* [cakes]. (Soma: Ātithyeṣṭi and Dīkṣaṇīyeṣṭi)
And [the *dīkṣaṇīyā* sacrifice] ends with the *patnīsaṃyāja* offerings.

(ŚŚS 5.3) The Adhvaryu, having taken hold of the sacrificer from behind while he offers the *udagrabhaṇa* oblations, [makes him recite]: "May my mind be consecrated by the mind; may my speech be consecrated by speech; may my breath be consecrated by breath; may my sight be consecrated by sight; may my hearing be consecrated by hearing.
(ŚŚS 5.4) Or he should offer the oblations [himself]. (ŚŚS 5.4)
And there is a single initiation for both [fires].
(ŚŚS 5.4) "I approach the initiation of the mind," he says, [touching] the Āhavanīya fire. (ŚŚS 5.4) "I approach the initiation of speech," he says, [touching] the Gārhapatya fire. (ŚŚS 5.4)
"Prāṇa, I enter upon the consecration (dīkṣā)," [with these words] he approaches the Dakṣiṇāgni. (ŚŚS 5.4.6) The consecrations are unlimited; at their conclusion, there is the Prāyaṇīyā sacrifice.
(ŚŚS 5.4.7) [He offers] to Pathyā Svasti, Agni, Soma, and Savitṛ with clarified butter, and to Aditi with a caru-oblation. (ŚŚS 5.5.1)

"May there be well-being for us on our paths; may there indeed be well-being. "O Agni, lead us; O Agni, do you ferry us across. "O Soma, you are wise; [worship] those stations of yours with oblation. "That most excellent [glory] of Savitṛ... "He who [created] all these beings... "The great, good protectress... (Soma:
Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, Prāyaṇīyā-iṣṭi). There are fifteen *sāmidhenī* verses.
The oblation is performed in a low voice (*upāṃśu*).
The two *ājyabhāga* offerings do not take place. (Soma:
Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 5.5) The *sviṣṭakṛt* offering is performed with the verses: "O most glorious one" (*tvām citraśravastama*) and "That which is most carrying" (*yad vāhiṣṭham*).
(Soma: Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 5.5) And it concludes with the *śamyu* formula. (Soma: Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 5.5)

Having purchased the King (Soma) and placed him on a cart, [the Adhvaryu] is addressed with the formula: "For Soma being carried around. (ŚŚS 5.6) Standing between the two tracks, he recites: "Go from good to better; let Bṛhaspati be your forerunner. Then, choosing the best place upon the earth, drive the enemies far away, you who possess all heroes. (ŚŚS 5.6)

While following [the cart], he recites the four verses beginning with *imāṃ dhiyaṃ śikṣamāṇasya* and *vaneṣu vyantarikṣaṃ soma yāsi*. He should follow between the two tracks. Having stopped the cart in front of the hall, they cause the King (Soma) to descend.
He should follow by whichever way they go.
Having entered with the verse, "Those abodes of thine which [are reached] by oblation" (RV 1.91.19),
standing to the south in front of the Āhavanīya fire, he concludes with the verse, "The god has come" (RV 10.172.1).
Having touched water, he releases his vow.

From this point forward, until the carrying forth (*praṇayana*) of the *Āgnīṣoma* [fires], the purpose of water is served by the *madantī* waters. (ŚŚS 5.6.9) The *Ātithyā* sacrifice is dedicated to Viṣṇu.
(ŚŚS 5.7.1) It is a modification (*vikāra*) of the Full Moon sacrifice (*Paurṇamāsī*). (ŚŚS 5.7.2)
"Viṣṇor nu kam," "pra tad viṣṇuḥ"—these two [verses] are for the churning of the fire (agnimanthana).

(ŚŚS 5.7) "Hotāram citraratham," "yas tvā svāśvaḥ"—these two are for the Sviṣṭakṛt offering. (ŚŚS 5.7) And the verses for the churning of the fire are recited when the oblation has been placed near [the fire]. (ŚŚS 5.7)
5.7. The oblation is performed in a low voice.
5.7. [The mantras] end with the word *īḍā*.
5.8. Having touched water, all [the priests] [perform the *tanūnaptra* rite].

"Unassailable art thou, unassailable; the vigor of the gods, a protector from imprecation, not to be imprecated. May I directly attain truth; place me in prosperity. Having thus touched the *tānūnaptra*—the clarified butter belonging to the *dhruva* vessel, containing gold, placed in a bowl and set upon the sacrificial grass—they touch it together.
(ŚŚS 5.8) Having touched [water] and having gone around the front of the *āhavanīya* fire while touching the stalks (*aṃśu*), they cause the King [Soma] to swell. (ŚŚS 5.8)

"O divine Soma, may each drop of thine swell for Indra, the winner of the single prize; may Indra swell for thee, and mayest thou swell for Indra. Make us, thy friends, swell with gain and wisdom; may it be well with thee! O divine Soma, may I attain the completion of the pressing. (Soma: Āpyāyana, Tanūnaptra)

"May that ray which the Ādityas cause to swell, which the imperishable ones drink as their own abode—by that may King Varuṇa, Bṛhaspati, and the guardians of the world cause us to swell. Having touched his chest with this [verse], (Śrauta Sūtra 5.8), and having sipped water, he places his right hands, palms upward, upon the sacrificial grass (prastara); in the afternoon, he conceals them with the left hands, palms upward, [reciting]: "Desired riches for the impulse toward fortune; to the speakers of Truth, to Truth; homage to Heaven and Earth! (Śrauta Sūtra 5.8). (Soma: Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, Tanūnaptra).
From the *āpyāyana* rite until the *upasada*, once the *upasada* has been completed. (ŚS 5.8) The first sacrifice is without the *pravargya*.
(ŚS 5.9) There is an option for one who is learned in the Vedas (*śrotriya*). (ŚS 5.9)

To the north of the *gārhapatya* fire. (Soma: Āṣ: Āpavargya & Upasads) While the *mahāvīra* vessels are being set down, [the Adhvaryu] enters the hall by the eastern door. Having gone to the north of the *āhavanīya* fire, he passes between the two *khara* mounds and the vessels, and sits down behind them. Being addressed with the words, "O Hotṛ, recite the *abhiṣṭava*," he recites each verse without pausing, accompanied by the *praṇava*. (Soma: Āṣ: Āpavargya & Upasads)

Brahman was born first in the east; from the boundary, Vena brought forth the radiant ones. His foundations, his highest stations, and the source of both the existent and the non-existent, he has disclosed.
This royal power goes before the Father for the sake of the first-born; she is the leader of the earth. For him they prepare this radiant, well-impelled Gharma, the first draught.

"Towards that god Savitṛ, the source of protection, whose wisdom is inspired by the seers, I sing praise—him of true impulsion, the bestower of jewels; towards the beloved sage, the thought. At his impelling, his lofty light shone forth; the golden-handed one of good skill has measured out the heaven with his form, which is a source of well-being. (ŚŚS 5.9) "When the [Soma] is being anointed in the cavity, [he recites] 'They anoint him'.
(ŚŚS 5.9) "When it is being set down, [he recites] 'Sit down together'. (ŚŚS 5.9)

"O Agni, be well-disposed toward us in our austerities; O Agni, he who is our kinsman..."—these [verses] are recited while the embers are being pushed together. (ŚŚS 5.9.10) "Prepare your vigor..."—these five [verses].
(ŚŚS 5.9.11) "O lover of songs, [be] around us... and "upon the two [stones]... (ŚŚS 5.9.12)
"O Worthy One, you bear the bright [Soma]" (RV 9.83.1). (Soma: Āṣ;
Āpavargya & Upasads) "The winged one, smeared on the jaws, of the drop..."—these two hymns. (Soma: Āṣ;
Āpavargya & Upasads) "Purifying is your [filter]..."—these two verses. (Soma: Āṣ; Āpavargya & Upasads)
When the *dhiṣaṇās* wove the purifying [filter] while bearing the glowing *gharma* at the *praṇavas*, the Āyus perceived within the ocean the far-seeing name of Sūrya three times a day.
(16) Having extracted the hymn "This Vena... and the verse "The eagle on the firmament...
(17), [one recites] the hymn "Thee, the Lord of the hosts... (18).
"Bṛhad vadema vidathe suvīrāḥ"—one desiring a hero should meditate upon a hero [with this verse].
(ŚŚS 5.9/19) "Kā rādhat..."—nine [verses]. (ŚŚS 5.9/20) "Ā no viśvābhir ūtibhiḥ"—three [verses]. (ŚŚS 5.9/21)
"In the forenoon, the hymn 'prātar yāvāṇaḥ' [is recited];
in the afternoon, 'ā bhāti' [is recited].
Having suspended all speech pertaining to heaven, [he remains silent]. (ŚŚS 5.9.22–24)
Having set aside the final verse, when it is said, "The Gharma has shone forth according to one's desire," he recites the hymn, "It has indeed shone forth" (arūrucat).

Having performed the concluding rite with the final verse, having touched water and stood up, he worships the Mahāvīra vessel with the Anuvāka for the openings, and having touched water again, he sits down.
"Upahvaya" (Summon! when the cow is being called;
"Him kṛṇvati" (She makes the sound *him*) as she approaches;
"Abhi tvā deva savitaḥ" (O God Savitṛ, toward you... as she is being addressed.
When [the calf] is being brought near, [he recites]: "Like a cow with her calf, like a calf with its mother" (ŚS 5.10).
When the calf is touching the udder, [he recites]: "That breast of thine... (ŚS 5.10).
When [the milk] is being drawn out, [he recites]: "The cow has lowed" (ŚS 5.10).
“With reverence, sit down; being in agreement, sit down,” [the Adhvaryu] says as they sit down.

(ŚŚS 5.10) “They milk the cow with a milking-vessel, with seventeen [verses] containing the word *ātman*. ‘The fire is kindled, O Aśvins; the Gharma is heated for you; come hither! The cows are milked here, the milch-kine; O wonder-workers, the singers rejoice. ‘That indeed is most manifest’—[he recites this] while the cow is being milked. (ŚŚS 5.10)
"Adhukṣat uttiṣṭha brahmaṇaspate"—with these words he rises.

(ŚŚS 5.10) "Upadrava payasā godhukaḥ su mā gharmaṃ siñca paya usriyāyāḥ / vi nākam akhyat savitā damūnā anu dyāvāpṛthivī supraṇīte //"—with these words [he recites] while the two milks are being brought forward.
(ŚŚS 5.10) "Ā sute siñcata śriyam ā nūnam aśvinoḥ ṛṣiḥ"—with these words [he recites] while the two [milks] are being poured. (ŚŚS 5.10)
When [the vessel] is being lifted up, [he recites]: "Up has risen this god Savitṛ with his golden [hands]" (RV 7.45.1).
(12) In the event of a reversal of the ritual actions, [one should proceed] according to the respective action.
(13) When they are departing, [he recites]: "May Brahmanaspati go forth" (RV 1.40.3). (14)
Having recited "In the vault of heaven, the fair-winged bird... while moving along, (15);
having sat down upon the Hotṛ’s seat, (16);
and being addressed with the call, "Recite the offering prayer for the Gharma," (17).

"Drink both! The heated *gharma* approaches you; your own *hotṛ* priest attends. The *adhvaryu*, bearing the sacrificial food, moves forward for you. O Aśvins, partake of the stream of the sweet milk that has been milked; drink of the milk of the cow! Having uttered *vaṣaṭ* with these two verses together, [he offers]. (ŚŚS 5.10) "O Agni, enjoy the *gharma*!"—thus he utters the *anuvaṣaṭ* call in the forenoon.
(ŚŚS 5.10) Now, in the afternoon: (ŚŚS 5.10)

"Drink of this! That which is offered in the cows—clarified butter and milk—this is your portion, O Aśvins; come hither! O lovers of sweetness, upholders of the assembly, lords of the virtuous, drink the heated *gharma* in the radiant realm of heaven! Having uttered *vaṣaṭ* with these two verses taken together, (21) likewise, having uttered the secondary *vaṣaṭ*, (22). (Soma: Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra: Pravargya and Upasad rites)

"Oblation made with *svāhā*, pure among the gods, is the Gharma which is the cup of the Aśvins, the drinking-vessel of the gods. All the immortals, rejoicing, lick it as they draw it back from the Gandharva. Having thus praised it, [he recites] "O friend, [protect] the friend," as he approaches. [He recites] "The Gandharva is here," as it is being set down.
He will recite the *pragāthika* verse beginning with "tam gha itthā" (ŚS 5.10.26).
Before the offering, he recites "haviḥ haviṣmān" (ŚS 5.10.27).
The *hotṛ*’s portion is consumed as a breath-sacrifice (*prāṇabhakṣa*).
[The Pravargya] is directly perceived by the sacrificer.
(29) [It is also performed] with the *dadhigharma*.

(30) "O God Gharma, may we partake of your oblation that has been offered—the great oblation, honeyed, full of vigor, and full of nourishment, in the most Indra-like fire"—this is the mantra for the consumption. (31)

While the great-hero vessels (*mahāvīra*) are being heated: "Upon which the seven Vasus mount as ancient mounts; for he is the Ṛṣi of most far-reaching fame, the guest of Indra’s roar"—having thus praised [them], (32) (Soma: Āśv.; Pravargya & Upasad). Having concluded with "From good pasture...
(Sūyavasa-), (33) (Soma: Āśv.; Pravargya & Upasad), and having touched [water], they are released. (34) (Soma: Āśv.; Pravargya & Upasad)
On the day of the Soma-pressing, the *pravargya* rite is performed either at the *āgnīdhrīya* fire-altar, after the *bahiṣpavamāna* stotra has been chanted, or during the midday pressing.
Having concluded the *pravargya* rite, they perform the *upasad* rites by placing [the offering] upon the sacrificial grass (*prastara*).
For the first *upasad* on the preceding day, he recites three *sāmidhenī* verses without pausing; each verse is recited three times with the *praṇava* (the syllable *oṃ*) at the end.

"In this manner, O Agni, [I offer] this fuel-stick for me"—with these three verses, he performs the rite in the afternoon. (ŚŚS 5.11.2) Joining the latter verse with the third word of the former, he concludes.
(ŚŚS 5.11.3) Having joined [the verses] with the *praṇava* (*oṃ*), [he recites]: "Bring Agni; bring Soma; bring Viṣṇu. (ŚŚS 5.11.4)
Having caused the two *sruva*-ladles to be taken up by means of the *sruc-ādāpana* formula, he sacrifices in a low voice (*upāṃśu*).

"O Agni, you who are like a fierce one, [slay] the Vṛtras. "O Soma, you who are invincible in battles through your mental powers (*kratubhiḥ*). "The singers praise him who belongs to the ancient [time]. (RV 8.4.1; 9.61.22; 1.30.11)

One should perform [the rites] as prescribed. (8) (Soma: Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, Pravargya & Upasads) On the afternoon [of the second day], there is a reversal of the *yājyā* and *puronuvākyā* verses. (9) (Soma: Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, Pravargya & Upasads) On the second day, in the forenoon, there are three *sāmidhenī* verses beginning with "This fuel for me, O Agni" (*imām me agne samidham*). (10) (Soma: Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, Pravargya & Upasads)
"In the afternoon, [the mantra] is 'To him who is to be approached' (upasadyāya).
(ŚŚS 5.11.11) "As in the first [day], so in the third. (ŚŚS 5.11.12) "But their own specific times should be extended. (ŚŚS 5.11.13)
Or rather, there is a reversal day by day.
(14) On the Upavasatha day, having completed both ritual sequences in the morning.
(15) The carrying forward of the fire (*agnipraṇayana*) takes place when the *Pravargya* rite is not performed. (1) ŚŚS 5.11–12.1.
5.12. In the rite accompanied by the *pravargya*, there is the removal of the *mahāvīra* vessel.
2. Therein, the *prastotṛ* sings the *sāman*. 3. Therein, the *hotṛ* employs the *nidhana* chant. 4. (Śrautasūtra: Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, Pravargya and Upasads)

The carrying forward of the fire (*agnipraṇayana*) has been explained. (ŚŚS 5.12) Summoned for the purpose of moving the two *havirdhāna* carts, he stands between the northern track of the southern *havirdhāna* cart and the southern track of the northern one; thus addressed, [he stands] while the two *havirdhāna* carts are being moved forward. (ŚŚS 5.13)

"O slayer of Vṛtra, may the danger from one's own kin and that from others depart; the wheels have turned away. Having recited this with his right forefoot, he pushes aside the tuft of hair on the west side.
(ŚŚS 5.13) Standing, he recites after [the verse]: "May they go forth for the sacrifice.

(ŚŚS 5.13) Leaning upon the northern track of the southern [chariot] while walking along it, he recites: "O Heaven and Earth, protect this [sacrifice] for us; of these two, let there be a place rich in ghee; like Yama and Yamī... (ŚŚS 5.13)
“*Adhi dvayoḥ*” (upon the two)—this [is recited] when the covering is being placed on them.
“*Viśvā rūpāṇi prati*” (toward all forms)—this [is recited] when they are being encircled. “*Ā vām upastham*” (into your lap)—this [is recited] when they are situated on the navel.

In the case of a reversal of ritual action, it is according to the action [performed]. (ŚŚS 5.13) Having performed the concluding verse, "Around thee, O lover of songs," (ŚŚS 5.13) he releases [the vow] while standing at the very spot where he stood when he first recited the [first] verse. (ŚŚS 5.13)

In measured sacrificial halls, they lead forward Agni and Soma. From that point until the conclusion of the Anubandhyā sacrifice, the space between the Cātvāla pit and the Utkara mound is the *tīrtha*. Having entered by way of it, [one performs the rites].
Having gone to the north of the Āgnīdhrīya hearth and the Sadas;
