"Arise!"; "To my call! (Soma: Āśir;
Morning Litany) Now follows the section in the *anuṣṭubh* meter. (Soma: Āśir; Morning Litany)
"Come to us with all your aids; whatever you two stand today in the far distance"—these are the two hymns [of the *Ṛgveda*].
(Soma: Āśir; Morning Litany) Now follows that which is in the *Triṣṭubh* meter.

(Soma: Āśir; Morning Litany) "The light shines forth"—this is the hymn. "To the Nāsatyas," these three [verses]. "O Vasus and Rudras," these three [verses]. "Your realms," this is the hymn. (Soma: Āśir; Morning Litany)
*Grāvāṇa iva*, *Dhenur pratnasya*, the hymn *Ka u śravat*, and the hymn *Stuṣe naraḥ*—excluding the five-footed verse—and the five hymns beginning with *Ā vām ratho rodasī badbadhānaḥ*.

(Soma: Āśvin Śastra; Prātar-anuvāka) Now follows the Bārhata [Śastra]. (Soma: Āśvin Śastra; Prātar-anuvāka) *Imā u vām diviṣṭayaḥ*, *Ayaṃ vām madhumattamaḥ*—the first, third, and fifth [verses] of these. (Soma: Āśvin Śastra; Prātar-anuvāka)
Now follows the *auṣṇiha* [metre]:
"yuvor u ṣu ratham" and so forth, five verses.
Now follows the *jāgata* [metre].
"Triścin no adya," "Īḷe dyāvīyam," and "Ghoṣāṃ ca saputrām. (Soma: Āśva; Prātar-anuvāka) Then follows the *pāṅkta* [section]: "Prati priyatamam. (Soma: Āśva; Prātar-anuvāka)

Having clothed himself with the *uttama* (final) [verse] and having released his speech, he recites the *chandas* (metres) one after another, as well as the *pratipad*, the *samārohaṇīyas*, and three hundred and sixty verses of this *samāmnāya*. (17) Or, beyond a hundred verses, he may proceed according to his desire.
(18) He should not omit the *pāṅkta* (fivefold) verses. (19)
"The time for the enclosing [of the fires] is when they shall offer the *upāṃśu* [libation] before sunrise.

(ŚŚS 6.6.20) "Or rather, the restraint of speech [begins] from the *āntaryāma* [libation]. (ŚŚS 6.6.21) "Having been addressed with 'O Hotṛ, impel [the waters],' he [recites] starting from 'pra devatrā,' omitting the twelfth [verse]. (ŚŚS 6.7.1) [Regarding the *āponaputrīyā* verses]
When the eleventh verse of the *anūcya* has been recited and the oblation is being poured into the waters; (Soma: Āṣ: Āponaputrīyā).
When they have turned back toward those waters, [he offers] the tenth [verse]; (Soma: Āṣ: Āponaputrīyā).
When the waters are visible, [he recites] the verse beginning with "prati yad āpaḥ. (Soma: Āṣ: Āponaputrīyā).
"Come together, O friends," [he recites] when they are coming together. (Soma Āśir:

Āponaptrīya) "O divine waters," [he recites] while the water is being poured into the Hotṛ’s cup. (Soma Āśir: Āponaptrīya) "Like milch-cows," [he recites] as they are approaching; having uttered the entire verse, he pauses with the *praṇava*. (Soma Āśir: Āponaptrīya)

"O Adhvaryu, have you sought the waters?"—with these words he asks the Adhvaryu. (ŚS 6.7.8) "Indeed, they have bowed down"—thus he replies. (ŚS 6.7.9) Being thus addressed, [the Adhvaryu] recites the *nigada* over those waters:

"O Adhvaryu, pour out the Soma for Indra—full of vigor, full of greatness, thirst-quenching, accompanied by the Vasus, the Rudras, the Ādityas, the Ṛbhus, the Vibhus, the Vājins, Bṛhaspati, and all the gods. (ŚS 6.7.10a)

"Having drunk of which Indra, intoxicated, struck down the Vṛtras—may he carry us across those [enemies] belonging to the people. Having recited the verse beginning with "O Waters" (*ambayaḥ*) consisting of one and a half verses, having stood up and turned toward the Adhvaryu, having recited the subsequent verse and a half, and having recited the penultimate verse of the hymn, and having concluded with the final verse, he turns around and sits down.
(ŚŚS 6.7) "Protect my breath; enliven my breath; *svāhā*! To thee, O auspicious one, for Sūrya!"—with these words, he breathes out after the *upāṃśu* cup as it is being offered. (ŚŚS 6.8)
"Protect my out-breath; quicken my out-breath. *Svāhā*! To thee, O auspicious one, for Sūrya!"—with these words he follows the Antaryāma cup.
(ŚŚS 6.8) The Brahman and the Maitrāvaruṇa sit down to the south. (ŚŚS 6.8) When addressed with "O Brahman, we shall chant the stotra; O Praśāstṛ [give the directions]," they respond. (ŚŚS 6.8)
Having murmured, "O long-lived ones, do not depart from the Ṛg-verses; protect our bodies; chant the Sāman-hymns at the impulse of the god Savitṛ," [he says], "Om!

Chant! (ŚŚS 6.8). Having murmured, "O long-lived ones, do not depart from the Ṛg-verses; protect our bodies; chant the Sāman-hymns at the impulse of the god Savitṛ," [he says], "Om! Chant! (ŚŚS 6.8). "Om! Chant! (ŚŚS 6.8).
The *prasava* (impulse) belongs to all the *stotras*.

"Lead me from non-existence to existence; lead me from darkness to light; lead me from the finite to the infinite; lead me from death to immortality"—thus the sacrificer speaks when about to approach the *pavamāna* chants. (ŚŚS 6.8)

“Thou art a falcon, winged, having the Gāyatrī metre; I take hold of thee; carry me safely across to the completion of this sacrifice, O *ṛc*!”—this [formula] is recited when the *bahiṣpavamāna* has been chanted. (ŚŚS 6.8.10) “Thou art a well-winged bird, winged, having the Triṣṭubh metre”—this [formula] is used at the midday [pressing]. (ŚŚS 6.8.11) “Thou art a friend, winged, having the Jagatī metre”—this [formula] is used at the third pressing (*ārbhava*). (ŚŚS 6.8.12)
The conclusion is the same. (Soma: Āśir; Upāṃśu and Antaryāma cups; the secret formula.

"Invited are the gods to the portion of this Soma, the purifying, the far-seeing. May the gods invite me to the portion of this Soma, the purifying, the far-seeing. With the mind I consume you; with speech I consume you; with breath I consume you; with sight I consume you; with hearing I consume you. Thus [recites] the Hotṛ when the Bahiṣpavamāna has been chanted. (Soma: Āśir; Upāṃśu and Antaryāma cups; the secret formula.)
The Savanīya animal sacrifice belongs to Agni;
or it may belong to Indra and Agni;
or it may consist of the set of eleven animals.
In the case of the sets of eleven animals tied to single posts, the verse used for the girding of the ropes is repeated three times each, because the ropes are distinct.
(ŚŚS 6.9) Between the eleventh [post] and the girding verse, he recites the *pragātha* "yān vo naraḥ" and the remainder of the hymn.
(ŚŚS 6.9) With the final [verse], he consecrates the animal lying nearby (*upaśaya*). (ŚŚS 6.9)

If the [stakes] were raised on the previous day but have not yet been bound around, one should perform the binding with the first verse. (ŚS 6.9) Or, for the sake of continuity, one may wait until the half-verse alone is reached.
(ŚS 6.9) One should join together those of the same kind. (ŚS 6.9)
As for the best [animal], so it is by modification (ūha).

(ŚS 6.9) Having invoked the deity of the animal and Vanaspati, [he says]: "Bring Indra accompanied by the Vasus; bring Indra accompanied by the Rudras; bring Indra accompanied by the Ādityas, the Ṛbhus, the Vibhus, the Vājins, Bṛhaspati, and the Viśve Devas"—thus [are invoked] the deities of the pressing. (ŚS 6.9)

They do not go to other places of recitation (nigama-sthāna). Or [they may do so] during the *sūktavāka*. Having touched one another, the two Adhvaryus offer the two *pravṛtāhuti* oblations in the sequence of their respective *pravara* lineages.

"May I be beloved by speech; O Lord of Speech, may I be beloved. That which is your divine speech, the sweetest of all speech—grant us that today, Svāhā! To Sarasvatī. With this, he offers the first oblation. (ŚŚS 6.9.17) The second [oblation] is performed silently.

(ŚŚS 6.9.18) "For Agni," "Lead us," "Thou art the lord of the sacrifice," "Forth for the bright one," and "O poets"—with these verses, he offers the oblations for the animal dedicated to Agni. (ŚŚS 6.10.1)

"From the great heaven, from the mountain, [we invoke] Sarasvatī, seeking the gods; O Sarasvatī, may the daughter Pāvīravī come toward us with her flood, these [oblations] being offered"—this is for the animal sacrifice to Sarasvatī.

"O Soma, you are the observer; you [know] these plants; Soma [is the milk-giver]; that which is your divine abode; in battles, those which are your abodes; the oblation is this"—this is for the animal sacrifice to Soma.

For the animal sacrifice to Pūṣan, [the verses] are: "Pūṣan these regions," "In the path of paths," "The path of paths," "That which is bright for thee," "Those which are thine, O Pūṣan," and "Pūṣan is a good kinsman. (ŚŚS 6.10.4) For the animal sacrifice to Bṛhaspati, [the verses] are: "To the divine ordainer," "Bṛhaspati has won," "For he is pure," "He with the *suṣṭubh*," "He with the *ṛk*, he," and "He to our womb. (ŚŚS 6.10.5)

"Viśve adya maruto viśva-ūtī yam devāso avatha viśve devā gṛṇata ye ke ca jmā; te hi yajñeṣu yajñiyāsa ūmāḥ stīrṇe barhiṣi"—this is for the Vaiśvadeva [offering]. (Śoma: Āśvin Śastra; Savanīya Paśu & Ekādaśinī) "Indram naro indro rājā indra kṣatram uru na ā no viśvābhir ūtibhiḥ sajoṣā ā te śuṣmo vṛṣabha"—this is for the Aindra [offering]. (Śoma: Āśvin Śastra; Savanīya Paśu & Ekādaśinī)
"O Maruts, you who possess cattle and horses, like spokes in a wheel, come hither; may you grant us protection"—this is for the Marut [victim].
(ŚS 6.10.8) "Both of you, O slayers of Vṛtra, fight together; the inspired singer now honors you with pure songs for the sake of the people"—this is for the Aindrāgna [victim]. (ŚS 6.10.9)

"May the divine Savitṛ come to us, the protector; may the god Savitṛ come with his restraints; that which is desirable today for you; those paths of yours—grant that to us from heaven. This is for the animal sacrifice to Savitṛ. "He propped up the sky; that I implore you; down upon thee [O Agni]; even thus do I praise this prayer of the one who strives; O Varuṇa, lift up the highest [from the fetter]. This is for the animal sacrifice to Varuṇa. Thus [are the yājyās] for the eleven animals.
And those deities who are likewise [the animals] for the Paśus. (13) "Indrā nu pūṣaṇā"—this is for the animal dedicated to Indra and Pūṣan.
(1) "Somā pūṣaṇā"—this is for the animal dedicated to Soma and Pūṣan. (2)

"Sam vām karmaṇā" is for the animal sacrifice dedicated to Indra and Viṣṇu. (Soma: Āśvina; Savanīya Paśu & Ekādaśinī) "Nāsatyābhyām" is for the animal sacrifice dedicated to the Aśvins. (Soma: Āśvina; Savanīya Paśu & Ekādaśinī) "Viṣṇor nu kam" is for the animal sacrifice dedicated to Viṣṇu. (Soma: Āśvina; Savanīya Paśu & Ekādaśinī)

"Rātrī" [is the name] for the night-verse. (6) "Bhūriṃ dve" [is the name] for the verse addressed to Heaven and Earth (*dyāvāpṛthivīya*). (7) "Janīyanta" [is the name] for the three verses beginning with "sa vāvṛdhe divyaṃ suparṇam. [The full verses are: "He whose law all creatures follow, whose law the waters attend, in whose law the Lord of Prosperity is established—that Sarasvant we invoke for our protection. (8) [These are] the verses for Sarasvant. (8)
[Regarding the Vaiśvakarman animal sacrifice: Having omitted the fourth [verse] of the Vaiśvakarman hymn, namely "ya imā viśvā bhuvanāni" (ŚS 6.11);
[one uses] "ā te pitar" for the one dedicated to Rudra;
and "ahaṃ rudrebhiḥ" for the one whose deity is Vāk.
There are three *pūrvā* verses for the omentum, three for the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*), and three for the animal victim; there are three subsequent *yājyā* verses for each.
Some do not perform the animal-cake offering for the *savanīya* sacrifice;
however, the ritual procedure remains the same.
The [offering] for Sāvitrī and Vāgdevatā is performed in a low voice.
(15) The Manotā hymn is repeated for each group of animals.

(16) Having performed the ritual actions for the animal sacrifice at the morning pressing (prātaḥsavana), beginning from the girding of the sacrificial post up to the offering of the omentum (vapā), he goes out and, having touched water in the same manner, [stands] at the Cātvāla pit. (17)
Having worshipped the *dhiṣṇya* hearths, they proceed to the *sadas*.
Standing in front of the two *havirdhāna* sheds, looking toward each [hearth] in turn, [the Adhvaryu addresses] the Āhavanīya fire with:

"Thou art the sovereign, O *kṛśānu*; protect me with thy Rudra-like countenance, O Agni; satisfy me; let there be homage to thee; do not harm me. (ŚŚS 6.12) 1–3. (Soma: Morning Pressing; Proceeding to the Sadas and Worship of the Dhiṣṇyas)
The concluding portion [of the mantra] begins with *raudra* (or similar terms).
Or it may be without a concluding portion (*anudarka*).
Having churned [the fire] with the mantra, "Thou art born of the wood, worthy of worship," he throws [the kindling stick] into the fire.
"Thou art the one to be praised by the assembly, O Pavamāna"—with these words he praises [the Soma].
(ŚŚS 6.12.7) "Thou art swift-moving, thou art cloud-bearing"—with these words [he approaches] the Cātvāla pit.
(ŚŚS 6.12.8) "Thou art the sage, the slayer of the sacrificial offerings"—with these words [he approaches] the Śāmitra fire. (ŚŚS 6.12.9)

"Thou art he who sweeps together, the sustainer of all," [with these words] he addresses the *utkara* heap. (ŚŚS 6.12.10) Turning to the right, "Thou art the pervasive one, the carrier," [with these words] he addresses the *āgnīdhra* hearth. (ŚŚS 6.12.11) Those about to enter the *sadas* touch it from above, saying: "Thou art the back of heaven; do not burn me. (ŚŚS 6.12.12)
Having touched the two door-posts with the formula, “O doors of *ṛta*, do not burn me,” they proceed to the north of the *āgnīdhrīya* hearth, those who pass by the hearths from west to east.
(ŚŚS 6.12) With the formula, “Thou art the robber, O Sagara,” [he addresses] the seat of the Acchāvāka.
(ŚŚS 6.12) With the formula, “Thou art the carrier, O bearer of oblations,” [he addresses] the hearth of the Hotṛ. (ŚŚS 6.12)

"Thou art Śvātra, thou art Pracetās"—this is for the Maitrāvaruṇa. (ŚŚS 6.12.16) "Thou art Tutha, thou art Viśvavedas"—this is for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin. (ŚŚS 6.12.17) "Thou art Uśij, thou art Kavi"—this is for the Potṛ. (ŚŚS 6.12.18)
"Thou art desiring [the gods], thou art the worshipper," [this is] for the Neṣṭṛ. (ŚŚS 6.12.19) "Thou art the remover of distress, thou art the remover of poverty," [this is] for the Acchāvāka.
(ŚŚS 6.12.20) Having looked at the Mārjālīya fire-altar, [he says]: "Thou art pure, O Mārjālīya. (ŚŚS 6.12.21)

"Thou art pure, worthy of being approached"—with these words [he approaches] the seat of the Brahman priest. (ŚŚS 6.12.22) "Thou art the abode of Truth, the light of heaven"—with these words [he approaches] the Audumbarī pillar.
(ŚŚS 6.12.23) "Thou art the ocean, all-pervading"—with these words, having looked toward the Sadas. (ŚŚS 6.12.24)
"Thou art the unborn, the one-footed"—this [formula] is for the *śālāmukhīya* fire.
(ŚŚS 6.12.25) "Thou art the serpent of the deep"—this [formula] is for the *prājahita* fire.
(ŚŚS 6.12.26) "Thou art food, the lord of food"—this [formula] is for the *vrataśrapaṇa* fire. (ŚŚS 6.12.27)

"O fires, you are the Sagaras; you are the Sagaras by name. With your fierce host, protect me, O fires! Sustain me! Homage be to you! Do not harm me!"—thus [he addresses] all of them. (Soma: Entering the Session Hall and Worshiping the Dhiṣṇya Fires)

"Thou art the lord of the road; may it stand with us today for our welfare on the path traveled by the gods"—having thus worshipped the sun, the Maitrāvaruṇa and the others proceed northward, excluding the Acchāvāka, and enter the *sadas* by the eastern door. (Soma: Āśv.; Entering the Sadas and Worship of the Dhiṣṇyas)

Reciting, “O All-Gods, glide along after me; O Indra, the threefold refuge; from whatever we fear, O Indra; [and] the wonderful Lord of the Assembly,” they proceed in front of and to the north of all the *dhiṣṇya* hearths.
(ŚŚS 6.13) Having gone first to each of the southern *dhiṣṇyas*, one sits down behind his own respective *dhiṣṇya*. (ŚŚS 6.13)

Having gone to the north of the *sadas*, the Brahman priest enters the *sadas* by the western door, goes to the south of the Maitrāvaruṇa, and sits down in his seat. (ŚŚS 6.13) They do not exit by the western door until the pressing has concluded. (ŚŚS 6.13)

Between the *dhiṣṇya* of the Hotṛ and that of the Maitrāvaruṇa lies the common path for those who do not have their own *dhiṣṇyas*. (ŚŚS 6.13.7) To the north of each respective *dhiṣṇya* is the path for those who possess their own *dhiṣṇyas*.
(ŚŚS 6.13.8) From the western half of the Āgnīdhrīya fire-altar, they proceed toward the north. (ŚŚS 6.13.9)
Or [the path] is to the south of the Mārjālīya fire.
(ŚŚS 6.13.10) And they return without turning back.
(ŚŚS 6.13.11) The worship of the Āditya [altar] does not take place during the night-rounds nor during the Āśvina [śastra]; it does not take place, it does not take place. (ŚŚS 6.13.13)
Having moved forward, they proceed with the *puroḍāśas* belonging to the *savanīya* offerings. (Soma: Āśvina Śastra;
*Savanīya-puroḍāśa*) "Accompanied by parched grains (*dhānāvantam*)"—this is the *puronuvākyā*. (Soma: Āśvina Śastra;

*Savanīya-puroḍāśa*) "The Hotṛ shall invoke Indra, the lord of the bay horses (*harivān*)"—thus is the *praiṣa* at each pressing, as it has been handed down in the traditional recitation. (Soma: Āśvina Śastra; *Savanīya-puroḍāśa*)
He distributes [the portions] according to the pressing (savana).
With that very [portion], having set it aside, the Hotṛ sacrifices, saying: "O Hotṛ, sacrifice for one who has sacrificed.
"O Agni, enjoy our oblation"—this is the invitatory verse (puronuvākyā) for the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.
"Let the Hotṛ sacrifice for the *puroḍāśas* of Agni"—with these *praiṣas* (directions), [the offering is made] at each pressing (*anusavana*). (Soma: Āśvina;
*savanīya-puroḍāśa*) "And 'O Agni, enjoy the oblation' (*haviḥ agne vīhi*) is the *yājyā* (offering verse). (Soma: Āśvina;
*savanīya-puroḍāśa*) The cups for Indra-Vāyu, Mitra-Varuṇa, and the Aśvins are those belonging to two deities (*dvidevatya*). (Soma: Āśvina; *dvidevatya-graha*)
"O Vāyu, come hither, O beautiful one! O Indra and Vāyu, here [are the offerings]!"—these are the two *puronuvākyās* for the cup belonging to Indra and Vāyu.
(ŚŚS 7.2) "Let the Hotṛ worship Vāyu; let the Hotṛ worship Indra and Vāyu"—these are the two *praiṣas*.
(ŚŚS 7.2) "Drink first with a hundred [powers] of ours"—this is the *yājyā*. (ŚŚS 7.2)

"O Mitra and Varuṇa, this [is for you]" is the *puronuvākyā* for the offering to Mitra and Varuṇa. (Soma: Āśvina; Dvidevatya; Grahya) "The Hotṛ shall worship Mitra and Varuṇa" is the *praiṣa*. (Soma: Āśvina; Dvidevatya; Grahya) "Praised by Jamadagni" is the *yājyā*. (Soma: Āśvina; Dvidevatya; Grahya)

"Prātar-yujā" is the invitatory verse (*puronuvākyā*) for the offering to the Aśvins. (Soma: Āśvina; offering to two deities; secret rite). "Hotā yakṣad aśvinā" is the direction (*praiṣa*). (Soma: Āśvina; offering to two deities; secret rite). "Vāvṛdhānā" is the offering verse (*yājyā*). (Soma: Āśvina; offering to two deities; secret rite).
He recites the *puronuvākyās* and the *praiṣas* for the dual-deity cups (*dvidevatya*) without taking breath. (11) Likewise, he performs the sacrifice.
(12) For the cup dedicated to Indra and Vāyu (*aindravāyava*), there are two separate *puronuvākyās* with distinct *praṇavas*. (13)

ŚŚS 7.2: When there are separate *vaṣaṭ* calls for the two portions to be offered, [the procedure is as follows]. (Soma: Āśvin; Dvidevatya; Secret) ŚŚS 7.2: The silent recitation (*japa*) performed previously, the *ye yajāmahe*, and the subsequent consecration formula (*anumantraṇa*) are each performed once.

(Soma: Āśvin; Dvidevatya; Secret) ŚŚS 7.3: Having received the cup for Indra and Vāyu with the mantra, "May the wealthy Purūvasu come," and having placed it in the wide right [hand], one should keep it uncovered and not look at it until the remnants of the Dvidevatya cups are poured out. (Soma: Āśvin; Dvidevatya; Secret)

Having received the cup for Mitra and Varuṇa with the formula, "May the wealthy one come; may the wealth-finder [find] wealth," and having carried it to the south of the cup for Indra and Vāyu, he places it to the south-west.

(ŚŚS 7.3) Having received the cup for the Aśvins with the formula, "May the wealthy one come; may the wealth-uniter [unite] wealth," and having carried it to the south of the two eastern cups, he places it to the north-west. (ŚŚS 7.3)

"O Agni, partake of the Soma"—this is the *anuvapaṭkāra* (the secondary *vaṣaṭ*-call) for all Soma-offering *yajyās*, excluding the dual-deity offerings (*dvidevatya*), the seasonal offerings (*ṛtuyāja*), the Āditya cup, the Sāvitra cup, and the Pātnīvata cup. Or, for the Pātnīvata cup, it may be performed in a low voice (*upāṃśu*). When the call "for those being lifted up" (*unnīyamānebhyaḥ*) has been made, [the priest recites] the hymn for the cups being lifted up: "May the bay steeds bring thee hither" (*ā tvā vahantu harayaḥ*). (Śrauta Sūtra 7.3–4: Soma; Āśvin; Dual-deity Cups; Hymns for the Lifting of the Cups; Offerings of the Departed Cups; Consuming.)
"Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to Indra for the morning pressing"—this is the *praisha* (direction).
"This Soma-mead is for thee," with these words he performs the *yajya* (offering verse).

"Beholding men, I, who behold men, gaze upon thee," [saying this] he gazes at the *hotṛ*'s cup; "I, who bestow vigor, receive thee, who bestowest vigor," [saying this] and having received it, he touches his chest and [the cups] for the two deities.
(ŚŚS 7.4) The *hotraka*s sacrifice from the cups that have been refilled. (ŚŚS 7.5)
"Friendship is ours," says the Maitrāvaruṇa. (ŚŚS 7.4.6) [Soma: Āś; Camasa-unnetra; Prasthita-homas;
Consuming] "O Indra, you the bull," says the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin. (ŚŚS 7.4.7) [Soma: Āś; Camasa-unnetra; Prasthita-homas;
Consuming] "Of whom the Maruts," says the Potṛ. (ŚŚS 7.4.8) [Soma: Āś; Camasa-unnetra; Prasthita-homas; Consuming]
"O Agni, [bring] the wives," [says] the Neṣṭṛ.
(ŚŚS 7.4.9) "O you whose food is the bull," [says] the Āgnīdhra.
(ŚŚS 7.4.10) When it is said, "O Āgnīdhra, with this [verse]," the Āgnīdhra responds, "With this. (ŚŚS 7.4.11)
"He has done us a kindness, he who will cause us to drink the Soma," says the Hotṛ. (ŚŚS 7.4.12) [Soma: Āś; Camasa-unnayana; Prasthita-homas;

Bhakṣaṇa] "O you who are about to consume the Soma, invite one another by means of your sacrificial names," say the performers to one another, seeking mutual invitation. (ŚŚS 7.4.13) [Soma: Āś; Camasa-unnayana; Prasthita-homas;
Bhakṣaṇa] The utterer of the *vaṣaṭ* is the first to consume [the Soma]. (ŚŚS 7.4.14) [Soma: Āś; Camasa-unnayana; Prasthita-homas; Bhakṣaṇa]

ŚŚS 7.4: He pours into the Hotṛ’s cup the remainder of the draughts for two deities that has been tasted, as well as the remnants of the Nārāśaṃsa cups, with the formula: “Having been tasted by thee when offered, I pour thee in—full of vigor for the gods, full of life for myself. (Soma: Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra; Camasa-unnetana; Prasthita-homas; Bhakṣaṇa) ŚŚS 7.4: The pouring of the remnant of the Aindravāyava cup occurs twice; in that case, the mantra is repeated. (Soma: Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra; Camasa-unnetana; Prasthita-homas; Bhakṣaṇa)
And there is no disposal of the portions for the dual deities until the remainder has been poured down. (ŚŚS 7.4.17) [Soma: Āśir; Drawing of the Cups; Oblations of the Prasthitas; Consuming]

In this rite, having taken up the cup for Indra and Vāyu with the formula, "Vasu, Purūvasu," and having invoked it with, "Vāyu and Indra-Vāyu are invited together with breath and together with luster; I am invited of them together with breath and together with luster," he drinks. Then, having again taken it up with the formula for taking up (*pragraha-mantra*), he drinks again with the formula for drinking (*bhakṣa-mantra*). (Soma: Āśir; Drawing out the Cups; Oblations of the Departed Cups; Consuming)
Having taken up the cup for Mitra and Varuṇa with the formula, "Here Vasu has provided wealth," (ŚŚS 7.5.2);
and having consumed it with the formula, "Mitra and Varuṇa are invited together with sight, together with luster; I am invited of them together with sight, together with luster" (ŚŚS 7.5.3).
Having carried the Āśvina cup around the head clockwise, having looked at it, having carried it back around, and having looked at it again; (ŚŚS 7.5).
Having lifted up the Āśvina cup with the formula, "Here is the Vasu, the bestower of wealth" (iha vasuḥ saṃyadvasuḥ); (ŚŚS 7.5).

"Invoked are the two divine Aśvins together with hearing and together with luster; may I be invoked of them together with hearing and together with luster"—having thus consumed [the soma], he touches water and invokes the *ilā*.
Then they lift up the cups.
He takes hold of the *hotṛ*’s cup. (ŚŚS 7.5.9) [Regarding the Soma: the drawing out of the cups, the *prasthita* offerings, and the consumption.
There is no contact anywhere with the Soma by means of the smearings of clarified butter.
(ŚŚS 7.5.10) Having invited one another, they consume the *prasthita* portions. (ŚŚS 7.5.11)
"Tejase tvā brahmavarcasāya bhakṣayāmi"—this is the mantra for consuming [the Soma] at the morning pressing (prātaḥsavana).
"Ojase tvā indriyāya bhakṣayāmi"—this is [the mantra] at the midday pressing (mādhyandina).
"Prājāyai tvā puṣṭyai bhakṣayāmi"—this is [the mantra] at the third pressing (tṛtīyasavana).
Having consumed [the soma], he touches his chest with the mantra: "Be auspicious to us in the heart" (ŚŚS 7.5).
Having placed the cups in the left hand, they cause them to swell with the right hand.
At the morning pressing, the swelling formula is: "Swell up; let [the juices] gather unto thee" (ŚŚS 7.5).
With the verse *sam te payāṃsi*, [they swell] the two subsequent [cups]. (ŚŚS 7.5.18) They cause the cups that have been set forth (*prasthita*) to swell.
(ŚŚS 7.5.19) This applies also to the cup for the Ājya-stotra and the Marutvatīya-stotra. (ŚŚS 7.5.20)

The *nārāśaṃsa* cups are [consumed] at the *ājya*, *prauga*, *niṣkevalya*, *marutvatīya*, and *vaiśvadeva* [śastras]. (ŚŚS 7.5.21) "Thou art the divine *nārāśaṃsa*; that which is thy wisdom, the light of heaven—of thee, who hast been consumed by the ancestors and invited, I, being invited, partake. This is the mantra for consuming the *nārāśaṃsa* cups at the morning pressing (*prātaḥsavana*). (ŚŚS 7.5.22)
"By the thighs"—this is the modification at the midday pressing.

(ŚŚS 7.5.23) "By the poetic insights"—this is at the third pressing. (ŚŚS 7.5.24) When addressed with "O Acchāvāka, sit down," he sits down to the north of the *sadas* in front of the *śruti*. Having taken the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*), and being addressed with "O Acchāvāka, recite," he recites the three verses beginning with "Toward Agni for your protection. (ŚŚS 7.6.1)
[The Ācchāvāka recites] the *praṇava* and the *nigada*:

"O Sacrificer, Hotṛ, Adhvaryu, Agnīdh, Brahman, Potṛ, Neṣṭṛ, and Upavaktṛ—impel for food, conquer for strength! Let your kinsmen bow down, let your non-kinsmen bow down; let your rivals be defeated on their path. You shall conquer the unassailable, you shall conquer with the unassailable. May Indra hear you, may Agni hear you! Having set forth, speak of Soma to Indra and Agni! O Brāhmaṇas, summon us Brāhmaṇas! (Soma: Āśir; Ācchāvāka)
"O Brāhmaṇa, this Acchāvāka desires your invitation," says the Adhvaryu; [the Hotṛ] replies, "Invite him, O Hotṛ. (4) (Soma: Āśrāvaṇa; Ācchāvāka) The Hotṛ invites him: (5) (Soma: Āśrāvaṇa;

Ācchāvāka) "The sacrificer, pressing the Soma, has grasped for you both these beautiful hymns; he has established himself as the Upavaktṛ; and our cows have been invited—yes, they are invited," [says the Hotṛ] while about to invite [the Ācchāvāka]. (6) (Soma: Āśrāvaṇa; Ācchāvāka)
"Or, [the formula] 'The cows are summoned for us'—from this point on, he who is not yet being invited [should proceed].
(ŚŚS 7.6) "The Acchāvāka, not having been invited, should run after [the Hotṛ] as far as he is able, [reciting] the hymn beginning with 'Turn back!
(ŚŚS 7.6) "Or the Hotṛ, having invited the Acchāvāka in return, [should do so] against one who is willing. (ŚŚS 7.6)
When it is said, "For him who is being led up," the Acchāvāka recites the *sūktavāka* beginning with "To him who desires to drink" (*praty asmai pipīṣate*).
He performs the *yajati* offering with the verse beginning, "With those who travel at dawn" (*prātar yāvabhiḥ*).

Having consumed [the soma] and handed over the cup, which has been replenished, to the Adhvaryu, he turns to the right, enters the *sadas* by the western door, sits down behind his own *dhiṣṇya* hearth, and eats the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*).

If the Acchāvāka has already moved forward [to his seat], he should perform the *acchāvākīyā* (the verse for the Acchāvāka). Having gone out by his own irregular path of movement, having performed the *bahiṣkarma* (external ritual act) for the Acchāvāka, he performs his own ritual act. (ŚŚS 7.7.4) But the Hotṛ [performs his act] at his own *dhiṣṇya* hearth.
(ŚŚS 7.7.5) There is an option regarding the *yājyās* (offering verses) of the *hotrakas* (assistant priests). (ŚŚS 7.7.6)
At the morning pressing, they sacrifice while reciting the invitatory verses (anuvākyās), or else by half-verses.
Here they consume the fast-food (vratayanti). And this continues after the Upasads.

Then they proceed with the offerings for the seasons (*ṛtu-yāja*). (1) [The Adhvaryu] gives the directions without pausing by means of the *ṛtu-praiṣa* formulas: "Let the Hotṛ worship Indra from the office of the Hotṛ," and so forth. (2) He performs the sacrifice in that same manner. (3)
That [deity] with which he sends forth [the command] is the one to be sacrificed to; having extracted [the portion], the Hotṛ sacrifices, saying, "May so-and-so sacrifice.

(ŚŚS 7.8) Or [he may say]: "O Indra, drink the Soma with the season-offering," as in the verse of Medhātithi. (ŚŚS 7.8) Whichever [name] is heard at the end of the *praiṣa* (direction), that very one performs the sacrifice. (ŚŚS 7.8)
"O Hotṛ, sacrifice this," says the Adhvaryu. (Soma: Āśvina Śastra; Seasonal Offerings) 7.
"And the Gṛhapati [sacrifices]. 8. He sacrifices for those two. 9. (Soma: Āśvina Śastra; Seasonal Offerings)
They consume [the soma] according to the *vaṣaṭ* call. (10) At the end, the Hotṛ consumes twice.

(11) In this case, as well as in the offerings to dual deities, he should smell it as if he were merely smearing it [on his lips]. (12) *Śrautasūtra* 7.8.10–12. (Soma: Āśvinagraha; Seasonal Offerings)

Intending to recite the *ājya* śastra, he murmurs: "May Father Mātariśvan recite; may Uśij, whose steps are flawless, recite; may Soma, who knows the ways, lead us through the ways; may Bṛhaspati recite the hymns and songs of praise. Having thus murmured, at the beginning of the recitation at the morning pressing (*prātaḥsavana*), he utters the call: "Śoṃsāvaḥ! (Recite!). Having called with this, he recites the *upāṃśu* portion silently. (Śoma: Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 6.5.9; Ājya-śastra)

Having paused after reciting "Agni is light, light is Agni," having paused after reciting "Indra is light, light is Indra," and having paused after reciting "Sūrya is light, light is Sūrya," he pauses at every half-verse while reciting the *puroruḥ* hymn. (Soma: Ājya-śastra)

"Agni kindled by the gods; Agni kindled by Manu; the charioteer of the sacrifices; the inviolable Hotṛ; the swift bearer of oblations; may the god bring the gods hither; may Agni the god sacrifice to the gods; may he, Jātavedas, perform the sacrifices"—this is the *ājya* [verse], beginning with "pra vo devāya. (ŚŚS 7.9) Of this [verse], the first half-verse is recited foot by foot. (ŚŚS 7.9) And [the same applies] to the *marutvatīya* and *vaiśvadeva* [śastras]. (ŚŚS 7.9)

Having recited the remainder of the *sūkta*, having called [the Hotṛ] and clothed [him] with the final verse, he mutters the *ukthavīrya*: "Radiance, splendor, the Dawn, light—for the sake of renown, the *uktha* has been spoken unto thee.
(ŚŚS 7.9.6) At all the *śastra-yājyās*, the Adhvaryu says, "O reciter of the *uktha*! (ŚŚS 7.9.7) He offers the oblation with the verse, "O Agni and Indra... (ŚŚS 7.9.8)

When the *ājya* [laud] has been completed, they chant the stotra. (Soma: Ājya; Praüga-śastra) "Among the *śastras* that possess a *stotra*, this is the one," he says; then, having called out after the final *pratīhāra*, they recite the *śastra*. (Soma: Ājya; Praüga-śastra) In the *praüga*, they insert verses between the *ṛcas* of the Mādhucchandasa triads; these are called the *puroruc*s. (Soma: Ājya; Praüga-śastra)

Before those [verses], there is the *āhāva* (the call). (Soma: Āśva-Śastra; Prauga-Śastra) And before the *paridhānīyā* (concluding verse), there is the *āhāva*. (Soma: Āśva-Śastra; Prauga-Śastra) The verse addressed to the Viśvedevas consists of six feet. (Soma: Āśva-Śastra; Prauga-Śastra)

In that [recitation], having paused after each pair [of verses], he recites the *praṇava* (the syllable *oṃ*) with two [verses] at a time. (ŚŚ 7.10) Regarding the verse addressed to Sarasvatī, there is an option: one may either recite it or not. However, the *āhāva* (the call "Oṃ śoṃsāvoṃ") is obligatory. (ŚŚ 7.10) Having recited once the verses beginning, "Vāyu, who goes first, the lover of sacrifice; come together with the mind to the sacrifice, auspicious with your auspicious teams," he then recites three times the first of the three verses beginning, "O Vāyu, come hither, O beautiful one. (ŚŚ 7.10)
"O men, the two gods with golden paths, the lords, for our aid—Vāyu and Indra, the excellent sacrificers. [The hymn] "Indra-vāyū imā" consists of three verses. (Soma: Āśvin-śastra;

Prauga-śastra) "In the assemblies of the two sages, by the power of the skillful one’s will, O destroyers of enemies, come to the common dwelling-place. [The hymn] "Mitraṃ huve" consists of three verses. (Soma: Āśvin-śastra; Prauga-śastra)
"O two divine Adhvaryus, come on your chariot with sun-bright skins; anoint the sacrifice with honey!"—these three verses [beginning] "O Aśvins, [bring] sacrificial refreshments.

(ŚS 7.10) "Indra, most eager for hymns and lord of spoils, is the friend of the pressed juices, he who possesses the bay steeds."—these three verses [beginning] "O Indra, come, you of wondrous luster! (ŚS 7.10)

We invoke all the gods, being of one accord at this sacrifice. May those divine gods come to this sacrifice with their holy thought—those who are the makers of the body of the sacrifice, all of them for the drinking of Soma. "The protectors, the upholders of the people"—these three [verses]. (Soma: Āśir; Prauga-śastra)

"Of all divine speeches, we invoke Sarasvatī, the goddess of speech, the well-adorned, at this sacrifice. Having performed the concluding rite (*paridhāna*) with the last of the three verses beginning "The purifying Sarasvatī," he mutters the *ukthavīrya*: "Quicken my speech; satisfy my breath; protect my sight; preserve my hearing; grant me color; protect my body; bestow glory upon me; for the sake of resonance, the *uktha* has been spoken for you. (Soma: Āśvina-śastra, Prauga-śastra)
With the verse, "To all [gods] the Soma-mead," he performs the *yajña* (offering).
(ŚŚS 7.10) The *stotriya* and *anurūpa* consist of triplets (*ṛcaḥ*), excluding the *pragāthas*.
(ŚŚS 7.11) "Come to us, O Mitra and Varuṇa," and "Come to us"—these two are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* for the Maitrāvaruṇa’s *ājya-śastra*. (ŚŚS 7.11–12)

"Forward to Mitra" (*pra vo mitrāya*) is the opening of the *uktha* (ŚS 7.11.3). Having concluded with the last of the nine verses beginning "Of the two Mitras" (*pra mitrayoḥ*), he performs the *yajyā* with "Come hither to the pressed [juice]" (*upa naḥ sutam ā gatam*) (ŚS 7.11.4). "Come hither" (*ā yāhi*) and "We have pressed" (*suṣuma*) are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin’s *ājya-śastra* (ŚS 7.12.1).
The remainder of the hymn constitutes the *ukthamukha*, excluding the last verse.
(Soma: Āśvina-śastra; Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin’s Ājya-śastra) "O Indra, thee the bull...

(Soma: Āśvina-śastra; Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin’s Ājya-śastra) Having performed the *paridhāna* (concluding recitation) with the last of the three verses beginning "Up indeed [he has risen] over...", he offers the oblation with the verse, "O Indra, the finder of wisdom... (Soma: Āśvina-śastra; Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin’s Ājya-śastra)

"O Indra and Agni, come to the pressed [soma]"—these are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses for the *acchāvāka*. (ŚŚS 7.13.1) The remainder of the hymn constitutes the *ukthamukha*. (ŚŚS 7.13.2) "O Indra and Agni, here I call you hither"—these five [verses follow]. (ŚŚS 7.13.3)
With the verse *iyam vāmasya manmanaḥ* as the ninth of nine, having performed the *paridhāna* (concluding verse), he recites the *yajyā*: *indra-agnī ā gatam sutam*.

(ŚŚS 7.13) For the *bṛhat-pṛṣṭha* [stotra], the *stotriya* verses are *mitram vayam indram id gāthinaḥ* and *indra agne*. (ŚŚS 7.14) The *acchāvāka* performs the *stotriya* and the *anurūpa* according to the *rathantara* melody. (ŚŚS 7.14)
The opening of the *uktha* (recitation) should be appropriate [to the occasion]. (3) The *hotraka* priests perform four *āhāva*s (calls).
(4) And the *hotṛ* performs [the *āhāva*] for the additional *ukthas*. (5)

[The *pra-sthāna* chant is performed] with the *stotriya* and the *anurūpa*, and that which follows immediately after the *anurūpa* up to the *paridhānīyā*. (ŚŚS 7.14.6) The *pragātha* following the *anurūpa* is the fifth [in sequence] after that, at the midday pressing. (ŚŚS 7.14.7) At night, it is for all [the *śastras*] from the beginning of the *uktha*. (ŚŚS 7.14.8)
When the Adhvaryu says, "O Praśāstṛ, give the command," the Praśāstṛ says, "Om, creep forth! (ŚŚS 7.14).
Turning to the right, they creep out by the western door, passing to the north of the Udumbara post and to the south of the Brahman. (ŚŚS 7.14).
They proceed northward along the front of the hall. (ŚŚS 7.14).
For the midday pressing, having gone forth as they had emerged [at the morning pressing], they sit down according to their respective seats.
(ŚŚS 7.14) At the beginning of the midday pressing, they press the King [Soma]. (ŚŚS 7.15)

The Grāvastut, having entered the *havirdhāna* shed by the eastern door, stands to the south in front of the southern wheel of the northern *havirdhāna*. Having wrapped the mouth [of the soma-vessel] with the soma-cloth and having heard the sound of the pressing-stones, he recites the hymn without being prompted—either in half-verses or without pausing—without joining the verses together. (Soma: Āśvina Śastra; Mādhyandina Pavamāna)
"O divine Savitṛ, they harness their minds for thee, and they harness their thoughts; O Indra, bring us food, bring it to us with thy right hand; come hither, bring it! (ŚS 7.15).

Having recited the first of the three verses beginning with "Swell up, let [the waters] gather unto thee," he recites two verses of Arbuda. (ŚS 7.15). Having recited the second verse, he recites two verses of Arbuda. (ŚS 7.15). (Soma: Āśvina Śastra; Mādhyandina Pavamāna Stotra)

Having recited the third [verse], he recites one verse of the *Arbuda* hymn: "The ten fingers cleanse you," "This very one, the ten fingers [cleanse]," and "They cleanse him who is to be cleansed. Having thus recited these verses containing the word "cleansed" (*mṛṣṭavatī*), he recites the verses containing the word "jar" (*kalaśavatī*): "Up to the jars they have sung," "He runs into the jars," and "O Soma, thy juice flows around. Having thus recited these verses containing the word "jar," [he concludes the midday pressing].
From the *āpyāyitavatī* onwards, the second pressing is thus distributed: five [verses] beginning with the sixth belong to the *arbuda*.
(ŚŚS 7.15) Thus the third pressing is also distributed: three [verses] beginning with the eleventh belong to the *arbuda*.
(ŚŚS 7.15) In whichever pressing they should utter the word "bṛhat," there [the formula] is "bṛhad vadanti. (ŚŚS 7.15)
The sixth [verse] is used at the first [pressing]. (Soma: Āśvina;
Mādhyandina Pressing) When the filter has been spread out, [he recites] two verses beginning with *pavitram te* and one verse beginning with *vi yat pavitram*. (Soma: Āśvina;
Mādhyandina Pressing) While the streams are flowing, [he recites] the verses beginning with *prāsya dhārāḥ*, *pra dhārā asya*, and *pra te dhārāḥ*. (Soma: Āśvina; Mādhyandina Pressing)
7.15. When the cups are being drawn, whichever [priest] should desire the *pāvamānī* [verses], [he should recite them]. 15. (Soma: Āśvin; Mādhyandina Pavamāna) 7.15.
He restrains [the Soma] with the three verses beginning, "O Indu, for Indra accompanied by the Maruts. 16. (Soma: Āśvin; Mādhyandina Pavamāna) 7.15.

When the last cup has been drawn, having performed the concluding ritual (*paridhāna*) with the final verse of the *Arbuda* hymn, and having taken off his turban (*uṣṇīṣa*), he releases it. 17. (Soma: Āśvin; Mādhyandina Pavamāna)

In the case of *satras* and *ahīnas*, however, [the *arbuda* hymn] is recited on the final day. (ŚŚS 7.15.18) Or one may recite the pure *arbuda* hymn. (ŚŚS 7.15.19) When the *pavamāna* has been chanted at the midday pressing (*mādhyandina-savana*), they proceed with the *dadhigharma* offering, provided that the *pravargya* rite has been performed. (ŚŚS 7.16.1) [ŚŚS 7.16: The *dadhigharma*]
When addressed with "O Hotṛ, speak!", he recites the first [verse] with "Arise! Behold! (ŚŚS 7.16.2).
When addressed with "The oblation is cooked," he recites the second verse of the hymn (ŚŚS 7.16.3).
When addressed with "Recite the offering prayer for the Dadhigharma," he offers the sacrifice with the third verse (ŚŚS 7.16.4).
Without taking breath, he recites each verse individually, accompanied by the *praṇava*. (Soma: Āśir;
Dadhigharma) Likewise, he performs the *yajati* offering. (Soma: Āśir;
Dadhigharma) "O Agni, partake of the *dadhigharma*!"—this is the *anuvaṣaṭkāra*. (Soma: Āśir; Dadhigharma)

"May that great sensory power be in me; may skill be in me, may wisdom be in me. May the three-pointed Gharma shine forth together with intention and mind, together with the Virāj and the light. May we partake of its draught. This is the mantra for the consumption [of the Soma].

(ŚS 7.16) Having performed the ritual with the animal-cake (*paśu-puroḍāśa*), they proceed from here with the *savanīya* cakes. (ŚS 7.16) "For the midday pressing"—this is the invitatory verse (*puronuvākyā*). (ŚS 7.17) (Soma: Āśir; Dadhigharma; Prasthita-homas)
"Regarding the midday pressing, [the offering] for the *sviṣṭakṛt* [is as follows].
(ŚŚS 7.17.2) "The hymn for the soma being drawn up is 'asāvi deva...
(ŚŚS 7.17.3) "The call for the *praisha* is: 'The Hotṛ shall worship Indra at the midday pressing. (ŚŚS 7.17.4)
He offers with the verse, "Drink the Soma, O fierce one, for whom... (RV 8.4.1). (Soma: Āś;
Prasthita-homas) The second [verse] belongs to the Maitrāvaruṇa. (Soma: Āś;
Prasthita-homas) The third [verse] belongs to the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin. (Soma: Āś; Prasthita-homas)
"Come hither, O Courser!"—this is for the *potṛ*. (8) "This Soma is yours"—this is for the *neṣṭṛ*.
(9) "For Indra, the Somas known from of old"—this is for the *acchāvāka*. (10)
"Āpūrṇo asya... is for the Āgnīdhra. (ŚŚS 7.17, Soma: Āśir;
Prasthita Homas) In the two subsequent pressings, there are no offerings to the dual deities nor seasonal offerings. (ŚŚS 7.17, Soma: Āśir;
Prasthita Homas) There is no external ritual activity for the Acchāvāka. (ŚŚS 7.17, Soma: Āśir; Prasthita Homas)
The rest is the same as for the morning pressing (prātaḥsavana).
Having invoked the *iḍā* and consumed the portions that have been set forth (*prasthita*),
this is the time for the sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*).
One should give one hundred and twelve cows.
Or, beginning with twenty-one, as many as are available.
He receives the gold with the formula: "May Varuṇa give thee to me for Agni; may I attain immortality. Be a giver of life; be a source of joy to me, O receiver. (ŚŚS 7.17–18)

"To Rudra I give you; may Varuṇa grant you to me; may I attain immortality. Be a cow to the giver, a source of joy to me as I accept you. Thus for cows. (ŚS 7.18) "To Bṛhaspati I give you; may Varuṇa grant you to me; may I attain immortality. Be skin to the giver, a source of joy to me as I accept you. Thus for clothing. (ŚS 7.18)

"For Yama, may Varuṇa give thee to me; may I attain immortality. Be a horse for the giver, a joy for me who receives"—with these words [he addresses] the one-hoofed animal. (ŚŚS 7.18.4) "For Prajāpati, may Varuṇa give thee to me; may I attain immortality. Be vital breath for the giver, a joy for me who receives"—with these words [he addresses] the other [animal].
(ŚŚS 7.18.5) Or he may say "Om" for all of them. (ŚŚS 7.18.6)
He recites the mantra over the living being: "Who gave? To whom did he give? (ŚŚS 7.18).
He touches the other [offering].
(ŚŚS 7.18). Having given it, he murmurs: "Given by us, full of sweetness, go to the gods; enter the giver. (ŚŚS 7.18).

"Indrāya marutvate" is said [as the introductory formula]. (Soma: Āśvin-śastra; Marutvatīya-śastra) "Indra marutvaḥ" is the *puronuvākyā*. (Soma: Āśvin-śastra; Marutvatīya-śastra) "Hotā yakṣad indraṃ marutvantam" is the *praiṣa*. (Soma: Āśvin-śastra; Marutvatīya-śastra)
With the verse, "O Indra, rejoicing with thy troop," he performs the *yajñā* offering.
(ŚŚS 7.19.4) Having consumed that [Soma], he recites the *marutvatīya-śastra*.
(ŚŚS 7.19.5) At the beginning of the *śastra* during the midday pressing, the call for the *adhvaryu* is: "O Adhvaryu, *śoṃśāvo*! (ŚŚS 7.19.6)
The *antah-śastra* (concluding recitation) belongs to the morning pressing (*prātaḥsavana*).
(ŚŚS 7.19) Having recited the triplet beginning with "Come to us as a chariot for our aid" (*ā tvā ratham yathā ūtaye*), he calls for the response.
(ŚŚS 7.19) Having recited the triplet following it, "O Vasu, this pressed juice" (*idam vaso sutam andhaḥ*), he calls for the response. (ŚŚS 7.19)
Having recited the *Indra-nihava* *pragātha*, "O Indra, come nearer," he calls for the *uktha*.
(10) Having recited the *Brāhmaṇaspati* *pragātha*, "Now forth [brings] Brahmaṇaspati," he calls for the *uktha*.
(11) Having recited the single verse, "Agni is the leader," he calls for the *uktha*. (12)
Having recited the verse "O Soma, with thy powers" (*tvam soma kratubhiḥ*), he makes the call.
(13) Having recited the verse "They swell the waters" (*pinvanti apaḥ*), he makes the call.
(14) Having recited the six verses beginning with "The fierce one was born" (*janiṣṭhā ugraḥ*), he makes the call for the *nivid*. (15)

(16) Having recited with one verse more than the others, there is an inequality among the verses.

Having recited one [verse] of the *ṛcas*, [he recites the rest].
(ŚS 7.19) The two final [verses] are for the increase of the hymn (*sūktavivṛdhau*).
(ŚS 7.19) But at the first [of these], there is the *āhāva* call. (ŚS 7.19)
Having set aside the final [verse], at the third pressing (the *marutvatīya* recitation),
he recites the *nivid* by pādas as it is spread out;
at the final word, there is the *praṇava*.

Having recited the remainder of the hymn (*sūkta-śeṣa*), having called for the response, having performed the concluding verse (*paridhānīyā*) with the final verse, and having murmured the *ukthavīrya*, he performs the offering with the verse beginning "ye tvā hi hatye" (ŚS 8.68.1). The *Rathantara* is the *pṛṣṭha-stotra* for the *niṣkevalya-śastra*; or alternatively, the *Bṛhat*.

"Abhi tvā śūra nonumaḥ" and "Abhi tvā pūrvapītaye" are the two *pragāthas* serving as the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* for the *rathantara* [sāman]. (ŚŚS 7.20) "Tvām id dhi havāmahe" and "Tvaṃ hy ehi ceravaḥ" are [the *stotriya* and *anurūpa*] for the *bṛhat* [sāman].
(ŚŚS 7.20) "Yad vāvāna" is the *dhāyyā*. (ŚŚS 7.20)
"Drink of the pressed juice, the flavorful one"—this *pragātha* belongs to the *rathantara*.
"May he hear both"—this belongs to the *bṛhat*.
"Now, the heroic deeds of Indra"—this belongs to the *rathantara-pṛṣṭha*.
"Sing praise to him indeed"—this is [the verse] for the Bṛhat-pṛṣṭha [stotra].
(ŚS 7.20) One should recite the concluding verse (*paridhānīyā*) with particular intensity.
(ŚS 7.20) Having murmured the *ukthavīrya*, he offers the oblation with the verse: "Drink the Soma, O Indra; let it exhilarate you. (ŚS 7.20)
In the case of a *ubhayasāman* [rite], (ŚS 7.21).
In a rite where the *rathantara* is the *pṛṣṭha-stotra*, having extracted that *pragātha* which precedes the hymn (*sūkta*), he recites the source-verse (*yoni*) of the *bṛhat*. (ŚS 7.21).
In a rite where the *bṛhat* is the *pṛṣṭha-stotra*, [he recites] the source-verse of the *rathantara*. (ŚS 7.21).
After the *sāmapragātha*, in the subsequent ritual terminuses (*saṃsthā*),
this recitation of the *yoni* verses is what they call the *anuśaṃsana*.
Kauṣītaki, however, said that one should recite only the *bṛhat* and *rathantara* [verses] as the *anuśaṃsana*.
The ordinary *agniṣṭoma* has a limited number of verses; therefore, he extracts the *pragātha*. (Soma: Āśvina-śastra;

Niṣkevalya-śastra) There is a call (*āhāva*) for the *stotriya*, for the *anurūpa*, for the *dhāyyā*, for the *pragātha*, for the *sūkta*, for the *nivid*, and for the *paridhānīyā*. (Soma: Āśvina-śastra; Niṣkevalya-śastra) The *nivid* is either "the horse" (*aśvaḥ*) or "the boon" (*varaḥ*). (Soma: Āśvina-śastra; Niṣkevalya-śastra)
The Vāmadevya [Sāman] belongs to the Maitrāvaruṇa.
(ŚŚ 7.22) "Kayā naś citraḥ," "Kayā tvam na ūtyā"—these are the Stotriya and Anurūpa verses. (ŚŚ 7.22) "Kaṣ tam indra"—this is the Sāmapragātha. (ŚŚ 7.22)
“Born this very day” (RV 10.119.13).
“Thus, O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, here [be]... (RV 8.6.1). With the verse beginning “Desiring [it], now indeed for us...
(RV 8.6.2), he performs the *yajyā* offering. (ŚŚS 7.22)

The *Naudhasa* [Sāman] is for the *Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin* when the *Rathantara* is the *Pṛṣṭha* stotra. (ŚŚS 7.23.1) The *Śyaita* [Sāman] is for the *Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin* when the *Bṛhat* is the *Pṛṣṭha* stotra. (ŚŚS 7.23.2) *Tam vo dasmam*, *tat tvā yāmi suvīryam*: these are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* *pragāthas* of the *Naudhasa*. (ŚŚS 7.23.3)
"Abhipravaha pra suśrutam" is the Śyaita [Sāman].
(ŚŚ 7.23.4) "Ud u tye madhumattamāḥ" is the Sāmapragātha. (ŚŚ 7.23.5) "Indraḥ pūrbhit" is for the Naudhasa [Sāman]. (ŚŚ 7.23.6)
"asāvi somaḥ puruhūta" (The Soma has been pressed for you, O much-invoked one)—this is the Śyaita [hymn].
(ŚS 7.23.7) "ud u brahmāṇi" (Upward indeed the sacred hymns)—this is the same [as the preceding].
(ŚS 7.23.8) "ṛjīṣī vajrī" (The possessor of the dregs, the wielder of the thunderbolt)—with these words he performs the *yajati* offering. (ŚS 7.23.9)
The *kāleya* is for the *acchāvāka*.
(ŚŚ 7.24) "Tarobhir vas taraṇir it siṣāsati"—these are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* *pragāthas*. (ŚŚ 7.24) "Ud inv asya ricyate"—this is the *sāman-pragātha*. (ŚŚ 7.24)
"He has grown even further" (ŚS 7.24.4); "This [soma] here, indeed" (ŚS 7.24.5);
with "Drink and grow strong," he performs the *yajyā* (ŚS 7.24.6).
Regarding the *śastras*:
(General remarks on the *śastras* of the *āśvin* [pressing]). Generally, they do not follow the order of the traditional recitation (*samāmnāta*).
When a *bṛhatī* verse precedes and a *kakubh* or *sato bṛhatī* follows, that is called a *pragātha*.
The Bārhata [stotra] is [chanted] upon a Bṛhatī verse as the first. (Soma: Āśva-Śastra:
General Remarks) The Kākubha [stotra] is [chanted] upon a Kakubh verse. (Soma: Āśva-Śastra:

General Remarks) Having recited the Bṛhatī [verse], having taken up the last foot, having paused with the first [foot] of the following [verse], having chanted forward with the second, having taken that up again, having paused with the third, he chants forward with the last [foot]. (Soma: Āśva-Śastra: General Remarks)
These [verses] consist of three *bṛhatī*s, with the first and the last two being *kakubh*s. (Soma: Āśvina-śastra;
General Remarks) [They apply] to the *bṛhat* and *rathaṃtara* [sāmans]. (Soma: Āśvina-śastra;
General Remarks) And [they apply] to the *hotṛ*-assistants (*hotraka*) where these two form the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras] based on *pragātha*s. (Soma: Āśvina-śastra; General Remarks)
In all cases, [the *praüga-śastra*] belongs to the *yajñāyajñīya* [Sāman].
(ŚŚS 7.25, 10) And [it belongs] to the *indranīhava* and the *brāhmaṇaspatya* [stotras]. (ŚŚS 7.25, 11) Other than these, it belongs to those [stotras] based on the *bṛhatī* [meter]. (ŚŚS 7.25, 12)

Having recited the *bṛhatī*, having repeated the final foot twice and paused, and having performed the *praṇava* with the first half-verse of the next [verse], he repeats the second foot twice and pauses, and then performs the *praṇava* with the final half-verse.
These three are *bṛhatīs*. He takes up the final [foot] of the *kakubh*.
The *Indranihava* hymns are without a concluding verse (*astotriya*). (Soma: Āśir; Śastra:
General Remarks) And the hymns addressed to Bṛhaspati-pati are likewise [without a concluding verse].

(Soma: Āśir; Śastra: General Remarks) Having paused after two [verses], and having paused after another two, he pronounces the *praṇava* with one [verse] from among the *Paṅkti* verses. (Soma: Āśir; Śastra: General Remarks)
[The *praṇava* is applied] to the *triṣṭubh*, *jagatī*, and *akṣarapaṅkti* verses, as well as to the *dvipadā* verses. (Soma: Āśir-śastra;
General Remarks) The second and the fourth [verses] are accompanied by the *praṇava*. (Soma: Āśir-śastra;

General Remarks) However, in the case of five-footed (*pañcapada*) verses that occur within a sequence primarily consisting of *triṣṭubh* or *jagatī* verses, one should combine those two [footed units] where there is a [repeated] foot; there is no separation of one foot from another foot. (Soma: Āśir-śastra; General Remarks)
7.26. The two final [verses] are for the *apunar-pada* [recitation]. (General remarks on the *śastra* of the *āśvinā-śastra*) 7.26.

Having paused after two [padas], having paused after two, he pronounces the *praṇava* after two; this applies to the six *pada*s and the *punar-pada*s. 7.26. Having paused after two, he pronounces the *praṇava* after one; this applies to the *apunar-pada*s. Having paused after two, he pronounces it after one. (General remarks on the *śastra* of the *āśvinā-śastra*)

The *praṇava* (the syllable *oṃ*) should be uttered for the eight-syllabled [verse]. (Soma: Āśir; Śastra; General Remarks) Having made a pause after one [foot], he utters the *praṇava* after two of the seven feet, and having made a pause after two, [he utters it] after two [more]. In the first rounds (*paryāyas*) of the night, they repeat the first quarters of the *gāyatra* *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses. (Soma: Āśir; Śastra; General Remarks)

In the middle [stotras], [the verses] are in the middle [metres]. (ŚS 7.26.13) In the last [stotras], [the verses] are in the last [metres]. (ŚS 7.26.14) Or, the morning pressing may be performed half-verse by half-verse. (ŚS 7.26.15)
Excluding the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses as well as the *pragāthas*.
(Soma: Āśvina Śastra; General Remarks) The three-footed *gāyatrī*. (Soma: Āśvina Śastra; General Remarks) The *uṣṇih*. (Soma: Āśvina Śastra; General Remarks)
7.27. First, the *uṣṇih* (verse). /3/ (Soma: Āśvina Śastra:
General Remarks) 7.27. The *kakubh* (verse). /4/ (Soma: Āśvina Śastra: General Remarks) 7.27.
And the *virāj*, preceded by [the former]. /5/ (Soma: Āśvina Śastra: General Remarks)
The Virāj has four more syllables [than the Gāyatrī]. (Soma: Āśvina Śastra:
General Remarks) The Bṛhatī [has thirty-six syllables]. (Soma: Āśvina Śastra: General Remarks) The Sato-bṛhatī [has thirty-nine syllables]. (Soma: Āśvina Śastra: General Remarks)
Jagatī. (Soma: Āśir Śastra; General Remarks) Anuṣṭubh. (Soma: Āśir Śastra; General Remarks) And Triṣṭubh. (Soma: Āśir Śastra; General Remarks)
[The *stotriya*] consists of five verses.

(Soma: Āśvina-śastra; General Remarks) "Six, seven"—this refers to the *aticchandas* meters. (Soma: Āśvina-śastra; General Remarks) "Sa hi śardho na mārutam"—this consists of eight verses. (Soma: Āśvina-śastra; General Remarks)
There are two [verses] for the Dvipadā;
they generally consist of eight syllables each.
There is one Jagatī consisting of twelve syllables.
The third [verse] belongs to both the *uṣṇih* and the *bṛhatī* meters.
(18) The first and third [verses] belong to the *sato bṛhatī*.

The first [verse] is a *pura-uṣṇih*. (ŚS 7.27) The *triṣṭubh* and *virāj* [metres] consist of eleven syllables.
(ŚS 7.27) In the subsequent [verse], there are ten syllables. (ŚS 7.27)
They also call that the *akṣarapaṅkti*.
