A *jagatī* consists of six feet of eight syllables each. (Soma: Āśvina Śastra; General Remarks)

When there is a deficiency [of verses], it is *nicṛt* by one or two; when there is an excess, it is *bhurik*. Having completed the calculation by means of the quarter-verse portion, the verses to be added are equalized; they are made complete by that quarter-verse portion.
The Gāyatrī, Uṣṇih, Anuṣṭubh, Bṛhatī, Paṅkti, Triṣṭubh, and Jagatī—this is the sequence of the meters, beginning with twenty-four syllables and increasing by four syllables each time.
Just as for the midday pressing, so do they proceed after the midday pressing.
At the beginning of the third pressing, they perform the rite with the Āditya-graha cup.
"Obeisance to the Ādityas," it is said. (Soma: Āśvina; Third Pressing) "With the aid of the Ādityas," is the *puronuvākyā*. (Soma: Āśvina;
Third Pressing) "The Hotṛ shall sacrifice to the Ādityas," is the *praiṣa*. (Soma: Āśvina; Third Pressing)
He performs the sacrifice with the formula, "The Ādityas, Aditi. (Soma: Āśva;
Third Pressing) He does not look at the oblation, nor does he consume it. (Soma: Āśva;
Third Pressing) And so too in the case of the Sāvitra cup. (Soma: Āśva; Third Pressing)
When the *pavamāna* has been praised with the *ārbhava* [sāman], having performed the *paśu-karman* ending with the *manotā* and the *iḷā*, they proceed with the *savaniya-puroḍāśas* from this point.
(ŚŚS 8.1) "O Dhānās, at the third pressing! is the *puronuvākyā*.
(ŚŚS 8.2) "O Agni, at the third pressing! is the *sviṣṭakṛt* [offering]. (ŚŚS 8.2)
8.2. Here, "He has approached" (*iha upayataḥ*) is the *unnīyamānasūkta*. (Soma: Āśvina-śastra; Prasthita-homa) 8.2.
"The Hotṛ shall sacrifice to Indra for the third pressing" (*hotā yakṣad indraṃ tṛtīyasya savanasya*) is the *praiṣa* (direction). (Soma: Āśvina-śastra; Prasthita-homa) 8.2.
"O Indra, with the Ṛbhus, who possess strength" (*indra ṛbhubhir vājavadbhiḥ*)—with these words he recites the *yajyā*. (Soma: Āśvina-śastra; Prasthita-homa)

"O Indra and Varuṇa, drinkers of the pressed [juice]"—this is for the Maitrāvaruṇa. (ŚŚS 8.2.6) "And Indra [drinks] the Soma"—this is for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin. (ŚŚS 8.2.7) "May they carry you hither"—this is for the Potṛ. (ŚŚS 8.2.8)
The Neṣṭṛ [recites]: "As if with Amā" (ŚŚS 8.2). The Acchāvāka [recites]: "O Indra and Viṣṇu, drink" (ŚŚS 8.2).
The Āgnīdhra [recites]: "This hymn" (ŚŚS 8.2).

The rest is the same as for the morning pressing (prātaḥsavana). Having invoked the *iḷā* and consumed the *prasthita* cups, they place three balls (*piṇḍa*) each to the south of the *nārāśaṃsa* goblets that contain the mixture of the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*) and the parched grain (*parivāpa*), according to their respective goblets, with the formulas: "O Fathers, rejoice here; O Fathers, come to your portions according to your shares. At each ball, he says:
"To the god Savitṛ," when so directed.
"O God, he has come forth"—this is the *puronuvākyā*. (Soma: Āśvin;
Savitṛ-graha) "Let the Hotṛ worship the god Savitṛ"—this is the *praiṣa*. (Soma: Āśvin;

Savitṛ-graha) "He is the domestic god, the desirable Savitṛ, bestowing treasure upon the fathers for their life-span. Let him drink the Soma; the offerings have gladdened him. Even the wind finds delight in his ordinance. With these words he recites the *yajyā*. (Soma: Āśvin; Savitṛ-graha)

"O Adhvaryu, *śoṃsāvaḥ*!"—this is the *āhāva* at the beginning of the *śastra* during the third pressing when there is an *uktha*. (ŚŚS 8.3) The [formula] belonging to the morning pressing is used within the *śastra*. (ŚŚS 8.3) And it is also used from the *śloka* onwards. (ŚŚS 8.3)
“*tat savitur vṛṇīmahe* and *adyā no deva savitar*—these two triplets (*tṛca*) are the opening and the following verses (*pratipad* and *anucara*) for the Vaiśvadeva [śastra].

(ŚŚ 8.3) “*abhūd deva*... is the [verse] dedicated to Savitṛ. (ŚŚ 8.3) “With one and with ten, O self-existent one; with two and with twenty; with three and with thirty, you carry [the offerings], O Vāyu—with those teams (*niyut*), release them here. (ŚŚ 8.3)
"May Heaven and Earth, who increase the cosmic order through sacrifices," is the verse addressed to Heaven and Earth (dyāvāpṛthivīya).
(ŚŚS 8.3.11) "Let there be exhilaration in this response.
(ŚŚS 8.3.12) "Surūpakṛtnu... is one [verse]. (ŚŚS 8.3.13)
"takṣan ratham" is the [hymn] for the Ārbhava [Śastra].
(14) "ayam venaḥ," "yebhyaḥ mātā," and "evā pitre" are the one-footed verses (ekapātinyaḥ).
(15) Having recited the Nivid, one leaves the last verse of the Vaiśvadeva [Śastra], beginning with "ā no bhadrāḥ. (16)
The final verse is the concluding one (paridhānīyā). (17) He recites it foot by foot twice, and a third time by hemistichs.
(18) Having murmured the *ukthavīrya* formula, he performs the *yajyā* sacrifice with the words, "O All-Gods, hear this! (19) (Soma: Āśvinagraha; Sāvitragraha)

When addressed with "Recite the offering prayer for the ghee" (*ghṛtasya yaja*), he recites the *upāmśu* offering: "The ghee has been poured" (*ghṛtam mimikṣe*). (Soma: Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 8.4; Saumya Caru) When addressed with "Recite the offering prayer for the Saumya [oblation]" (*saumyasya yaja*), he recites: "O Soma, with the fathers... (*tvam soma pitṛbhiḥ...*). (Soma: Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 8.4;

Saumya Caru) When addressed with "Recite the offering prayer for the ghee" (*ghṛtasya yaja*), he recites the *upāmśu* offering: "Stride out widely, O Viṣṇu; make wide room for our dwelling. O you whose source is ghee, drink the ghee; further and further extend the lord of the sacrifice. (Soma: Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 8.4; Saumya Caru)
There is an option regarding the purification. (Soma: Āśvina;
Saumya Caru) The Hotṛ, having looked at the offering for Soma, touches clarified butter with his two fingers. (Soma: Āśvina;
Saumya Caru) With the formula, "Thou art the protector of the eye; protect my eye," he rubs his two eyes. (Soma: Āśvina; Saumya Caru)
When [the Adhvaryu] has been addressed with, "O Agnīdh, sacrifice for the Pātnīvata," he sacrifices silently with the verse, "With these, O Agni, on the same chariot...
(RV 3.4.9). Having taken the cup without consuming it, having entered the Sadas by the eastern door, and having sat down close to the Neṣṭṛ from the north... (Śrautasūtra 8.5).
Or [he may drink] from his lap. (Soma: Āśir;
Pātnīvata-graha) Having said, "O Neṣṭṛ, invite [the gods]," (Soma: Āśir;
Pātnīvata-graha) and having consumed [the portion] and sipped water, (Soma: Āśir; Pātnīvata-graha) 5–6.
Having returned from where he went (ŚS 8.5).

(Soma: Āśir; Pātnīvata cup) The Yajñāyajñīya is the stotra for the Āgnimāruta Śastra. (Soma: Āśir; Āgnimāruta Śastra) "Vaiśvānarāya pṛthupājase" is the Vaiśvānara hymn. (Soma: Āśir; Āgnimāruta Śastra)
"Come to us, O Father"—this is one verse. (Soma: Āśir;
Āgnimāruta Śastra) "O you of great power"—this is the Marut hymn. (Soma: Āśir;
Āgnimāruta Śastra) "Yajñā yajñā vo agnaye" and "Devo vo draviṇodāḥ"—these are the Stotriya and Anurūpa Pragāthas for the Yajñāyajñīya. (Soma: Āśir; Āgnimāruta Śastra)
"May he be more powerful"—this is the *jātavedasīya* hymn. (Soma: Āśir;
Āgnimāruta Śastra) The three verses beginning with "O Waters, you indeed... (āpo hi ṣṭhā). (Soma: Āśir;
Āgnimāruta Śastra) "And may Ahi Budhnya hear us"—this is one verse. (Soma: Āśir; Āgnimāruta Śastra)

"O wives of the gods," two verses. (Soma: Āśvina; Āgnimāruta Śastra) "I invoke Rākā," two verses. (Soma: Āśvina; Āgnimāruta Śastra) "He found skill," three Akṣarapaṅkti verses. (Soma: Āśvina; Āgnimāruta Śastra)
"Let the paternal [somas] arise"—these three [verses] belong to the Pitṛs.
(ŚŚS 8.6.12) "O Yama, with Mātali, with the Kavyas, with the Aṅgirases"—these [verses] belong to Yama. (ŚŚS 8.6.13) The three [verses] beginning with "svāduṣkiliya. (ŚŚS 8.6.14)
"May he be rich in cattle; let him accept these [gifts]"—this is the *pratigara*.
(ŚŚS 8.6.15) "The two by whose might... and "Of Viṣṇu indeed... while reciting "Stretching out the thread"—these are the *ekapātinī* verses.

(ŚŚS 8.6.16) Having concluded with "Thus indeed may Indra the Maghavan... and having murmured the *ukthavīrya*, he performs the *yajyā* with "O Agni, together with the Maruts who shine forth... (ŚŚS 8.6.17)
The first *nivid* belongs to the *marutvatīya* [śastra]; (Soma: Āśv;
General Remarks) the second belongs to the *niṣkevalya*; (Soma: Āśv; General Remarks) and those beginning with the third belong to the *vaiśvadeva* and the *āgnimāruta*. (Soma: Āśv; General Remarks)
The *nivid* formulas for the *ṣoḍaśin* [cup] are the best. (Soma: Āśvina;
General Remarks) There are as many *nivid*s as there are hymns (*sūkta*s). (Soma: Āśvina; General Remarks) Before each hymn, there is an *āhāva* call. (Soma: Āśvina; General Remarks)
The *nivid*s and the *nivids*. (Soma: Āśv.
General Remarks) One for each [verse] that falls singly. (Soma: Āśv.
General Remarks) And for the *paridhānīyā* [concluding verse]. (Soma: Āśv. General Remarks)

In the Vaiśvadeva [śastra], [the chanting] is performed on the *pratipad* and its *anucara*; (Soma: Āśv; General Remarks) In the Āgnimāruta [śastra], [the chanting] is performed on the *stotriya* and its *anurūpa*; (Soma: Āśv; General Remarks) [The chanting] is performed on the verses beginning with "āpo hi ṣṭha"; (Soma: Āśv; General Remarks)

[The verses] of the wives of the gods (devānām patnī). 13. (General remarks on the Soma-āśīḥ) [The verse] of Rākā. 14. (General remarks on the Soma-āśīḥ) [The verses] of the Akṣarapaṅkti meters. 15. (General remarks on the Soma-āśīḥ)
Of the Paitrīṇas; (Soma Āṣ:
General Remarks) of the Yāmīs;
and of the Svāduṣkilīyas. 16–18. (Soma Āṣ: General Remarks)
The *vaiśvadeva* chant has its weapons extended.
(ŚŚS 8.7) The *āgnimāruta* chant has [its weapons] brought close, with the exception of the *āpo hi ṣṭhā* verses. (ŚŚS 8.7)

Having placed the *soma* cups in the waters and having performed the animal ritual beginning with the *anuyāja* offerings and ending with the *śamyu*, they proceed with the *hāriyojana* cup. (Soma: Āśv; General Remarks) "Stand up for the sake of the good [world]" (*tiṣṭhā sukam*) is the invitatory verse (*puronuvākyā*). (Soma: Āśv; Hāriyojana Cup) "The roasted grains (*dhānāḥ*) of the *somas*, O Indra! (*dhānāḥ somānām indra*)—this is the direction (*praiṣa*). (Soma: Āśv; Hāriyojana Cup)
"yunajmi tvā" (I yoke you) is the *yājyā* verse. (Soma: Āśvina;

Hāriyojana Graha) "dhānāḥ somānām agne vīhi" (O Agni, partake of the roasted grains of the Soma-libations) is the *anuvaṣaṭkāra*. (Soma: Āśvina; Hāriyojana Graha) Or alternatively, "somasya agne" (of the Soma, O Agni). (Soma: Āśvina; Hāriyojana Graha)

"O divine Soma, you who are washed in the waters, whose wisdom is known by men, praised with hymns, recited with *ukthas*, and offered with *yajus* formulas—of that portion of yours which is the gain of horses and the gain of cattle, being invited, I, invited, partake. Having thus partaken of the *prāṇa-bhakṣas* (breath-portions), they distribute the parched grains (*dhānās*).
(ŚŚS 8.8) The Hotṛ should seek to obtain the largest portion. (ŚŚS 8.8)
Having looked at the *dhiṣṇya* hearths with the verse, "As you have come, O Vasus... (VS 8.8), they proceed from the north of the *āgnīdhrīya* fire toward the *āhavanīya*.

With the formulas, "Bhūḥ! Bhuvah! Svaḥ! Svāhā! and "O Agni, as such, be our nearest [friend]... (VS 5.4), "O Agni, [protect us] from Varuṇa... (VS 5.5), and "O Mitra and Varuṇa... (VS 5.6), they offer the expiatory oblations (*prāyaścittāhutīḥ*) into the *āgnīdhrīya* fire. (ŚŚS 8.8.9–10)

"Fill us with offspring and cattle; fill us! Having thus spoken, they place parched grains at the edge of the ashes of the Āhavanīya fire and add five wood-shavings each. 11. (Soma: Āṣ: Prāyaścitti, etc.)

"You are the expiation for sin committed by oneself; you are the expiation for sin committed against men; you are the expiation for sin committed against the ancestors; you are the expiation for sin committed against the gods; whatever sin I have committed knowingly and whatever I have committed unknowingly—you are the expiation for all that. (Soma: Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, Prāyaścitti section)

Turning to the left, they enter by the northern side of the Āhavanīya fire. Having sat down behind the waters according to their respective cups (*camasa*), and having placed the strainers (*pavitra*) therein, they perform the ritual action with the formula: "The waters have united with the waters; the plants with their sap. Let the wealthy ones be mixed with the moving ones; let the honey-sweet ones be mixed with the honey-sweet ones. (ŚŚS 8.9.2) "We have been invited together," [they say]. (ŚŚS 8.9.3)
"O divine Soma, of you who are shaken in the waters, of that portion which knows the mind, which wins horses and wins cattle—of you, being invited, I, being invited, partake.
Having thus partaken of the breath-portions (*prāṇabhakṣa*), he pours [the remains] eastward or northward with the verse, "Toward this [place], O you two, by whose power... (RV 10.9.7).
Then he consecrates them with the formula, "Into the ocean, O you... (RV 10.9.8). ŚŚS 8.9.4–6. (Soma: Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra; Prāyaścitti, etc.)
With the four verses beginning with *śaṃ no devīr*, he should touch his chest.
(ŚŚS 8.9) The touching of the breaths and the wiping of the mouth are the same [as previously described].
(ŚŚS 8.9) Turning to the right, he should consume curds at the Āgnīdhrīya fire according to the procedure for consuming curds. (ŚŚS 8.9)
Having completed the *patnīsaṃyāja* offerings and once the *samiṣṭayajus* oblations have been offered, he proceeds to the purificatory bath (*avabhṛtha*).

"May my sensory power return to me; may my self, my wealth, and my Brahmanical luster return. May the fires on their hearths remain right here, each in its proper place. Having thus looked at the hearth-fires, the sacrificer should look at the officiating priests either at this point or when the *anūbandhyā* sacrifice has been concluded.
"Both are young poets; by the law of truth, we two lords of the law of truth—let us sever our bonds of friendship.

Thus [he says]. (Soma: Āś: Āvabhṛtha) "For wide indeed is the King... with this [verse], they proceed together. (Soma: Āś: Āvabhṛtha) All chant the *nidhana* finale of the *sāman*. (Soma: Āś: Āvabhṛtha)
"Obeisance to Varuṇa; the noose of Varuṇa is placed upon me"—having recited this, he places his foot in the water. (ŚŚS 8.10) The sacrifice is dedicated to Varuṇa.
(ŚŚS 8.11) It is a modification of the Full Moon sacrifice. (ŚŚS 8.11)
"O Agni, in the waters; O Soma, in the waters for me"—these two [verses] contain the word "waters.
Standing, he performs the sacrifice. "Lift up the highest," "Release us from Varuṇa's bond. (The *avabhṛtha*. ŚŚS 8.11.3–5.
"O Agni, you are our nearest; O Agni, you who know [the way], [protect us] from Varuṇa"—with these words he addresses Agni and Varuṇa.
(6) He does not recite the *nigada* formula. (7) Or he may recite it. (8) (Soma: Āśvina-Śastra; Avabhṛtha)
He performs the *prayāja* and *anuyāja* offerings excluding the *barhis*. (Soma:
Āśvamedha, Avabhṛtha) The sequence begins with the *prayāja* and ends with the *anuyāja*.
Or, it may end with the *sviṣṭakṛt*. (Soma: Āśvamedha, Avabhṛtha)
"Either omitting the two *ājyabhāga* offerings and the two *anuyāja* offerings.

(ŚŚS 8.11) "With that by which you made the two women, with which you touched the *surā*, with which you sprinkled the axle, and with that glory of yours, O Aśvins, by which [you overspread] this great earth—with that, sprinkle me! With these words, the *hotṛ* sprinkles himself.
(ŚŚS 8.11) "With a gracious eye, I, a mortal, go toward my home. Saying this, the sacrificer returns. (ŚŚS 8.11)

"May Pūṣan, even though he has given a thousand as sacrificial fees, sit down here. Having sat down thus, he places two fuel-sticks on the Āhavanīya fire: the first with the formula "Thou art the fuel of the gods," and the second silently. (15) [Soma: Āś: Āvabhṛtha] The wife [places a stick] silently on the Gārhapatya fire.
(16) [Soma: Āś: Āvabhṛtha] The Udayanīyā offering is explained by the Prāyaṇīyā offering. (1) [Soma: Āś: Udayanīya-iṣṭi]
8.12. There is a transposition of the *yājyā* and *puronuvākyā* verses, with the exception of those for the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering. (Soma: Āṣ; Udayanīya-iṣṭi) 8.12.
He performs the sacrifice to Pathyā Svasti as the fourth [deity]. (Soma: Āṣ; Udayanīya-iṣṭi) 8.12.
Savitṛ is the third. (Soma: Āṣ; Udayanīya-iṣṭi)
And a barren cow dedicated to Mitra and Varuṇa is to be bound as the Anubandhyā sacrifice.
Or there may be a dish of curdled milk (payasyā).
The invitatory verses (puronuvākyās) are: "O Mitra and Varuṇa, come hither," "That [is] yours, O Mitra and Varuṇa," and "Om, O Mitra and Varuṇa. (Śrauta Sūtra 8.12)
"yuvam vastrāṇi yad bāṃhiṣṭham" and "pra bāhavaḥ" are the *yājyās*.
(ŚŚS 8.12) From the *dīkṣaṇīyā* sacrifice up until the conclusion of the *ānubandhyā*, he does not cause the wife to recite [the formulas] at the altar (*veda*), nor does he strew [grass].
(ŚŚS 8.12) At the *ānubandhyā*, having caused her to recite [the formulas], he strews [grass] in front of the *āgnīdhrīya* hearth. (ŚŚS 8.12)
Do not harm the waters, do not harm the plants; you are pain (*śuc*). May that pain of yours reach him whom we hate.
O King Varuṇa, from every station release us! From whatever we have sworn by the waters, by the inviolable [cow], or by Varuṇa—O Varuṇa, from that release us!

Having performed the worship with the *hṛdaya-śūla* mantra, and having touched water with the words, "May the waters and plants be friendly to us," they step out toward the south with the words, "May they be unfriendly to him who hates us and whom we hate.
(ŚŚS 8.12) Alternatively, the rite begins with the *ājya-bhāga* offerings up to the *payasyā*. (ŚŚS 8.12) It is a modification of the New Moon sacrifice (*amāvāsyā*). (ŚŚS 8.12)
The *iḷā* ends with the word *anigada*.
(ŚŚS 8.12) Having gone northward and performed the full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*) with a verse addressed to Viṣṇu, he performs the concluding sacrifice (*udavasānīyā*).
(ŚŚS 8.13) This is an offering to Agni. (ŚŚS 8.13)

It is a modification of the Full Moon sacrifice. (Soma: Āśv: Udavasānīya-iṣṭi) Those [offerings] which are at the re-establishment of the fires belong to the *havis* and the *sviṣṭakṛt*. (Soma: Āśv: Udavasānīya-iṣṭi) The sacrifice pertaining to the re-establishment of the fires consists of five potsherds. (Soma: Āśv: Udavasānīya-iṣṭi)

When [the fire] has been established, he performs the evening *agnihotra* offering. (ŚŚS 8.13) With a low voice, he performs the morning pressing (*prātaḥsavana*). (ŚŚS 8.14) The *prauga-śastra* is performed at a louder pitch than the *ājya-śastra*. (ŚŚS 8.14)
With the middle [pitch] he performs the midday pressing. (Soma: Āś:

General Remarks) The Marutvatīya and Niṣkevalya [stotras] are performed at a higher pitch. (Soma: Āś: General Remarks) With the highest [pitch] he performs the third pressing. (Soma: Āś: General Remarks)
The *āgnimāruta* [śastra] is indeed louder than the *vaiśvadeva*.

(Soma: Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 8.14) Or else, the midday pressing is performed with the highest [pitch]. (Soma: Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 8.14) The third pressing is performed with a soft [pitch]. (Soma: Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 8.14)
Or [he may recite] with the middle [tone].
(ŚŚS 8.14) He restrains his speech from the moment he gives a direction until its conclusion.
(ŚŚS 8.15) And [he restrains his speech] from the call (*āhāva*) until the secondary *vaṣaṭ*-utterance (*anuvaṣaṭkāra*). (ŚŚS 8.15)

The Brahman priest [performs his duties] during the Prātar-anuvāka; (Soma: Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra, Brahmatva in Soma) he does so until the consumption [of the soma], and from the consumption until the impulse for the stotra; (Soma: Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra, Brahmatva in Soma) and from the impulse until the anuvaṣaṭkāra. (Soma: Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra, Brahmatva in Soma) 8.15.3–5.

Having heard the *atipraiṣa* up to the point of the carrying away of the *vasatīvarī* waters; (ŚŚS 8.15). With the verses "That drop of thine which falls" and "The drop has fallen," there is an oblation for the droplets prior to the *pavamāna* chants; (ŚŚS 8.15).
And he follows after those who are moving; (ŚŚS 8.15).
And [the Maitrāvaruṇa is also his assistant].
(ŚŚ 8.15.9) And at the piling of the fire-altar, when the fire is being led forward, he mutters the *Apratiratha* hymn:
(ŚŚ 8.15.10) "O Aśvins, come hither from all directions, bringing all the gods; drink of the sweet, consecrated *gharma* with the cry of *svāhā*! Thus he follows the *mahāvīra* vessel. (ŚŚ 8.15.11)
"O Aśvins, drink the *gharma* that warms the heart, with your daily aids! Homage to the weaver and to Heaven and Earth!"—thus at the *vaṣaṭ*-call.
(ŚŚS 8.15) "The two Aśvins have drunk the *gharma*; Heaven and Earth have approved it. May the gifts be right here!"—thus at the secondary *vaṣaṭ*-call.
(ŚŚS 8.15) That which is not specifically prescribed is the same [as the preceding]. (ŚŚS 8.15)
Thus concludes the *brahman* ritual action at the *soma* sacrifice.

"May Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, drink of the *soma*. Praised by the Maruts, surrounded by the host of Maruts, strengthened by the Maruts, and having the Maruts as his friends—he whom the gods rejoiced in following, in the crossing of waters, in the conquest of Vṛtra, in the slaying of Śambara, and in the search for cattle—him who praises with secret steps. (These are the *ṇivids* for the *marutvatīya* cup.)

In the furthest distance, he slew Vṛtra and released the waters together with the might of the Maruts; then the prayers increased him, whose powers are unassailable by force. (1b) (Soma: Āṣ: ṇivids for the Marutvatīya)

Bringing offerings to the gods, together with his friends, the Maruts—may Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, hear us here; may he drink of the Soma here. May the god favor this invocation of the gods with divine wisdom. May he favor this sacred formulation (*brahman*), may he favor this ruling power (*kṣatra*), and may he favor this sacrificer who presses the Soma. (1c) May the Wondrous One, with his wondrous aids, hear our prayers; may he come hither with his protection. (1d) (Soma: Āśir; Nivid for the Marutvatīya)
Now, the *uktha-vīrya* (the power of the hymn).
"Thy form, the corresponding form, the matching form, the beautiful form—here is the *upayaja* offering. For thee who art listening, O Indra, this hymn has been recited.

May the god Indra drink the soma. He is the most heroic among those born once; the strongest among those born many times. He is the rider of the bay horses; the leader of the speckled ones; the wielder of the thunderbolt; the breaker of forts.

The breaker of forts; the leader of waters; the leader of heroes; the slayer from afar whose fame is wide-reaching; the creator of the highest limits, possessed of wondrous power; having been here as a god, O Uśan, may Indra the god hear us here and drink the Soma here. "O God, forward this [prayer]"—the rest is the same. (Soma: Āś;
Ṇivids for the Niṣkevalya) Now follows the *ukthavīrya*. (Soma: Āś; Ṇivids for the Niṣkevalya)

"You are the sovereign, you are the self-ruler, you are the far-shining, you are the king, you are the overcomer; may we overcome him whom we hate. For you, who do not hear [the enemy], this hymn has been recited for Indra. (Soma: Āśir; Nivid for the Niṣkevalya)

May the god Savitṛ exhilarate himself with Soma—he of the golden hands, the fair tongue, the beautiful arms, and the lovely fingers; he who thrice a day offers the true libation; he who has impelled the two treasuries of wealth; he who delights in both when they are urged to give. I have impelled the most excellent gift of Savitṛ: the milch-cow that yields milk, and the draft-ox that carries the load. (ŚS 8.18)

The swift steed, the victorious one standing in the chariot, the woman who is the fulfiller of the city, the youthful man fit for the assembly—may the god Savitṛ impel away disease and away the curse of evil speech. May he hear us here; may he rejoice here in Soma. "O God, forward this [song]... and so on, as before. (Soma: Āśvin-Ṛtu-nivid for Vaiśvadeva)

May Heaven and Earth, the Father and the Mother, rejoice in Soma. May the Cow and the Bull, the Blessed One and the Support, the one of good seed and the well-milking, the source of happiness and the source of delight, the full of vigor and the full of milk—may Heaven and Earth hear us here; may they rejoice in Soma here. (Soma: Āśvin-Śastra; Nivid for the Vaiśvadeva)

May these two goddesses protect this invocation to the gods with divine wisdom. May they protect this *brahman* (spiritual power), may they protect this *kṣatra* (secular power). May they protect this pressing sacrificer with their wondrous aids. O you who are renowned, come to our prayers with your help! 1b. (Soma: Āśvin-śastra; Nivid for the Vaiśvadeva)

The *Ṛbhus*, the gods, have become exhilarated by Soma. Having performed their work with skillful hands, they are well-formed through their craft. They are most blessed, most wealthy, most tranquil through peace, and most powerful through power. They who fashioned the all-impelling, all-shaped cow—they fashioned the cow; she became the possessor of every form. (Soma: Āśvin-śastra; *ṇivids* for the Vaiśvadeva)

Awakening together with their younger brothers, they rejoiced; they yoked the two bay steeds, *harī*, to go toward the gods. In the course of a year, the skillful ones came to their sacrificial portion. The *Ṛbhus* became gods here; they have heard [our call] here and shall delight in the soma. O gods, may you favor this invocation of the gods with divine thought. (Soma: Āśvin-śastra, *ṇivids* for the Vaiśvadeva)

Forward this priesthood, forward this nobility! May they protect this sacrificer who presses the Soma, with their various aids, O various ones! May the glorious ones come hither with their help, listening to our prayers.

(ŚS 8.20) May all the gods, the Vaiśvānaras, rejoice in the Soma—great ones, mighty, possessing cooked food, not neglecting the guest, united, bringing the cooked offerings—who have established themselves in both heaven and earth, and in the waters and the sun. (ŚS 8.21)
Brahman and Kṣatra; the sacrificial grass and the altar; the sacrifice and the wide mid-air; those whose self is the wind, whose messenger is Agni—those who are three times eleven.
(1b) Three and thirty; three and three hundred; three and three thousand; so many in their rising, so many in their settling; so many are the wives. (1c)

So many are the Gnas; so many are the Abhiṣācas; so many are the Rātiṣācas. Even more than these, O gods, are you. May no god deceive you; may I not deceive you; I summon you, the life-force. "May all the gods hear this here; may they rejoice here in the Soma"—this is the same as the verse beginning with *pra imām devāḥ*. (Soma: Āśir; Nivids for Vaiśvadeva) Now follows the *ukthavīrya*. (Soma: Āśir; Nivids for Vaiśvadeva)

You are the past, you are the future, you are the manifested, you are the abundant; you are the existent, you are the eye, you are vigor, you are auspiciousness. For the sake of sacred learning, I have spoken this hymn to you—for Indra, for the gods.

Agni Vaiśvānara has become exhilarated by Soma; he is the kindler of all the gods, the imperishable divine light. He who shines for the people and for the wise, flashing forth in the ancient days, ageless at the face of the dawns. *Śaṅkhāyana Śrautasūtra 8.21–22* (Soma: Āśir; Nivids for Vaiśvadeva and Āgnimāruta)

He who shines upon the sky, upon the earth, and across the wide mid-air—may that Agni Vaiśvānara, worthy of sacrifice, grant us protection with his light. May he hear us here; may he rejoice in the Soma here. "O God, forward this [prayer]... and so on, as before. (Soma: Āśvin-Śastra; Niṣkevalya-Śastra; Nivid for the Āgnimāruta).

The Maruts, the gods, have exhilarated themselves with Soma; they are well-praising with fine hymns, possessing lofty strength, with the *arka* as their praise, clothed in rain from the clouds, brilliant, sons of Pṛśni, radiant, with golden girths.

(1a) The powerful ones, whose gifts are to be celebrated, heroes with unassailable chariots—the Maruts, the gods—have heard us here; here they have exhilarated themselves with Soma. "O gods, forward this [prayer]... and so on, as before. (1b)

Agni Jātavedas, exhilarated by Soma—of beautiful aspect, of wondrous radiance; the householder who never departs, visible even through the darkness; to whom the clarified butter is offered, worthy of praise; whose armor is thick, who has spread the sacrifice; who advances against his enemies as an unconquered victor—O Agni Jātavedas, bestow upon us splendor and overwhelming power! (1a) (Soma: Āṣ: Ṇivids for the Āgnimāruta)

"Stuśo astuśah; protect us from distress, O kindler [of the fire]. May Agni Jātavedas hear us here; may he rejoice here in the Soma. "O God, this [hymn]... and so on, as before. (Soma: Āśvin-Śastra; Nivids for the Āgnimāruta). Now follows the *ukthavīrya*. (Soma: Āśvin-Śastra; Nivids for the Āgnimāruta)

Thou art brilliance; thou art boldness; thou art courageous; thou art impetuous; thou art support; thou art sustenance; thou art the firm; thou art the steadfast. For the sake of hearing thee, it has been spoken: an *uktha* for Indra, for the gods. (Soma: Āśvin-śastra; Nivids for the Āgnimāruta)

In the exhilaration of this Soma, O singer, Indra shall rejoice. In the exhilaration of this, O singer, Indra slew the serpent. In the exhilaration of this, O singer, Indra slew Vṛtra. In the exhilaration of this, O singer, Indra propped up the sky and spread out the earth. In the exhilaration of this, O singer, Indra extended the mid-air and reached the sun with heavenly rays. In the exhilaration of this, O singer, Indra extended the noble race and struck down the Dāsa race. (1a) (Soma: Āṣ: Nivids for the Ṣoḍaśin)

In the exhilaration of this [Soma], O singer, Indra caused the waters that were not yet swollen to swell; he quickened those that were slow. In the exhilaration of this, O singer, Indra stilled the agitated mountains as they were puffing like seers. In the exhilaration of this, O singer, Indra set in motion the rush of the waters. In the exhilaration of this, O singer, Indra heard here from where he stood upon the mountain. In the exhilaration of this, O singer, Indra heard here; here he shall delight in the Soma. To Agni Gṛhapati (the Lord of the House), to Soma Vanaspati (the Lord of the Forest), to Savitṛ Satyaprasava (the Impeller of True Procreation), to Rudra Paśupati (the Lord of Animals), to Bṛhaspati Vācaspati (the Lord of Speech), to Indra Jyeṣṭha (the Eldest), to Mitra Satya (the Truthful One), and to Varuṇa Dharmapati (the Lord of Dharma). Agni is the Hotṛ, the Lord of the House, the bearer of oblations; Agni, who does not neglect the Viśvedevas; we [invoke] Indra for the great prize, for our wide [space].

To Agni of the spring, of the *gāyatrī* metre, of the *trivṛt* stoma, and of the *rathantara* sāman; to Indra of the summer, of the *triṣṭubh* metre, of the *pañcadaśa* stoma, and of the *bṛhat* sāman; to the Viśvedevas of the rainy season, of the *jagatī* metre, of the *saptadaśa* stoma, and of the *vairūpa* sāman; to Mitra and Varuṇa of the autumn, of the *anuṣṭubh* metre, of the *ekaviṃśa* stoma, and of the *vairāja* sāman; to Bṛhaspati of the winter, of the *paṅkti* metre, of the *triṇava* stoma, and of the *śakvara* sāman; to Savitṛ of the cool season, of the *aticchandas* metre, and of the *trayastrimśa* stoma.

(ŚŚ 10.8.6) "Rich for us," "O wealthy one," and "O wealthy one"—these are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* for the *raivata* [śastra].
(ŚŚ 10.8.7) "Let us not think of anything else"—this is the *sāmagātha*. (ŚŚ 10.8.8)
"O Indra, come hither; indeed, come now toward us with thy bay steeds"—these three verses constitute the *niṣkevalya* [śastra].
(ŚŚS 10.8.9) "Towards that god... is the opening verse (*pratipad*) of the *vaiśvadeva* [śastra].

(ŚŚS 10.8.10) Of this [verse], having divided it with a sixteen-syllable [pāda], having pronounced the *praṇava* with an eighteen-syllable [pāda], having paused with a fifteen-syllable [pāda], [and] with a fifteen-syllable [pāda]. (ŚŚS 10.8.11)
For this [day], the *uttara* (subsequent) verses are "asya hi sva-yaśastaram" and so forth. (12) The *anucara* (following verse) is from the third day.

(13) In the *vaiśvadeva* [śastra], the modification is as follows: having recited the verses beginning with "ud u sya devaḥ savitā savāya," "katarā pūrvā," "kim u śreṣṭhā," and "idam itthā," one leaves aside the final portion; then, having recited the verses beginning with "ye yajñena," one recites the remaining portions. (14)

And at the end of the Vaiśvadeva [śastras], one performs the three verses beginning with "Svasti no mimītām."
"tatam ma" is the Ārbhava [Śastra] for the fourth day. (18) "pra yantu vājāḥ"—these three [verses] are at the end of the Māruta [Śastra].

For one who has the *bṛhat* as the *pṛṣṭha*, the *rathantara* as the *pṛṣṭha*, the *upāṃśu* as the *pṛṣṭha*, the *ārbhava* as the *pṛṣṭha*, the *tanū* as the *pṛṣṭha*, or whose *stoma* follows the *chandoruc* [pattern], the *stotriyas*, *anurūpas*, and *sāmapragāthas* are determined according to the authority of the *chandogas*. (ŚŚS 10.8.21) The rest is the same as in the *samūḷha* [arrangement]. (ŚŚS 10.8.22) It is likewise in the *viśvajit*. (ŚŚS 10.8.23)
The seventh day has the Caturviṃśa-stoma, the Bṛhat-pṛṣṭha, and both Sāmans. (Soma: Daśarātra:
Seventh Day of the Ten-Day Period) "pra vaḥ śukrāya" is the Ājya [Śastra]. (Soma: Daśarātra:
Seventh Day of the Ten-Day Period) The Praüga [Śastra] is in the Triṣṭubh metre. (Soma: Daśarātra: Seventh Day of the Ten-Day Period)

"pra vīrayā te satyena," "ud vām cakṣur ā gomata," "no deva pra vo yajñeṣu," and "pra codasā"—these are the *prauga* triplets. (ŚŚS 10.9) Those which are the opening (*pratipad*) and following (*anucara*) verses of the first three-day period (*tryaha*), together with those addressed to Bṛhaspati (*brāhmaṇaspatya*), are used in the *chandome* days, in the *svarasāman* days, and in the *abhiplava* six-day periods. (ŚŚS 10.9)
From the first [day], [the chant] of the first day of the Chāndomika [period];
from the second, that of the second;

Thus is the first three-day period consisting of *abhiplava* days.
(Soma: Daśarātra: Seventh day of the ten-day period) Thus is the subsequent [three-day period]. (Soma: Daśarātra:
Seventh day of the ten-day period) Thus are the *svarasāman* days. (Soma: Daśarātra: Seventh day of the ten-day period)

"By what [means], O auspicious one? and "This well-sought [one]"—these are for the Marutvatīya [śastra]. (12) "Him indeed, praise! and "Toward that ram"—these are for the Niṣkevalya [śastra]. (13) One should not recite the *yoni* verse of the Kaṇvarathantara [sāman]. (14)

Those [verses] which are the *pratipad* and *anucara* of the *vaiśvadeva* on the first two days are used in the *chandomeya* and the *abhiplava* [six-day periods]. (ŚŚS 10.9) The modifications for the *vaiśvadeva* are: the three triplets beginning with *tat savitur vareṇyam*, *pretām yajñasya śamitāram*, and *ayaṃ devāya*; the five verses beginning with *ṛjunītī*; and the three verses beginning with *yāhi vanasā saha* and *omāsaś carṣaṇidhṛtaḥ*. (ŚŚS 10.9)
May Vaiśvānara come for our protection; may Vaiśvānara come to this sacrifice with joy, O Agni, along with the hymn as your vehicle.

(17a) Vaiśvānara generated the *stoma* and the sacrifice of the Aṅgirases; he has brought celestial splendor upon them. With the verses beginning "When you [sing] the *triṣṭubh*" and "Fifteen," or "Nine," and "Singing unto you," [the *ṛc*s] are used in the *āgnimāruta* [śastra]. (17b)

The eighth day has the Catuścatvāriṃśa-stoma and the Rathantara-pṛṣṭha. (Soma: Daśarātra: Eighth Day of the Ten-Day Period) "O Agni, you, the god... is the Ājya [Śastra]. (Soma: Daśarātra: Eighth Day of the Ten-Day Period) The Praüga [Śastra] is in the Triṣṭubh metre. (Soma: Daśarātra: Eighth Day of the Ten-Day Period)

The *prauga* triplets are: *kuvid aṅga*, the first [verse] of the third [turn]; *ā vāyo bhūṣa* and one [verse] of *yāvattaraḥ*; *prati vām sūra udite*; *apa svasuḥ ayam somaḥ*; *pra brahmāṇa uta syā naḥ sarasvatī juṣāṇā*. (Soma: Daśarātra: Eighth Day of the Ten-Day Period)

"Great is Indra, like a man," "These [songs] for you," "Of the most frequent one," "Where is this hero?"—in all [these stanzas], excluding the last four, [one recites]. "Even great is he; him, heaven and earth... is the Marutvatīya hymn.

(ŚŚS 10.10) "You are great, O Indra," "For you indeed," "You are great, O Indra, who [performed] the unprecedented," "This fame of yours," "This prayer of yours"—these are the Niṣkevalya hymn. (ŚŚS 10.10)

"śśṣ10.10. *hiraṇyapāṇim ūtaye*—these four [verses]; *mahī dyauḥ*, *yuvānā pitarā*—these two triplets; *devānām idam*, *imā nu kam*, *viśve devā ṛtāvṛdhaḥ*—these three. Thus is the modification for the Vaiśvadeva [śastra]. (Soma: Daśarātra: Eighth day of the Ten-day Period)

"Vaiśvānara Agni has generated for us a new hymn, increasing upon the earth with his might. O bull, purifier, shine forth, O Vaiśvānara Agni, resplendent, invoked by the Jamadagnis. "The observer of Truth, Vaiśvānara—when indeed now? When [is he] dear? Your envoy, the all-knowing"—this is used in the *agni-māruta* [śastra]. (Soma: Daśarātra:
Eighth day of the Ten-day Period) "The forty-eighth *stoma*, with the *bṛhat-sāman* as the *pṛṣṭha*-laud, is the ninth [day]. (Soma: Daśarātra: Ninth day of the Ten-day Period)
"Aganma mahāsomasya mā tavasam" is the *ājya* [śastra];
or it may be the former [of the two]. The *prauga* is in the *triṣṭubh* meter.

"Ā vāyo bhūṣa" is the first [verse]; "arvanto na śravasaḥ," "divi kṣayantā viśvavārāḥ," "indram naro," "ūrdhvo agniḥ," and "pra kṣodasā" are the *prauga* triplets for the third and the last [days]. (ŚŚS 10.11) "try aryamā," "indro rathāya," "tiṣṭhā harī," "gāyat sāma," and "pra mandine" constitute the *marutvatīya* [śastra] for the ninth day of the ten-day period. (ŚŚS 10.11)

"May he come to us as one who is true; that power of yours, O Indra, which is all-conquering—that indeed have I become. This is the *niṣkevalya* [śastra]. (Soma: Daśarātra: Ninth Day of the Ten-Day Period)

The two triplets *abhi tvā deva*, *pra vām mahi dyāvāpṛthivī*, and *indra iṣe*; the two verses *te no ratnāni*; the five hymns beginning with *agniḥ ukthe* for the mind; excluding the penultimate verse of the hymn *ye triṃśati*; the single verse *na hi vaḥ asty arbhakaḥ*; the four verses *aśarmā*; the single verse *babhruḥ ekaḥ* or *manu-pravalhaḥ*; and the triplet *viśve devāsa ā gata*—these constitute the modification (*vikāra*) for the Vaiśvadeva [śastra] in the ninth day of the ten-day period.

In the vault of heaven, Agni Vaiśvānara shone forth, great; with his light he dispels the darkness. He has arranged everything; as the sovereign, he sends forth the seasons, furthering the vigor of the sacrifice. "Agni in the highest abodes... the Maruts, whose priest and domestic chaplain is Agni"—thus [it is said] in the Āgnimāruta [śastra]. (Soma: Daśarātra: Ninth Day of the Ten-Day Period)
Those which are the morning and third pressings of the first three-day period are combined in the Chandomas.
(10) In the Niṣkevalya and Marutvatīya [stotras], he omits the Jāgata verses.
(11) The fifteen [verses] beginning with "sa yo vṛṣā" follow the "kayā śubhīya" [sūkta]. (12)
One should recite for him [the verse] beginning with *yo jāta*.

(Soma: Daśarātra: Ninth Day of the Ten-Day Period) All [the stotras] have the Bṛhat and Rathantara as their Pṛṣṭha-stotras and consist of two hymns each. (Soma: Daśarātra: Ninth Day of the Ten-Day Period) The tenth day is the Avivākya, having the Caturvimśa Stoma. (Soma: Daśarātra: Tenth Day of the Ten-Day Period)

The Agniṣṭoma-sāman is the Trayastrimśa. (Soma: Daśarātra: Tenth Day of the Ten-Day Period) The Mānasa is the Trika. (Soma: Daśarātra: Tenth Day of the Ten-Day Period) The Rathantara is the Pṛṣṭha-stotra, based on the womb of the Vāmadevya. (Soma: Daśarātra: Tenth Day of the Ten-Day Period)
In case of lack of inspiration, another [priest] should perform the private recitation (svādhyāya).

Having extracted the *ānuṣṭubh* verses from the other meters, one should complete a fifteen-thousand-verse collection in the *ānuṣṭubh* meter for one of the *savanīya* offerings. There are thirty-two *gāyatrī* verses.
ŚŚ 10.12: “*agnim naro dīdhitibhiḥ*, *prati tyam*, and *sūnaryā śubhrāḥ*—these three triplets are to be placed in the position of the *anuṣṭubh*s.
(8) ŚŚ 10.12: There are twenty-four *triṣṭubh*s. (9) ŚŚ 10.12: Likewise, there are [twenty-four] *jagatī*s. (10)
Fifteen *pragāthas*.
Fifteen triplets in the *uṣṇih* meter.
And [triplets] in the *paṅkti* meter.

The morning litany (*prātar-anuvāka*) consists of one hundred and fifteen *anuṣṭubh* verses. (ŚŚS 10.12.14) Having omitted the third and fourth *stokya* verses, two [verses] beginning with "abhi pravanta" are inserted.
(ŚŚS 10.12.15) The three verses beginning with "acchā naḥ śīraśociṣam" take the place of those beginning with "acchā vo agnim avase. (ŚŚS 10.12.16)
*Pratiśrutāya*—these three [verses] take the place of *praty asmai pipīṣate*.
(ŚŚS 10.12) *Agne tam adya* is the Ājya-stotra.
(ŚŚS 10.13) In its first [verse], having divided [the verse] with a five-syllable pause, he pauses after two five-syllable units and pronounces the *praṇava* with the remaining two. (ŚŚS 10.13)
The *prauga* chant belongs to Mādhucchandasa. (3) There are twenty-two *gāyatrī* verses.
(4) "Being cleansed in the fleece, purifying himself through the sheep's wool"—this is the *grāvastut* hymn; it may be recited according to preference. (5)
"Utthānn ojasā"—this single verse takes the place of "Uttishṭhatāva paśyata. (Soma: Daśarātra:
Tenth Day of the Ten-Day Period) The *trikadrukīyā* is the introductory verse for the *marutvatīya* [śastra].

(Soma: Daśarātra: Tenth Day of the Ten-Day Period) Of that [verse], having divided it with sixteen-syllable units, having uttered the *praṇava* with sixteen-syllable units, having paused with sixteen-syllable units, [and] with sixteen-syllable units. (Soma: Daśarātra: Tenth Day of the Ten-Day Period)
"Tuviśuṣma" is the next [verse]. (Soma: Daśarātra:
Tenth Day of the Ten-Day Period) From the hymn "Bṛhad indrāya," he recites the two preceding *pragāthas* and the *pinvanty apīyā*; this constitutes the *marutvatīya* [śastra].

(Soma: Daśarātra: Tenth Day of the Ten-Day Period) Having recited the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses of the Vāmadevya [sāman], he recites the *dhyāyyā*, followed by the *rāthaṃtara* *pragātha* and the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses. (Soma: Daśarātra: Tenth Day of the Ten-Day Period)
"O friends, let us pray for blessings"—this is the ninth [verse]. (Soma: Daśarātra:
Tenth Day of the Ten-Day Period) "And 'Upon the yokes, for him, the thunderbolt, one'—these are the two-footed verses.
(Soma: Daśarātra: Tenth Day of the Ten-Day Period) "And the Hiraṇyastūpīya [hymn]. (Soma: Daśarātra: Tenth Day of the Ten-Day Period)
Before the *Hairaṇyastūpīya*, he recites with a *pragātha*.
Thus ends the *niṣkevalya* [śastra]. From the sixth day, the *pratipad* and *anucara* of the *vaiśvadeva* [śastra] are used.
In the Vaiśvadeva [śastra], there is a modification: "purastāc ca no bhadrīyāt pra śukrīyam" (ŚŚ 10.13).
Having extracted [the verse] with "uru viṣṇo" (ŚŚ 10.13), he performs the offering with "bhavā mitra" (ŚŚ 10.13).
"Agnim nara" (ŚŚ 10.13) serves as the stotriya and anurūpa for the Agniṣṭoma-sāman (ŚŚ 10.13).
"Āyam gauḥ pṛśnir akramīt" and "Mahī dyauḥ" are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses.
(21) "Tam pratnathā" consists of thirteen verses.
(22) Having concluded with "Yajño babhūva," (23) [the *paridhānīyā* is recited]. (Soma: Daśarātra: Tenth day of the Ten-day period)
He sacrifices with the formula, "To Prajāpati, svāhā!
(ŚŚS 10.13.23). The call for the *āhāva* with the *uktha* verses has been explained (ŚŚS 10.13.24).
Thus, in this collection, there is an additional *uktha*. (ŚŚS 10.13.25)

Before the Patnīsaṃyāja offerings, having concluded the ritual and offered oblations in the Gārhapatya fire, he enters the Sadas by the eastern door, sits behind his own Dhiṣṇya hearth, and while the Stotra is being chanted mentally, he recites the Sārparājñī verses beginning with "āyam gauḥ" in a low voice (*upāṃśu*), without uttering the *praṇava*. When addressed by the Adhvaryu with "O Hotṛ!", he responds everywhere with "Ho, Hotṛ! (or "Hauṣaṭ, Hotṛ!").
ŚŚS 10.13: When [the Hotṛ] says, "Oṃ, Hotṛ! Likewise, O Hotṛ!", he (the Adhvaryu) responds with the *anugraṇa* formula.
ŚŚS 10.14: When he is about to recite the Daśahotṛ formula, [he addresses the Adhvaryu] as "Adhvaryo! (with the protracted vowel).

Prajāpati desired: "May I become many; may I procreate; may I pervade this entire universe—whatever exists here, whether gods, humans, or anything else. He beheld this sacrificial rite, the *daśahotṛ*, namely the *agnihotra*.
Having spoken thus, he then [performed it] in a low voice (*upāṃśu*).

Intention is the offering-spoon; thought is the clarified butter; speech is the altar; what has been meditated upon is the sacrificial grass; insight is the fire; what has been discerned is the *agnīdh* priest; the Lord of Speech is the *hotṛ* priest; the mind is the *upavaktṛ*; breath is the oblation; the *sāman* is the *adhvaryu*. These are the *hotṛ*s. (ŚŚS 10.14) Now follows the cup-draught. (ŚŚS 10.14)
O Lord of Speech, O you who ordain the heart, O Name! Vācaspati has drunk the Soma; bestow manly vigor upon us.
(6) Thus [he recites] in a low voice. (7) (Soma: Daśarātra: Tenth day of the Ten-day Period)

By him, Prajāpati generated these three: gods, humans, and asuras. He who, knowing thus, becomes the Hotṛ priest, is indeed propagated with offspring and cattle; and those sacrificers for whom he becomes the Hotṛ priest, knowing thus, are likewise propagated with offspring and cattle. (8) "O Adhvaryu!"—thus one should say when about to recite the Caturhotṛ formula. (1) (Soma: Daśarātra: Tenth Day of the Ten-Day Period)

They were divided into two groups: the gods and the humans. The Asuras turned away from him; he desired, "May a hero be born to me by whom I may overcome these Asuras. He saw this sacrificial rite, the Four-Hotṛ, namely the New and Full Moon sacrifices. Having said this, [he spoke] then in a whisper.

Pṛthivī is the Hotṛ; Dyau is the Adhvaryu; Tvaṣṭṛ is the Agnīdh; Mitra is the Upavaktṛ. These are the Hotṛs. (Soma: Daśarātra: Tenth day of the Ten-day Period) Now follows the cup-drawing. (Soma: Daśarātra: Tenth day of the Ten-day Period)

"O Lord of Speech, with the most perfectly gathered power of speech you draw [the Soma]; you prepare wealth and power for the lord of the sacrifice. Let the Lord of Speech drink the Soma; he has generated Indra for the sake of Indra-power.
Svāhā! (6) Thus [he recites] in a low voice. (7)

By means of that [sacrifice], Prajāpati generated Indra as a hero; through him, he overcame those Asuras. For those for whom one who knows thus serves as the Hotṛ-priest, a hero is indeed born to that Hotṛ; heroes are born to those sacrificers. That Hotṛ indeed overcomes his hateful rival; those sacrificers for whom one who knows thus serves as the Hotṛ overcome their hateful rivals. (Soma: Daśarātra: Tenth Day of the Ten-Day Period)
"O Adhvaryu!"—thus he says when about to recite the *pañcahotṛ* formula. (Soma: Daśarātra:

Tenth Day of the Ten-Day Period) To that Indra, the deities did not submit for the sake of preeminence and supremacy. He beheld this sacrificial rite, the *pañcahotṛ*, namely the *Cāturmāsya* sacrifices. Having said this, he then [recites] in a low voice (*upāṃśu*). (Soma: Daśarātra: Tenth Day of the Ten-Day Period)
Agni is the *hotṛ*; the two Aśvins are the *adhvaryus*; Rudra is the *agnīdh*; Bṛhaspati is the *upavaktṛ*. These are the *hotṛ*s.
Now follows the cup-drawing (*graha*).
"O Lord of Speech, with unimpaired speech, with an unimpaired ladle, do thou, O God, increase the office of the *hotṛ* in heaven."
Thus [it is recited] in a whisper.

Then indeed, the deities stood firm for Indra, for preeminence and for supremacy. For those whose Hotṛ-priest is one who knows thus, they stand firm for that Hotṛ for the sake of supremacy; they stand firm for those sacrificers for the sake of supremacy, for whom the Hotṛ-priest is one who knows thus. Thus [it is recited]. 8. (Soma: Daśarātra: Tenth Day of the Ten-Day Period)
"Adhvaryo!"—thus he says when about to recite the *Ṣaḍḍhotṛ* formula. (Soma: Daśarātra:

Tenth Day of the Ten-Day Period) He desired, "May I be an eater of food, a lord of food. He saw this sacrificial rite, the *Ṣaḍḍhotṛ*, which is a form of animal sacrifice (*paśubandha*). (Soma: Daśarātra:
Tenth Day of the Ten-Day Period) Having said this, he then [recites] in a low voice (*upāṃśu*). (Soma: Daśarātra: Tenth Day of the Ten-Day Period)

"May the sun be your eye; the wind your breath; the intermediate space your self; the sacrifice your limbs; the sky your back; the earth your body. Thus say the Hotṛ priests. (ŚŚS 10.17.4) Now follows the cup-offering (graha).
(ŚŚS 10.17.5) "May Soma drink of Soma; may the bright one drink of the bright one. O Indra, these Soma juices are cooked for you, O Vātāpi, you who hear our invocation! (ŚŚS 10.17.6)

Thus [he says] in a whisper. Then indeed he became an eater of food and a lord of food. For those for whom one who knows thus becomes the *hotṛ*, that *hotṛ* indeed becomes an eater of food and a lord of food; and those sacrificers for whom one who knows thus becomes the *hotṛ* become eaters of food and lords of food. Thus [it is said].
"O Adhvaryu!"—thus he says when about to recite as the Saptahotṛ.
(Soma: Daśarātra: Tenth Day of the Ten-Day Period) Those gods desired: "May we be established in the well-ordered worlds. They beheld this sacrificial rite of the Saptahotṛ, the Soma sacrifice.
Having said this, [he speaks] then in a low voice (*upāṃśu*). (Soma: Daśarātra: Tenth Day of the Ten-Day Period)

Mahāhavir is the Hotṛ; Satyahavis is the Adhvaryu; Acittapāja is the Agnīdh; Acittamanas is the Upavaktṛ; Anādhṛṣya and Apratidhṛṣya are the two Abhigarus; Ayāsya is the Udgātṛ. These are the Hotṛs. Now follows the cup (graha).

O Vācaspati, O Vidhi, we revere your name; may you revere our names. May the thread of the gods not be severed, nor that of men. Invoked together with Heaven and Earth, drink of the Soma, svāhā! (Ṣoma: Daśarātra:
Tenth Day of the Ten-Day Period) Thus [he recites] in a low voice. (Ṣoma: Daśarātra: Tenth Day of the Ten-Day Period)

Then indeed they were established for them; those gods, being established, came to reside in established worlds—even today, they remain established in established worlds. For those whose Hotṛ priest is one who knows thus, the security of possession (*yoga-kṣema*) is indeed established for that Hotṛ; the security of possession is established for those sacrificers. That Hotṛ attains the heavenly world and finds firm support in this world; those sacrificers attain the heavenly world and find firm support in this world.
"Those for whom a Hotṛ who knows thus becomes their priest stand firm in this world.
(ŚŚS 10.18) / Then he speaks the *tanū* [verses]. (ŚŚS 10.19)

"O Adhvaryu, those for whom the Hotṛ is one who knows Prajāpati’s body as 'the eater of food' (annādī), that Hotṛ indeed becomes an eater of food, and those sacrificers become eaters of food. O Adhvaryu, those for whom the Hotṛ is one who knows Prajāpati’s body as 'the mistress of food' (annapatnī), that Hotṛ indeed becomes a lord of food, and those sacrificers become lords of food. (Ṣoma: Daśarātra: Tenth Day of the Ten-Day Period)

O Adhvaryu, for those for whom the Hotṛ, knowing the auspicious body (*tanū*) of Prajāpati, performs the office, it becomes auspicious for that Hotṛ; it becomes auspicious for those sacrificers. (2b) O Adhvaryu, for those for whom the Hotṛ, knowing the beautiful body (*tanū*) of Prajāpati, performs the office, it becomes beautiful for that Hotṛ; it becomes beautiful for those sacrificers. (2c)

"O Adhvaryu, for those whose Hotṛ is one who knows Prajāpati’s ‘homeless’ (anilayā) body, that Hotṛ indeed becomes homeless; those sacrificers become homeless. "O Adhvaryu, for those whose Hotṛ is one who knows Prajāpati’s ‘fearless’ (abhayā) body, there is indeed fearlessness for that Hotṛ, and there is fearlessness for those sacrificers."

"O Adhvaryu, those for whom the Hotṛ is one who knows the unattained body of Prajāpati—he indeed becomes an unattained Hotṛ, and those sacrificers become unattained. O Adhvaryu, those for whom the Hotṛ is one who knows the inviolable body (*tanū*) of Prajāpati—the Hotṛ indeed becomes inviolable, and those sacrificers become inviolable. O Adhvaryu, those for whom the Hotṛ is one who knows the unassailable body (*tanū*) of Prajāpati—the Hotṛ indeed becomes unassailable, and those sacrificers become unassailable.

O Adhvaryu, those for whom the Hotṛ is one who knows the unprecedented body of Prajāpati—indeed, no other Hotṛ becomes prior to that Hotṛ, nor do others become prior to those sacrificers. (Soma: Daśarātra: Tenth Day of the Ten-Day Period)

Listen to this, O people: Narāśaṃsa shall be praised. We have given sixty thousand and ninety thousand [cows] to the Kaurama among the Ruśamas.
(1) He whose twenty camels carry burdens and are yoked with female mules—his chariot’s height sinks down, as if shrinking from the sky, yet reaching out to touch it.
(2) For my sake, he has bestowed a hundred gold neck-ornaments, ten garlands, three hundred swift horses, and ten thousand cattle. (3)

The inspired singers (*rebhas*) move forward with their thoughts like cattle at will. Their sons are not tied up; they sit like cattle that have been released. (4) O singer (*rebha*), bring forth your prayer that finds cattle and finds wealth. Mix this speech for the gods, like an arrow that pierces its mark.
(5) Sing out, O singer, sing out! Like a bird on a ripe tree, your tongue moves to and fro like a razor from the barber’s sheath. (1)
Indra awakened the artisan: "Arise, go forth, O aged one! Praise me, the fierce one; everything here is yours to enjoy.
"May cattle be born here, may horses be born here, may men be born here! Here let Pūṣan, who bestows a thousandfold sacrificial fees, settle down.
"O Indra, let these cows not suffer harm; let their owner not suffer harm. Let no man hostile to them, nor any thief, prevail over them, O Indra."

O Indra, that superhuman deed which you performed at the battle of the ten kings—that was for Virūpa alone; he indeed fell under the power of consumption (yakṣma). O Maghavan, you made Vṛṣākapi bow down even as he was a youth; you released Rauhiṇa from his bonds and shattered the head of Vṛtra.

bound in three ways by the leather strap, he proclaims abundance and drives away scarcity.

O Indra, for the pigeon whose wings were severed as it fled, you prepared much cooked *śyāmāka* grain and *pīlu* fruit as its fodder.

O singer, the Ādityas brought a horse as a sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) to the Aṅgirases. O singer, they did not accept it; yet, O singer, they did accept it. O singer, they did not take hold of it; yet, O singer, they did take hold of it.

Having departed from the day, they have become unconscious; having departed from the sacrifice, they are without a leader. O Ādityas, Rudras, and Vasus, you have indeed come here; O Aṅgiras, accept this gift!
(ŚS 12.19) O gods, may they grant this great and wide gift, whatever is most excellent. May that be in harmony with you; may it be yours day after day. Now, indeed, take hold of it! (ŚS 12.19)
"Moreover, he possesses the swiftness of a white horse; moreover, as the youngest, he surpasses those who go on foot; moreover, he bears the measure of speed.

(1) He whose eyes are unanointed, whose [body] is unanointed, who has no jewels, no gold, and who is not a Brahmin though the son of a Brahmin—he is reckoned as one of the "Kalpas" among the reciters. (2–1)

He whose eyes are anointed, who is well-anointed, who possesses beautiful jewels and fine gold, who is a true Brahmin and the son of a Brahmin—he is a praiser commensurate with the ritual manuals (kalpas). The waterless pond, the pit without a bottom, the woman who does not give, and the maiden who is not to be approached—a beautiful girl such as this is a praiser commensurate with the ritual manuals.
The well-stepping reservoirs, the river Revatī, and he who is a liberal giver; the maiden Suyabhya, the auspicious, praised among the ritual manuals (kalpa).

The discarded queen, the great lady, the one who goes to battle without weapons; the swift horse that does not run, the one who goes to battle without a chariot—these are praised among the ritual manuals.
The favorite queen, the great lady, she who goes to battle with well-being; the swift horse that runs, the one who goes to battle with a chariot—these are praised among the ritual manuals.

When the victim has been brought forward (*upākṛta*) and is trembling, he offers an oblation with: "From whatever you trembled out of fear, from that grant us freedom from fear; protect all our cattle; homage to Rudra the giver! Svāhā! (ŚŚS 13.2).

Prajāpati, desiring to obtain this world, performed austerity and saw this sacrificial rite (*yajñakratu*), namely the *bhūḥ*. Having sacrificed with it, he obtained this world. Desiring to obtain this world, one should sacrifice with it.
